lessons.title: Exercise 1.1 — Percentages, Fractions and Decimals
lessons.notes_html:
Exercise 1.1 of Unit 1 — Percentage, Ratio and Proportion — complete solved exercises with every step shown.

Exercise 1.1 — Question 1: Express the following percentages as fractions in their lowest form

Q. (i) 95% (ii) 65% (iii) 75% (iv) 25% (v) 56% (vi) 48% (vii) 8% (viii) 33 1/2% (ix) 37 1/2% (x) 87 1/2% (xi) 5 1/4% (xii) 42 1/2%

Formula: To change a percentage into a fraction, divide the percentage by 100, i.e. x% = x/100, and then write the fraction in its lowest form.

(i) 95% = 95/100 = 19/20 (dividing by 5)

(ii) 65% = 65/100 = 13/20 (dividing by 5)

(iii) 75% = 75/100 = 3/4 (dividing by 25)

(iv) 25% = 25/100 = 1/4

(v) 56% = 56/100 = 14/25 (dividing by 4)

(vi) 48% = 48/100 = 12/25 (dividing by 4)

(vii) 8% = 8/100 = 2/25 (dividing by 4)

(viii) 33 1/2% = (67/2)/100 = 67/200

(ix) 37 1/2% = (75/2)/100 = 75/200 = 3/8

(x) 87 1/2% = (175/2)/100 = 175/200 = 7/8

(xi) 5 1/4% = (21/4)/100 = 21/400

(xii) 42 1/2% = (85/2)/100 = 85/200 = 17/40

Exercise 1.1 — Question 2: Express the following fractions as percentages, giving your answer correct to 1 decimal place, where necessary

Q. (i) 3/4 (ii) 3/5 (iii) 4/25 (iv) 13/20 (v) 31/25 (vi) 21/40 (vii) 23/60 (viii) 8/3 (ix) 8/5 (x) 7/8 (xi) 5/8 (xii) 3/8

Formula: To change a fraction into a percentage, multiply the fraction by 100 and write the % sign.

(i) 3/4 = (3/4) x 100% = 75%

(ii) 3/5 = (3/5) x 100% = 60%

(iii) 4/25 = (4/25) x 100% = 16%

(iv) 13/20 = (13/20) x 100% = 65%

(v) 31/25 = (31/25) x 100% = 124%

(vi) 21/40 = (21/40) x 100% = 52.5%

(vii) 23/60 = (23/60) x 100% = 38.33% = 38.3% (correct to 1 decimal place)

(viii) 8/3 = (8/3) x 100% = 266.67% = 266.7% (correct to 1 decimal place)

(ix) 8/5 = (8/5) x 100% = 160%

(x) 7/8 = (7/8) x 100% = 87.5%

(xi) 5/8 = (5/8) x 100% = 62.5%

(xii) 3/8 = (3/8) x 100% = 37.5%

Exercise 1.1 — Question 3: Express the following percentages as decimals, giving your answer correct to 3 places of decimal

Q. (i) 47% (ii) 58% (iii) 92% (iv) 8% (v) 12% (vi) 120% (vii) 180% (viii) 145% (ix) 5 1/2% (x) 5 1/3% (xi) 48 2/3% (xii) 58 1/3%

Formula: To change a percentage into a decimal, divide by 100, i.e. x% = x/100.

(i) 47% = 47/100 = 0.470

(ii) 58% = 58/100 = 0.580

(iii) 92% = 92/100 = 0.920

(iv) 8% = 8/100 = 0.080

(v) 12% = 12/100 = 0.120

(vi) 120% = 120/100 = 1.200

(vii) 180% = 180/100 = 1.800

(viii) 145% = 145/100 = 1.450

(ix) 5 1/2% = 5.5/100 = 0.055

(x) 5 1/3% = (16/3)/100 = 16/300 = 0.053 (correct to 3 decimal places)

(xi) 48 2/3% = (146/3)/100 = 146/300 = 0.487 (correct to 3 decimal places)

(xii) 58 1/3% = (175/3)/100 = 175/300 = 0.583 (correct to 3 decimal places)

Exercise 1.1 — Question 4: Express the following decimals as percentages

Q. (i) 0.5 (ii) 0.9 (iii) 1.25 (iv) 1.39 (v) 1.72 (vi) 0.22 (vii) 2.64 (viii) 3.41 (ix) 0.845 (x) 1.78 (xi) 1.58 (xii) 0.065

Formula: To change a decimal into a percentage, multiply by 100 and write the % sign.

(i) 0.5 = 0.5 x 100% = 50%

(ii) 0.9 = 0.9 x 100% = 90%

(iii) 1.25 = 1.25 x 100% = 125%

(iv) 1.39 = 1.39 x 100% = 139%

(v) 1.72 = 1.72 x 100% = 172%

(vi) 0.22 = 0.22 x 100% = 22%

(vii) 2.64 = 2.64 x 100% = 264%

(viii) 3.41 = 3.41 x 100% = 341%

(ix) 0.845 = 0.845 x 100% = 84.5%

(x) 1.78 = 1.78 x 100% = 178%

(xi) 1.58 = 1.58 x 100% = 158%

(xii) 0.065 = 0.065 x 100% = 6.5%

Exercise 1.1 — Question 5: Complete the following table

Q. I. Fraction 3/4, Percentage 75%, Decimal 0.75 (given) II. Fraction 4/5, Decimal 0.80 III. Percentage 40% IV. Decimal 0.62 V. Percentage 44%

Step 1: For II: 4/5 = (4/5) x 100% = 80%, and the given decimal 0.80 confirms it.

Step 2: For III: 40% = 40/100 = 2/5 (fraction), and 40/100 = 0.40 (decimal).

Step 3: For IV: 0.62 = 0.62 x 100% = 62% (percentage), and 0.62 = 62/100 = 31/50 (fraction).

Step 4: For V: 44% = 44/100 = 11/25 (fraction), and 44/100 = 0.44 (decimal).

Completed table: I. 3/4, 75%, 0.75 ; II. 4/5, 80%, 0.80 ; III. 2/5, 40%, 0.40 ; IV. 31/50, 62%, 0.62 ; V. 11/25, 44%, 0.44

mcqs.q: 95% expressed as a fraction in its lowest form is:
mcqs.why: Formula: x% = x/100. Step 1: 95% = 95/100. Step 2: Divide numerator and denominator by 5, so 95/100 = 19/20, which is the lowest form.

mcqs.q: 75% expressed as a fraction in its lowest form is:
mcqs.why: Formula: x% = x/100. Step 1: 75% = 75/100. Step 2: Divide numerator and denominator by 25, so 75/100 = 3/4, which is the lowest form.

mcqs.q: 37 1/2% expressed as a fraction in its lowest form is:
mcqs.why: Formula: x% = x/100. Step 1: 37 1/2% = (75/2)/100 = 75/200. Step 2: Divide by 25, so 75/200 = 3/8, which is the lowest form.

mcqs.q: 3/4 expressed as a percentage is:
mcqs.why: Formula: Fraction to percentage = fraction x 100%. Step 1: (3/4) x 100% = 300/4 %. Step 2: 300/4 = 75, so the answer is 75%.

mcqs.q: 21/40 expressed as a percentage is:
mcqs.why: Formula: Fraction to percentage = fraction x 100%. Step 1: (21/40) x 100% = 2100/40 %. Step 2: 2100/40 = 52.5, so the answer is 52.5%.

mcqs.q: 47% expressed as a decimal, correct to 3 decimal places, is:
mcqs.why: Formula: x% as a decimal = x/100. Step 1: 47% = 47/100. Step 2: 47 divided by 100 = 0.47, written to 3 decimal places as 0.470.

mcqs.q: 48 2/3% expressed as a decimal, correct to 3 decimal places, is:
mcqs.why: Formula: x% as a decimal = x/100. Step 1: 48 2/3% = (146/3)/100 = 146/300. Step 2: 146 divided by 300 = 0.4866..., which rounds to 0.487 to 3 decimal places.

mcqs.q: 0.5 expressed as a percentage is:
mcqs.why: Formula: Decimal to percentage = decimal x 100%. Step 1: 0.5 x 100% = 50%. Step 2: Move the decimal point two places to the right and write the % sign.

mcqs.q: 0.065 expressed as a percentage is:
mcqs.why: Formula: Decimal to percentage = decimal x 100%. Step 1: 0.065 x 100% = 6.5%. Step 2: 0.065 times 100 is 6.5, so the answer is 6.5%.

mcqs.q: 44% expressed as a fraction in its lowest form is:
mcqs.why: Formula: x% = x/100. Step 1: 44% = 44/100. Step 2: Divide numerator and denominator by 4, so 44/100 = 11/25, which is the lowest form.

lessons.title: Exercise 1.2 — Percentage Problems
lessons.notes_html:
Exercise 1.2 of Unit 1 — Percentage, Ratio and Proportion — complete solved exercises with every step shown.

Exercise 1.2 — Question 1

Q. If 45% of the students in a school are girls. What is the percentage of the boys?

Step 1: Total students = 100%

Step 2: Percentage of boys = 100% - 45%

Step 3: = 55%

So the percentage of the boys is 55%.

Exercise 1.2 — Question 2

Q. If 82% of the houses have a television, what is the percentage of the houses which do not have?

Step 1: Total houses = 100%

Step 2: Houses without a television = 100% - 82%

Step 3: = 18%

So 18% of the houses do not have a television.

Exercise 1.2 — Question 3

Q. A hockey team won 62% of their matches and 26% of them were ended in a draw. What is the percentage of the matches they lost?

Step 1: Won + drawn matches = 62% + 26% = 88%

Step 2: Lost matches = 100% - 88%

Step 3: = 12%

So the team lost 12% of the matches.

Exercise 1.2 — Question 4

Q. An aeroplane carries 400 passengers, 52% of the passengers were Pakistani, 17% were Chinese, 12% were from Iran and the rest were British. (i) How many people of each nationality were on the plane? (ii) What is the percentage of the British?

Step 1: Pakistani passengers = 52% of 400 = (52/100) x 400 = 208

Step 2: Chinese passengers = 17% of 400 = (17/100) x 400 = 68

Step 3: Iranian passengers = 12% of 400 = (12/100) x 400 = 48

Step 4: British passengers = 400 - (208 + 68 + 48) = 400 - 324 = 76

Step 5: (ii) British percentage = (76/400) x 100% = 19%

So (i) Pakistani 208, Chinese 68, Iranian 48, British 76 ; (ii) the British are 19%.

Exercise 1.2 — Question 5

Q. Amna scored 46 out of 50 in a Maths test, 64 out of 75 in a Chemistry test and 72 out of 80 in a Physics test. In which subject did she perform best?

Formula: Percentage of marks = (marks obtained / total marks) x 100

Step 1: Maths: (46/50) x 100 = 92%

Step 2: Chemistry: (64/75) x 100 = 85.33%

Step 3: Physics: (72/80) x 100 = 90%

Step 4: Comparison: 92% > 90% > 85.33%

So Amna performed best in Maths.

Exercise 1.2 — Question 6

Q. A table costs a carpenter Rs. 720 to make. He sells it for Rs. 920. What is the percentage of profit he earned?

Formula: Profit percentage = (profit / cost price) x 100

Step 1: Profit = 920 - 720 = Rs. 200

Step 2: Profit percentage = (200/720) x 100

Step 3: = 27.78%

So he earned a profit of 27.78%.

Exercise 1.2 — Question 7

Q. If 84% of a book consists of 420 pages. Find total number of pages in the book.

Step 1: Let the total number of pages = x

Step 2: 84% of x = 420, i.e. (84/100) x x = 420

Step 3: x = 420 x (100/84)

Step 4: x = 500

So the book has 500 pages in total.

Exercise 1.2 — Question 8

Q. Out of his total income Hamza spends 20% on house rent and 70% of the rest on household expenditure. If he saves Rs. 1800, what is his total income?

Step 1: Let the total income = Rs. 100 (for the percentage calculation)

Step 2: Rent = 20% of 100 = Rs. 20, remainder = 100 - 20 = Rs. 80

Step 3: Household expenditure = 70% of 80 = (70/100) x 80 = Rs. 56

Step 4: Saving = 80 - 56 = Rs. 24, i.e. 24% of the total income

Step 5: 24% = Rs. 1800, so total income = 1800 x (100/24) = Rs. 7500

So Hamza's total income is Rs. 7500.

Exercise 1.2 — Question 9

Q. Raheel's income is 25% more than that of Rauf. What percent is Rauf's income less than Raheel's?

Step 1: Let Rauf's income = Rs. 100

Step 2: Raheel's income = 100 + 25% of 100 = 100 + 25 = Rs. 125

Step 3: Difference = 125 - 100 = Rs. 25

Step 4: Formula: Percentage less = (difference / Raheel's income) x 100 = (25/125) x 100

Step 5: = 20%

So Rauf's income is 20% less than Raheel's.

mcqs.q: If 45% of the students in a school are girls, the percentage of boys is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Total students = 100%. Step 2: Percentage of boys = 100% - 45%. Step 3: 100 - 45 = 55, so the percentage of boys is 55%.

mcqs.q: If 82% of the houses have a television, the percentage of houses which do not have a television is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Total houses = 100%. Step 2: Houses without a television = 100% - 82%. Step 3: 100 - 82 = 18, so 18% of the houses do not have a television.

mcqs.q: A hockey team won 62% of their matches and 26% were drawn. The percentage of matches they lost is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Won plus drawn = 62% + 26% = 88%. Step 2: Lost = 100% - 88%. Step 3: 100 - 88 = 12, so the team lost 12% of the matches.

mcqs.q: An aeroplane carries 400 passengers. If 52% are Pakistani, the number of Pakistani passengers is:
mcqs.why: Formula: Number = percentage x total / 100. Step 1: 52% of 400 = (52/100) x 400. Step 2: 52 x 4 = 208, so there are 208 Pakistani passengers.

mcqs.q: An aeroplane carries 400 passengers: 52% Pakistani, 17% Chinese and 12% Iranian. The percentage of British passengers is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Pakistani plus Chinese plus Iranian = 52 + 17 + 12 = 81%. Step 2: British = 100% - 81% = 19%. Check: 76 British out of 400 is (76/400) x 100% = 19%.

mcqs.q: Amna scored 46 out of 50 in Maths. Her percentage in Maths is:
mcqs.why: Formula: Percentage of marks = (marks obtained / total marks) x 100. Step 1: (46/50) x 100. Step 2: 46/50 = 0.92, and 0.92 x 100 = 92, so her Maths percentage is 92%.

mcqs.q: A table costs Rs. 720 to make and is sold for Rs. 920. The percentage of profit is:
mcqs.why: Formula: Profit percentage = (profit / cost price) x 100. Step 1: Profit = 920 - 720 = Rs. 200. Step 2: (200/720) x 100 = 27.777...%, so the profit is 27.78%.

mcqs.q: If 84% of a book consists of 420 pages, the total number of pages in the book is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Let total pages = x, so 84% of x = 420, that is (84/100) x x = 420. Step 2: x = 420 x (100/84) = 42000/84. Step 3: 42000/84 = 500 pages.

mcqs.q: Hamza spends 20% of his income on rent and 70% of the rest on household expenditure. He saves Rs. 1800. His total income is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: On Rs. 100, rent = 20, remainder = 80. Step 2: Household = 70% of 80 = 56, saving = 80 - 56 = 24, that is 24%. Step 3: Total income = 1800 x (100/24) = Rs. 7500.

mcqs.q: Raheel's income is 25% more than Rauf's income. Rauf's income is less than Raheel's by:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Let Rauf = Rs. 100, so Raheel = 100 + 25 = Rs. 125. Step 2: Difference = 25. Formula: Percentage less = (difference / Raheel's income) x 100 = (25/125) x 100 = 20%.

lessons.title: Exercise 1.3 — Ratio and Its Simplest Form
lessons.notes_html:
Exercise 1.3 of Unit 1 — Percentage, Ratio and Proportion — complete solved exercises with every step shown.

Exercise 1.3 — Question 1: Find the ratio of first quantity to the second in its lowest form

Q. (i) Rs. 24, Rs. 6 (ii) 20 kg, 5 kg (iii) 20 cm, 80 cm (iv) 5 m, 5 m (v) 1500 km, 1200 km (vi) Rs. 150, Rs. 275

Formula: To write a ratio a : b in its lowest form, divide both terms by their HCF. A ratio has no unit.

(i) 24 : 6 = 4 : 1 (dividing by 6)

(ii) 20 : 5 = 4 : 1 (dividing by 5)

(iii) 20 : 80 = 1 : 4 (dividing by 20)

(iv) 5 : 5 = 1 : 1 (dividing by 5)

(v) 1500 : 1200 = 5 : 4 (dividing by 300)

(vi) 150 : 275 = 6 : 11 (dividing by 25)

Exercise 1.3 — Question 2: Express each of the following ratios in its simplest form

Q. (i) 2/3 : 3/5 (ii) 4/5 : 3/4 (iii) 5/6 : 7/10 (iv) 13/40 : 3/20 (v) 2/3 : 1/6 (vi) 4/10 : 20 (vii) 15/10 : 2 (viii) 12/10 : 28/10 (ix) 2/5 : 1/3

Method: To simplify a ratio of fractions, multiply both terms by the LCM of the denominators.

(i) 2/3 : 3/5 — multiply by 15: 10 : 9

(ii) 4/5 : 3/4 — multiply by 20: 16 : 15

(iii) 5/6 : 7/10 — multiply by 30: 25 : 21

(iv) 13/40 : 3/20 — multiply by 40: 13 : 6

(v) 2/3 : 1/6 — multiply by 6: 4 : 1

(vi) 4/10 : 20 — multiply by 10: 4 : 200 = 1 : 50

(vii) 15/10 : 2 — multiply by 10: 15 : 20 = 3 : 4

(viii) 12/10 : 28/10 — multiply by 10: 12 : 28 = 3 : 7

(ix) 2/5 : 1/3 — multiply by 15: 6 : 5

Exercise 1.3 — Question 3

Q. In a city 126 medical students traveled by: Rikshaw 14, Taxi 9, Bus 75, Car 28. Find ratio of the students who used: (i) Rikshaw to taxi (ii) Taxi to bus (iii) Taxi to car.

Step 1: (i) Rikshaw : Taxi = 14 : 9 (cannot be simplified further)

Step 2: (ii) Taxi : Bus = 9 : 75 = 3 : 25 (dividing by 3)

Step 3: (iii) Taxi : Car = 9 : 28 (cannot be simplified further)

So the ratios are 14 : 9, 3 : 25 and 9 : 28 respectively.

Exercise 1.3 — Question 4

Q. In a school library, there are 75 books on Mathematics, 115 on English, 85 on Chemistry and 60 on Physics. Find ratio of the following: (i) Mathematics books to English books (ii) English books to Chemistry books (iii) English books to Physics books (iv) Physics books to Chemistry books (v) Physics books to Mathematics books (vi) Chemistry books to Mathematics books.

(i) 75 : 115 = 15 : 23 (dividing by 5)

(ii) 115 : 85 = 23 : 17 (dividing by 5)

(iii) 115 : 60 = 23 : 12 (dividing by 5)

(iv) 60 : 85 = 12 : 17 (dividing by 5)

(v) 60 : 75 = 4 : 5 (dividing by 15)

(vi) 85 : 75 = 17 : 15 (dividing by 5)

mcqs.q: The ratio of Rs. 24 to Rs. 6 in its lowest form is:
mcqs.why: Formula: Divide both terms of a ratio by their HCF to get the lowest form. Step 1: 24 : 6. Step 2: Divide by 6, so 24/6 : 6/6 = 4 : 1. A ratio has no unit.

mcqs.q: The ratio of 20 cm to 80 cm in its lowest form is:
mcqs.why: Formula: Divide both terms by their HCF. Step 1: 20 : 80. Step 2: Divide by 20, so 20/20 : 80/20 = 1 : 4, which is the lowest form.

mcqs.q: The ratio of 1500 km to 1200 km in its lowest form is:
mcqs.why: Formula: Divide both terms by their HCF. Step 1: 1500 : 1200. Step 2: Divide by 300, so 1500/300 : 1200/300 = 5 : 4, which is the lowest form.

mcqs.q: The ratio of Rs. 150 to Rs. 275 in its lowest form is:
mcqs.why: Formula: Divide both terms by their HCF. Step 1: 150 : 275. Step 2: Divide by 25, so 150/25 : 275/25 = 6 : 11, which is the lowest form.

mcqs.q: The ratio 2/3 : 3/5 in its simplest form is:
mcqs.why: Method: Multiply both terms by the LCM of the denominators. Step 1: LCM of 3 and 5 is 15. Step 2: (2/3) x 15 = 10 and (3/5) x 15 = 9, so the ratio is 10 : 9.

mcqs.q: The ratio 4/5 : 3/4 in its simplest form is:
mcqs.why: Method: Multiply both terms by the LCM of the denominators. Step 1: LCM of 5 and 4 is 20. Step 2: (4/5) x 20 = 16 and (3/4) x 20 = 15, so the ratio is 16 : 15.

mcqs.q: The ratio 2/3 : 1/6 in its simplest form is:
mcqs.why: Method: Multiply both terms by the LCM of the denominators. Step 1: LCM of 3 and 6 is 6. Step 2: (2/3) x 6 = 4 and (1/6) x 6 = 1, so the ratio is 4 : 1.

mcqs.q: 126 students travelled by rikshaw 14, taxi 9, bus 75 and car 28. The ratio of taxi users to bus users is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Taxi : Bus = 9 : 75. Step 2: Divide both terms by 3, so 9/3 : 75/3 = 3 : 25, which is the ratio in its lowest form.

mcqs.q: In a library there are 75 Mathematics books and 115 English books. The ratio of Mathematics books to English books is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Mathematics : English = 75 : 115. Step 2: Divide both terms by 5, so 75/5 : 115/5 = 15 : 23, which is the lowest form.

mcqs.q: In a library there are 60 Physics books and 75 Mathematics books. The ratio of Physics books to Mathematics books is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Physics : Mathematics = 60 : 75. Step 2: Divide both terms by 15, so 60/15 : 75/15 = 4 : 5, which is the lowest form.

lessons.title: Exercise 1.4 — Ratio of Quantities with Units
lessons.notes_html:
Exercise 1.4 of Unit 1 — Percentage, Ratio and Proportion — complete solved exercises with every step shown.

Exercise 1.4 — Question 1

Q. Find the ratio of 6 rupees each to 72 rupees per dozen.

Step 1: Rs. 72 per dozen means 12 articles cost Rs. 72, so the price of each = 72/12 = Rs. 6

Step 2: Ratio = 6 : 6

Step 3: = 1 : 1 (dividing by 6)

So the required ratio is 1 : 1.

Exercise 1.4 — Question 2

Q. Find the ratio of Rs. 160 per meter to Rs. 150 per meter.

Step 1: Ratio = 160 : 150

Step 2: = 16 : 15 (dividing by 10)

So the required ratio is 16 : 15.

Exercise 1.4 — Question 3

Q. Find the ratio of Rs. 72 for 24 to rupees 4 each.

Step 1: 24 articles cost Rs. 72, so the price of each = 72/24 = Rs. 3

Step 2: Ratio = 3 : 4

So the required ratio is 3 : 4.

Exercise 1.4 — Question 4

Q. A square 'A' has side 2 cm and a square 'B' has side 6 cm. Find the ratio of: (i) The length of the side of the square A to the length of the side of the square B (ii) The perimeter of the square A to the perimeter of the square B (iii) The area of the square 'A' to the area of the square 'B'.

Formulas: Perimeter of a square = 4 x side ; Area of a square = side x side

Step 1: (i) Ratio of the sides = 2 : 6 = 1 : 3

Step 2: Perimeter of A = 4 x 2 = 8 cm ; Perimeter of B = 4 x 6 = 24 cm ; (ii) Ratio of the perimeters = 8 : 24 = 1 : 3

Step 3: Area of A = 2 x 2 = 4 cm^2 ; Area of B = 6 x 6 = 36 cm^2 ; (iii) Ratio of the areas = 4 : 36 = 1 : 9

So the ratios are 1 : 3, 1 : 3 and 1 : 9 respectively.

Exercise 1.4 — Question 5

Q. If a : b = 2 : 3, find the ratio 6a : 2b.

Step 1: a : b = 2 : 3, so take a = 2 and b = 3

Step 2: 6a : 2b = (6 x 2) : (2 x 3) = 12 : 6

Step 3: = 2 : 1 (dividing by 6)

So 6a : 2b = 2 : 1.

Exercise 1.4 — Question 6

Q. A triangle has sides of lengths 3 cm, 4 cm and 6 cm. Find the ratio of the lengths of the sides to one another.

Step 1: Ratio of the three sides together = 3 : 4 : 6

Step 2: 3, 4 and 6 have no common factor other than 1, so this is the simplest form.

Step 3: The ratios of the sides to one another in pairs (as listed in the book's answer key) are: first to second = 3 : 4 ; second to third = 4 : 6 = 2 : 3 ; first to third = 3 : 6 = 1 : 2.

So the ratio of the sides is 3 : 4 : 6 (pairwise: 3 : 4, 2 : 3 and 1 : 2).

Exercise 1.4 — Question 7

Q. Two angles in a triangle are 54 degrees and 72 degrees. Find the ratio of the third angle to the sum of the first two.

Formula: The sum of the three angles of a triangle = 180 degrees

Step 1: Third angle = 180 - 54 - 72 = 54 degrees

Step 2: Sum of the first two angles = 54 + 72 = 126 degrees

Step 3: Ratio = 54 : 126 = 3 : 7 (dividing by 18)

So the required ratio is 3 : 7.

Exercise 1.4 — Question 8

Q. Ali's father earns a salary of Rs. 40,000 in a month, while his father's monthly expenditures are Rs. 35,000. Find the ratio of his father's: (i) Income to expenditure (ii) Expenditure to savings (iii) Income to savings

Step 1: Savings = Income - Expenditure = 40,000 - 35,000 = Rs. 5,000

Step 2: (i) Income : Expenditure = 40,000 : 35,000 = 8 : 7 (dividing by 5,000)

Step 3: (ii) Expenditure : Savings = 35,000 : 5,000 = 7 : 1

Step 4: (iii) Income : Savings = 40,000 : 5,000 = 8 : 1

So the ratios are 8 : 7, 7 : 1 and 8 : 1 respectively.

Exercise 1.4 — Question 9

Q. A square A has side 6 cm and square B has side 8 cm. Find the ratio of: (i) The length of the side of a square A to the length of the side of the square B (ii) The area of square A to the area of square B.

Formula: Area of a square = side x side

Step 1: (i) Ratio of the sides = 6 : 8 = 3 : 4 (dividing by 2)

Step 2: Area of A = 6 x 6 = 36 cm^2 ; Area of B = 8 x 8 = 64 cm^2

Step 3: (ii) Ratio of the areas = 36 : 64 = 9 : 16 (dividing by 4)

So the ratios are 3 : 4 and 9 : 16 respectively.

Exercise 1.4 — Question 10

Q. A family has 12 pets of which 6 are cats, 2 are dogs and the rest are birds. Find the ratio of the number of: (i) birds to dogs (ii) birds to pets

Step 1: Birds = 12 - 6 - 2 = 4

Step 2: (i) Birds : Dogs = 4 : 2 = 2 : 1

Step 3: (ii) Birds : Total pets = 4 : 12 = 1 : 3

So the ratios are 2 : 1 and 1 : 3 respectively.

mcqs.q: The ratio of 6 rupees each to 72 rupees per dozen is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Rs. 72 per dozen means 12 articles cost Rs. 72, so price of each = 72/12 = Rs. 6. Step 2: Ratio = 6 : 6. Step 3: Divide by 6, giving 1 : 1.

mcqs.q: The ratio of Rs. 160 per metre to Rs. 150 per metre is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Ratio = 160 : 150. Step 2: Divide both terms by 10, so 160/10 : 150/10 = 16 : 15, which is the lowest form of the ratio.

mcqs.q: The ratio of Rs. 72 for 24 articles to rupees 4 each is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: 24 articles cost Rs. 72, so price of each = 72/24 = Rs. 3. Step 2: Ratio = 3 : 4. This is already in its lowest form, so the answer is 3 : 4.

mcqs.q: Square A has side 2 cm and square B has side 6 cm. The ratio of the side of A to the side of B is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Ratio of the sides = 2 : 6. Step 2: Divide both terms by 2, so 2/2 : 6/2 = 1 : 3, which is the ratio of the sides in lowest form.

mcqs.q: Square A has side 2 cm and square B has side 6 cm. The ratio of the area of A to the area of B is:
mcqs.why: Formula: Area of a square = side x side. Step 1: Area of A = 2 x 2 = 4, area of B = 6 x 6 = 36. Step 2: Ratio = 4 : 36, divide by 4 to get 1 : 9.

mcqs.q: If a : b = 2 : 3, the ratio 6a : 2b is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Take a = 2 and b = 3. Step 2: 6a : 2b = (6 x 2) : (2 x 3) = 12 : 6. Step 3: Divide by 6, so 12 : 6 = 2 : 1.

mcqs.q: A triangle has sides 3 cm, 4 cm and 6 cm. The combined ratio of the lengths of the sides is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Write the three side lengths together as 3 : 4 : 6. Step 2: 3, 4 and 6 have no common factor other than 1, so 3 : 4 : 6 is already the simplest combined ratio.

mcqs.q: Two angles of a triangle are 54 degrees and 72 degrees. The ratio of the third angle to the sum of the first two is:
mcqs.why: Formula: Sum of the angles of a triangle = 180 degrees. Step 1: Third angle = 180 - 54 - 72 = 54 degrees. Step 2: Sum of first two = 126. Step 3: Ratio = 54 : 126, divide by 18 to get 3 : 7.

mcqs.q: A father earns Rs. 40,000 and spends Rs. 35,000 in a month. The ratio of his income to his savings is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Savings = Income - Expenditure = 40,000 - 35,000 = Rs. 5,000. Step 2: Income : Savings = 40,000 : 5,000. Step 3: Divide by 5,000, giving 8 : 1.

mcqs.q: Square A has side 6 cm and square B has side 8 cm. The ratio of the area of A to the area of B is:
mcqs.why: Formula: Area of a square = side x side. Step 1: Area of A = 6 x 6 = 36, area of B = 8 x 8 = 64. Step 2: Ratio = 36 : 64, divide by 4 to get 9 : 16.

lessons.title: Exercise 1.5 — Proportion
lessons.notes_html:
Exercise 1.5 of Unit 1 — Percentage, Ratio and Proportion — complete solved exercises with every step shown.

Exercise 1.5 — Question 1

Q. Find the value of x in the proportion 20 : 50 :: 8 : x ?

Formula: In a proportion, product of extremes = product of means (ad = bc)

Step 1: In 20 : 50 :: 8 : x the extremes are 20 and x, and the means are 50 and 8

Step 2: 20 x x = 50 x 8

Step 3: 20x = 400

Step 4: x = 400/20 = 20

So x = 20.

Exercise 1.5 — Question 2

Q. The price of 15 suits is Rs. 6750. How many such suits can be purchased by an amount of Rs. 4050?

This is direct proportion (more money, more suits).

Step 1: Let the number of suits = x ; Proportion: 15 : x :: 6750 : 4050

Step 2: 6750 x x = 15 x 4050 (product of extremes = product of means)

Step 3: x = (15 x 4050)/6750 = 9

So 9 suits can be purchased for Rs. 4050.

Exercise 1.5 — Question 3

Q. A motorcycle covers 90 km in 2 liters of petrol. In how many liters of petrol will it cover 225 km?

This is direct proportion.

Step 1: Let the required petrol = x liters ; Proportion: 90 : 225 :: 2 : x

Step 2: 90 x x = 225 x 2

Step 3: x = 450/90 = 5

So 5 liters of petrol are required for 225 km.

Exercise 1.5 — Question 4

Q. A certain journey by train takes 5 hours at the speed of 45 km/h. What will be the speed of the train to complete the same journey in 3 hours?

This is inverse proportion (less time, more speed; the distance is the same).

Step 1: Distance = Speed x Time = 45 x 5 = 225 km

Step 2: New speed = Distance / Time = 225/3

Step 3: = 75 km/h

So the speed of the train will be 75 km/h.

Exercise 1.5 — Question 5

Q. Six men can paint a house in four days. How long it would take to paint the house if three men are employed?

This is inverse proportion (fewer men, more days).

Step 1: Let the required days = x ; Inverse proportion: 6 : 3 :: x : 4

Step 2: 3 x x = 6 x 4

Step 3: x = 24/3 = 8

So three men will take 8 days.

Exercise 1.5 — Question 6

Q. A manager plans to produce 100 bicycles with the help of 25 persons working 4 hours daily. How many bicycles can be made by 40 persons if they work 3 hours daily?

This is compound proportion: direct with the persons and also direct with the hours.

Formula: x = 100 x (40/25) x (3/4)

Step 1: Ratio of persons = 40/25 (direct)

Step 2: Ratio of hours = 3/4 (direct)

Step 3: x = 100 x (40/25) x (3/4) = 100 x (8/5) x (3/4) = 120

So 120 bicycles will be made.

Exercise 1.5 — Question 7

Q. A factory makes 560 fans in 7 days with the help of 20 machines. How many fans can be made in 12 days with the help of 18 machines?

Compound proportion: direct with the days and direct with the machines.

Formula: x = 560 x (12/7) x (18/20)

Step 1: x = 560 x 12 x 18 / (7 x 20)

Step 2: x = 120,960/140 = 864

So 864 fans will be made.

Exercise 1.5 — Question 8

Q. A factory makes 600 soaps in 9 days with the help of 20 machines. How many soaps can be made in 12 days with the help of 18 machines?

Compound proportion: direct with the days and direct with the machines.

Formula: x = 600 x (12/9) x (18/20)

Step 1: x = 600 x 12 x 18 / (9 x 20)

Step 2: x = 129,600/180 = 720

So 720 soaps will be made.

Exercise 1.5 — Question 9

Q. If the stay of 12 men for 28 days in a hotel costs Rs. 6720. Find the cost for the stay of 8 men for 14 days in the hotel.

Compound proportion: the cost is in direct proportion to both the men and the days.

Formula: x = 6720 x (8/12) x (14/28)

Step 1: x = 6720 x (2/3) x (1/2)

Step 2: x = 6720/3 = 2240

So the cost for the stay of 8 men for 14 days will be Rs. 2240.

Exercise 1.5 — Question 10

Q. If the stay of 14 men for 8 days in a hotel costs Rs. 22,400. Find the cost for the stay of 7 men for 13 days.

Compound proportion: the cost is in direct proportion to both the men and the days.

Formula: x = 22,400 x (7/14) x (13/8)

Step 1: x = 22,400 x (1/2) x (13/8) = 11,200 x 13/8

Step 2: x = 145,600/8 = 18,200

So the cost for the stay of 7 men for 13 days will be Rs. 18,200.

Exercise 1.5 — Question 11

Q. 14 cows consume 63 kg of hay in 18 days. How many cows will eat 770 kg of hay in 28 days at same rate?

Step 1: Hay per cow per day = 63/(14 x 18) = 63/252 = 0.25 kg

Step 2: Let the number of cows = x ; by compound proportion x = 14 x (770/63) x (18/28)

Step 3: x = (770 x 14 x 18)/(63 x 28) = 194,040/1764 = 110

So 110 cows will eat 770 kg of hay in 28 days.

Exercise 1.5 — Question 12

Q. Juice manufacturer produces 3000 bottles in a day employing 15 workers working 8 hours. Find the number of bottles manufactured when he employs 18 workers working 6 hours.

Compound proportion: direct with the workers and direct with the hours.

Formula: x = 3000 x (18/15) x (6/8)

Step 1: x = 3000 x (6/5) x (3/4)

Step 2: x = 3000 x 18/20 = 2700

So 2700 bottles will be manufactured.

mcqs.q: In the proportion 20 : 50 :: 8 : x, the value of x is:
mcqs.why: Formula: In a proportion, product of extremes = product of means. Step 1: Extremes are 20 and x, means are 50 and 8, so 20 x x = 50 x 8 = 400. Step 2: x = 400/20 = 20.

mcqs.q: The price of 15 suits is Rs. 6750. The number of suits that can be purchased for Rs. 4050 is:
mcqs.why: This is direct proportion. Step 1: 15 : x :: 6750 : 4050. Step 2: 6750 x x = 15 x 4050, using product of extremes = product of means. Step 3: x = (15 x 4050)/6750 = 9 suits.

mcqs.q: A motorcycle covers 90 km in 2 litres of petrol. The petrol needed to cover 225 km is:
mcqs.why: This is direct proportion. Step 1: 90 : 225 :: 2 : x. Step 2: 90 x x = 225 x 2 = 450, using product of extremes = product of means. Step 3: x = 450/90 = 5 litres.

mcqs.q: A train covers a journey in 5 hours at 45 km/h. The speed needed to complete the same journey in 3 hours is:
mcqs.why: This is inverse proportion. Formula: Distance = Speed x Time. Step 1: Distance = 45 x 5 = 225 km. Step 2: New speed = Distance / Time = 225/3 = 75 km/h.

mcqs.q: Six men can paint a house in 4 days. The time taken by three men to paint the same house is:
mcqs.why: This is inverse proportion, fewer men take more days. Step 1: 6 : 3 :: x : 4. Step 2: 3 x x = 6 x 4 = 24. Step 3: x = 24/3 = 8 days.

mcqs.q: 25 persons working 4 hours daily make 100 bicycles. The bicycles made by 40 persons working 3 hours daily are:
mcqs.why: This is compound proportion, direct with persons and direct with hours. Formula: x = 100 x (40/25) x (3/4). Step 1: 100 x (8/5) x (3/4) = 100 x 24/20. Step 2: x = 120 bicycles.

mcqs.q: A factory makes 560 fans in 7 days with 20 machines. The fans made in 12 days with 18 machines are:
mcqs.why: Compound proportion, direct with days and direct with machines. Formula: x = 560 x (12/7) x (18/20). Step 1: x = (560 x 12 x 18)/(7 x 20) = 120960/140. Step 2: x = 864 fans.

mcqs.q: A factory makes 600 soaps in 9 days with 20 machines. The soaps made in 12 days with 18 machines are:
mcqs.why: Compound proportion, direct with days and direct with machines. Formula: x = 600 x (12/9) x (18/20). Step 1: x = (600 x 12 x 18)/(9 x 20) = 129600/180. Step 2: x = 720 soaps.

mcqs.q: The stay of 12 men for 28 days in a hotel costs Rs. 6720. The cost for 8 men for 14 days is:
mcqs.why: Compound proportion, cost is direct with men and with days. Formula: x = 6720 x (8/12) x (14/28). Step 1: x = 6720 x (2/3) x (1/2) = 6720/3. Step 2: x = Rs. 2240.

mcqs.q: The stay of 14 men for 8 days costs Rs. 22,400. The cost for 7 men for 13 days is:
mcqs.why: Compound proportion, cost is direct with men and with days. Formula: x = 22400 x (7/14) x (13/8). Step 1: x = 22400 x (1/2) x (13/8) = 11200 x 13/8. Step 2: x = 145600/8 = Rs. 18,200.

Review Exercise 1 — Question 3

Q. A railway train carries 800 passengers, 55% passengers are men, 15% are children. What is the percentage of women?

Step 1: Men + children = 55% + 15% = 70%

Step 2: Women = 100% - 70%

Step 3: = 30%

So the percentage of women is 30%.

Review Exercise 1 — Question 4

Q. Azeem spends 25% of his income on house rent, 60% of the remaining on household expenditures. If he saves Rs. 2100, what is his total income?

Step 1: Let the total income = Rs. 100

Step 2: Rent = 25, remainder = 75

Step 3: Household expenditure = 60% of 75 = 45

Step 4: Saving = 75 - 45 = 30, i.e. 30% of the total income

Step 5: 30% = Rs. 2100, so total income = 2100 x (100/30) = Rs. 7000

So Azeem's total income is Rs. 7000.

Review Exercise 1 — Question 5

Q. In a school there are 220 student chairs, 110 student tables, 50 staff chairs and 30 staff tables. Find the ratio of the following: (i) Students chairs to students tables (ii) Students chairs to staff chairs (iii) Students tables to staff tables.

(i) 220 : 110 = 2 : 1 (dividing by 110)

(ii) 220 : 50 = 22 : 5 (dividing by 10)

(iii) 110 : 30 = 11 : 3 (dividing by 10)

Review Exercise 1 — Question 6

Q. Two angles in a triangle are 48 degrees and 60 degrees. Find the ratio of the third angle to the sum of the first two angles.

Formula: The sum of the angles of a triangle = 180 degrees

Step 1: Third angle = 180 - 48 - 60 = 72 degrees

Step 2: Sum of the first two = 48 + 60 = 108 degrees

Step 3: Ratio = 72 : 108 = 2 : 3 (dividing by 36)

So the required ratio is 2 : 3.

Review Exercise 1 — Question 7

Q. 8 persons can do a job in 24 days, if 4 more persons joined them, how much time they will take to complete the same job?

This is inverse proportion.

Step 1: Total persons = 8 + 4 = 12

Step 2: Inverse proportion: 8 x 24 = 12 x x

Step 3: x = 192/12 = 16

So the job will be completed in 16 days.

Review Exercise 1 — Question 8

Q. The stay of 18 students for 36 days in a hostel costs Rs. 58320. Find the cost for the stay of 9 students for 12 days.

Compound proportion: the cost is in direct proportion to both the students and the days.

Formula: x = 58,320 x (9/18) x (12/36)

Step 1: x = 58,320 x (1/2) x (1/3) = 58,320/6

Step 2: x = 9720

So the cost for the stay of 9 students for 12 days will be Rs. 9720.

mcqs.why: Formula: Percentage of a quantity = (percentage/100) x quantity. Step 1: 20% of 600 = (20/100) x 600. Step 2: 20 x 6 = 120, so 20% of 600 is 120.

mcqs.q: The fraction form of 70% is:
mcqs.why: Formula: x% = x/100. Step 1: 70% = 70/100. Step 2: Divide numerator and denominator by 10, so 70/100 = 7/10, which is the fraction form.

mcqs.q: 7/20 in terms of percentage is:
mcqs.why: Formula: Fraction to percentage = fraction x 100%. Step 1: (7/20) x 100% = 700/20 %. Step 2: 700/20 = 35, so the answer is 35%.

mcqs.q: 0.13 as a percentage is:
mcqs.why: Formula: Decimal to percentage = decimal x 100%. Step 1: 0.13 x 100% = 13%. Step 2: Move the decimal point two places to the right and write the % sign.

mcqs.q: In a ratio a : b, a is called the:
mcqs.why: In a ratio a : b, the first term a is called the antecedent and the second term b is called the consequent. So a is the antecedent by definition.

mcqs.q: In a ratio a : b, b is called the:
mcqs.why: In a ratio a : b, the second term b is called the consequent. Note: the book key prints mean for this item, which is wrong; the correct term for b is consequent.

mcqs.q: In a proportion a : b :: c : d, a and d are called the:
mcqs.why: In a proportion a : b :: c : d, the first and last terms a and d are the extremes, while the middle terms b and c are the means. So a and d are extremes.

mcqs.q: The lowest form of 75 : 95 is:
mcqs.why: Formula: Divide both terms by their HCF. Step 1: 75 : 95. Step 2: Divide by 5, so 75/5 : 95/5 = 15 : 19, which is the lowest form.
Formula: Percentage of a quantity = (percentage/100) x quantity. Step 1: 30% of 1500 = (30/100) x 1500. Step 2: 30 x 15 = 450, so the answer is 450.

mcqs.q: 2/3 in terms of percentage is:
mcqs.why: Formula: Fraction to percentage = fraction x 100%. Step 1: (2/3) x 100% = 200/3 %. Step 2: 200/3 = 66 2/3, so the exact value is 66 2/3%; the key rounds this to 67%.

lessons.title: Exercise 2.1 — Zakat, Ushr and Inheritance
lessons.notes_html:
Exercise 2.1 of Unit 2 — Zakat, Ushr and Inheritance — complete solved exercises with every step shown.

Exercise 2.1 — Question 1

Q. Calculate Zakat on gold amounting to Rs. 11,10,000.

Formula: Zakat = total value x 2.5% = total value x (2.5/100) = total value/40

Step 1: Zakat = 11,10,000 x (2.5/100)

Step 2: = 11,10,000/40 = Rs. 27,750

So the Zakat is Rs. 27,750.

Exercise 2.1 — Question 2

Q. Calculate Zakat on silver amounting to Rs. 3,00,000.

Formula: Zakat = total value x 2.5% = total value x (2.5/100) = total value/40

Step 1: Zakat = 3,00,000 x (2.5/100)

Step 2: = 3,00,000/40 = Rs. 7,500

So the Zakat is Rs. 7,500.

Exercise 2.1 — Question 3

Q. Calculate the amount of Zakat on 10 tola gold and 40 tola silver, if the rate of gold is Rs. 40,000 per tola and the rate of silver is Rs. 5000 per tola.

Step 1: Value of gold = 10 x 40,000 = Rs. 4,00,000

Step 2: Value of silver = 40 x 5000 = Rs. 2,00,000

Step 3: Total value = 4,00,000 + 2,00,000 = Rs. 6,00,000

Formula: Zakat = total value x 2.5% = total value x (2.5/100) = total value/40

Step 4: Zakat = 6,00,000/40 = Rs. 15,000

So the Zakat is Rs. 15,000.

Exercise 2.1 — Question 4

Q. Calculate Zakat on gold of worth Rs. 8,00,000, cash of amount Rs. 4,00,000 and silver of weight 50 tola (Rs. 5000 per tola).

Step 1: Value of silver = 50 x 5000 = Rs. 2,50,000

Step 2: Total value = 8,00,000 + 4,00,000 + 2,50,000 = Rs. 14,50,000

Formula: Zakat = total value x 2.5% = total value x (2.5/100) = total value/40

Step 3: Zakat = 14,50,000/40 = Rs. 36,250

So the Zakat is Rs. 36,250.

Exercise 2.1 — Question 5

Q. Calculate Ushr on a rice crop produced by natural resources amounting to Rs. 6,00,000.

Formula: The rate of Ushr on a crop watered by natural resources (rain etc.) = 10%

Step 1: Ushr = 6,00,000 x (10/100)

Step 2: = Rs. 60,000

So the Ushr is Rs. 60,000.

Exercise 2.1 — Question 6

Q. Calculate Ushr on a wheat crop amounting to Rs. 3,50,000 produced by artificial resources.

Formula: The rate of Ushr on a crop watered by artificial resources (canal, tube well etc.) = 5%

Step 1: Ushr = 3,50,000 x (5/100)

Step 2: = Rs. 17,500

So the Ushr is Rs. 17,500.

Exercise 2.1 — Question 7

Q. Work out the share of each, if the inherited property amounting to Rs. 7,50,000 is left by a deceased, who also left a widow, two son's and one daughter.

Rule: In the presence of children, the widow's share = 1/8 ; the remainder is divided among the sons and daughters in the ratio 2 : 1 (son = 2 shares, daughter = 1 share).

Step 1: Widow's share = 7,50,000 x (1/8) = Rs. 93,750

Step 2: Remainder = 7,50,000 - 93,750 = Rs. 6,56,250

Step 3: Sum of the ratio = 2 + 2 + 1 = 5

Step 4: Each son's share = (2/5) x 6,56,250 = Rs. 2,62,500

Step 5: Daughter's share = (1/5) x 6,56,250 = Rs. 1,31,250

So the widow gets Rs. 93,750, each son Rs. 2,62,500 and the daughter Rs. 1,31,250.

Exercise 2.1 — Question 8

Q. An amount of Rs. 4,00,000 left as an inheritance is to be distributed among a widow and four daughters. Work out the share of each.

Rule: In the presence of children, the widow's share = 1/8 ; the remainder is divided equally among the daughters.

Step 1: Widow's share = 4,00,000 x (1/8) = Rs. 50,000

Step 2: Remainder = 4,00,000 - 50,000 = Rs. 3,50,000

Step 3: Each daughter's share = 3,50,000/4 = Rs. 87,500

So the widow gets Rs. 50,000 and each daughter Rs. 87,500.

Exercise 2.1 — Question 9

Q. If a deceased left a property of worth Rs. 15,00,000, work out the share of the widow, if he left behind a widow (and no child).

Rule: In the case of no child, the widow's share = 1/4

Step 1: Widow's share = 15,00,000 x (1/4)

Step 2: = Rs. 3,75,000

So the widow's share is Rs. 3,75,000.

Exercise 2.1 — Question 10

Q. The inherited property amounting to Rs. 20,00,000 is left by a deceased. He left behind a widow and two son's. Work out the share of each.

Rule: In the presence of children, the widow's share = 1/8 ; the remainder is divided equally among the sons.

Step 1: Widow's share = 20,00,000 x (1/8) = Rs. 2,50,000

Step 2: Remainder = 20,00,000 - 2,50,000 = Rs. 17,50,000

Step 3: Each son's share = 17,50,000/2 = Rs. 8,75,000

So the widow gets Rs. 2,50,000 and each son Rs. 8,75,000.

Exercise 2.1 — Question 11

Q. Asghar left a property of worth Rs. 4,80,000. He left behind a widow, three sons and four daughters. Calculate the share of each one.

Rule: Widow's share = 1/8 ; in the remainder, son : daughter = 2 : 1

Step 1: Widow's share = 4,80,000 x (1/8) = Rs. 60,000

Step 2: Remainder = 4,80,000 - 60,000 = Rs. 4,20,000

Step 3: Sum of the ratio = (3 x 2) + (4 x 1) = 6 + 4 = 10

Step 4: Value of one share = 4,20,000/10 = Rs. 42,000

Step 5: Each son's share = 2 x 42,000 = Rs. 84,000 ; each daughter's share = Rs. 42,000

So the widow gets Rs. 60,000, each son Rs. 84,000 and each daughter Rs. 42,000.

Exercise 2.1 — Question 12

Q. Najeeb left a wealth amounting to Rs. 4,00,000. He left behind a widow, while they did not have any child. Find the share of Najeeb's widow.

Rule: In the case of no child, the widow's share = 1/4

Step 1: Widow's share = 4,00,000 x (1/4)

Step 2: = Rs. 1,00,000

So the widow's share is Rs. 1,00,000.

mcqs.q: The Zakat on gold amounting to Rs. 11,10,000 is:
mcqs.why: Formula: Zakat = total value x 2.5% = total value x (2.5/100) = total value/40. Step 1: Zakat = 11,10,000/40. Step 2: 11,10,000 divided by 40 = Rs. 27,750.

mcqs.q: The Zakat on silver amounting to Rs. 3,00,000 is:
mcqs.why: Formula: Zakat = total value x 2.5% = total value/40. Step 1: Zakat = 3,00,000 x (2.5/100) = 3,00,000/40. Step 2: 3,00,000 divided by 40 = Rs. 7,500.

mcqs.q: 10 tola gold at Rs. 40,000 per tola and 40 tola silver at Rs. 5000 per tola are held. The Zakat payable is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Gold value = 10 x 40,000 = Rs. 4,00,000, silver value = 40 x 5000 = Rs. 2,00,000, total = Rs. 6,00,000. Formula: Zakat = total/40. Step 2: 6,00,000/40 = Rs. 15,000.

mcqs.q: Gold worth Rs. 8,00,000, cash Rs. 4,00,000 and 50 tola silver at Rs. 5000 per tola are held. The Zakat payable is:
The Ushr on a rice crop of Rs. 6,00,000 produced by natural resources is:
mcqs.why: Formula: Ushr rate on a crop watered by natural resources = 10%. Step 1: Ushr = 6,00,000 x (10/100). Step 2: 6,00,000 x 0.10 = Rs. 60,000.

mcqs.q: The Ushr on a wheat crop of Rs. 3,50,000 produced by artificial resources is:
mcqs.why: Formula: Ushr rate on a crop watered by artificial resources = 5%. Step 1: Ushr = 3,50,000 x (5/100). Step 2: 3,50,000 x 0.05 = Rs. 17,500.

mcqs.q: A deceased leaves Rs. 7,50,000, a widow, two sons and one daughter. The widow's share is:
mcqs.why: Rule: In the presence of children, widow's share = 1/8 of the property. Step 1: Widow's share = 7,50,000 x (1/8). Step 2: 7,50,000 divided by 8 = Rs. 93,750.

mcqs.q: A deceased leaves Rs. 7,50,000, a widow, two sons and one daughter. Each son's share is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Widow = 7,50,000 x (1/8) = Rs. 93,750, remainder = 6,56,250. Step 2: Ratio sum = 2 + 2 + 1 = 5, son gets 2 shares. Step 3: Each son = (2/5) x 6,56,250 = Rs. 2,62,500.

mcqs.q: Rs. 4,00,000 is distributed among a widow and four daughters. Each daughter's share is:
mcqs.why: Rule: Widow's share with children = 1/8. Step 1: Widow = 4,00,000 x (1/8) = Rs. 50,000, remainder = Rs. 3,50,000. Step 2: Each daughter = 3,50,000/4 = Rs. 87,500.

mcqs.q: A deceased leaves Rs. 15,00,000 and a widow but no child. The widow's share is:
mcqs.why: Rule: In the case of no child, the widow's share = 1/4 of the property. Step 1: Widow's share = 15,00,000 x (1/4). Step 2: 15,00,000 divided by 4 = Rs. 3,75,000.

Review Exercise 2 — Question 3

Q. Calculate Zakat on gold amounting Rs. 15,00,000.

Formula: Zakat = total value x 2.5% = total value x (2.5/100) = total value/40

Step 1: Zakat = 15,00,000/40 = Rs. 37,500

So the Zakat is Rs. 37,500.

Review Exercise 2 — Question 4

Q. Calculate Ushr on a rice crop amounting Rs. 4,90,000 produced by artificial resources.

Formula: Ushr on a crop produced by artificial resources = value x 5%

Step 1: Ushr = 4,90,000 x (5/100) = Rs. 24,500

So the Ushr is Rs. 24,500.

Review Exercise 2 — Question 5

Q. A deceased left a property of worth Rs. 45,00,000. If he left behind a widow and two sons, work out the share of each.

Rule: Widow's share = 1/8 ; the remainder is divided equally among the sons.

Step 1: Widow's share = 45,00,000 x (1/8) = Rs. 5,62,500

Step 2: Remainder = 45,00,000 - 5,62,500 = Rs. 39,37,500

Step 3: Each son's share = 39,37,500/2 = Rs. 19,68,750

So the widow gets Rs. 5,62,500 and each son Rs. 19,68,750.

Review Exercise 2 — Question 6

Q. Akram left a property of worth Rs. 48,00,000. He left behind a widow, three sons and four daughters. Calculate the share of each.

Rule: Widow's share = 1/8 ; in the remainder, son : daughter = 2 : 1

Step 1: Widow's share = 48,00,000 x (1/8) = Rs. 6,00,000

Step 2: Remainder = 48,00,000 - 6,00,000 = Rs. 42,00,000

Step 3: Sum of the ratio = (3 x 2) + (4 x 1) = 10 ; one share = 42,00,000/10 = Rs. 4,20,000

Step 4: Each son = 2 x 4,20,000 = Rs. 8,40,000 ; each daughter = Rs. 4,20,000

So the widow gets Rs. 6,00,000, each son Rs. 8,40,000 and each daughter Rs. 4,20,000.
