lessons.title: Exercise 3.1 — Profit, Loss, Cost Price and Selling Price
lessons.notes_html:
Exercise 3.1 of Unit 3 — Business Mathematics — complete solved exercises with every step shown.

Exercise 3.1 — Question 1: Find the SP, when

Q. (i) CP = Rs. 950, Profit = 10% (ii) CP = Rs. 1540, Loss = 5% (iii) CP = Rs. 9600, Profit = 10% (iv) CP = Rs. 126000, Loss = 5% (v) CP = Rs. 480, Profit = 3% (vi) CP = Rs. 760, Loss = 4%

Formulas: Profit = SP - CP ; Loss = CP - SP ; Profit% = (Profit/CP) x 100 ; Loss% = (Loss/CP) x 100 ; SP = CP x (100 + Profit%)/100 (on profit) or CP x (100 - Loss%)/100 (on loss) — here CP = cost price, SP = selling price

(i) SP = 950 x (110/100) = Rs. 1045

(ii) SP = 1540 x (95/100) = Rs. 1463

(iii) SP = 9600 x (110/100) = Rs. 10,560

(iv) SP = 126,000 x (95/100) = Rs. 1,19,700

(v) SP = 480 x (103/100) = Rs. 494.40

(vi) SP = 760 x (96/100) = Rs. 729.60

Exercise 3.1 — Question 2

Q. Haris purchased a car for Rs. 248000 and spent Rs. 12000 on its denting and painting. He sold that at a profit of 5%. What did the customer pay to Haris?

Step 1: Actual cost price = 2,48,000 + 12,000 = Rs. 2,60,000 (extra expenses are included in the cost price)

Step 2: Formula: SP = CP x (100 + Profit%)/100

Step 3: SP = 2,60,000 x (105/100) = Rs. 2,73,000

So the customer paid Rs. 2,73,000.

Exercise 3.1 — Question 3: Find the CP, when

Q. (i) SP = Rs. 672, Profit = 5% (ii) SP = Rs. 851, Loss = 8% (iii) SP = Rs. 1755, Profit = 12 1/2% (iv) SP = Rs. 2640, Loss = 12% (v) SP = Rs. 100, Profit = 33 1/2% (as printed)

Formula: CP = SP x 100/(100 + Profit%) (on profit) or SP x 100/(100 - Loss%) (on loss)

(i) CP = 672 x 100/105 = Rs. 640

(ii) CP = 851 x 100/92 = Rs. 925

(iii) CP = 1755 x 100/112.5 = Rs. 1560

(iv) CP = 2640 x 100/88 = Rs. 3000

(v) CP = 100 x 100/(100 + 33 1/3) = 100 x 100/(400/3) = Rs. 75

Note: In part (v) the book's answer (Rs. 75) shows that the profit is 33 1/3%; the print resembles 33 1/2%.

Exercise 3.1 — Question 4

Q. A shop-keeper gains a profit of 7% by selling a dinner set for Rs. 3852. If he sells it for Rs. 4050, find his profit percentage.

Step 1: Formula: CP = SP x 100/(100 + Profit%) = 3852 x 100/107 = Rs. 3600

Step 2: Profit at the new SP = 4050 - 3600 = Rs. 450

Step 3: Profit% = (450/3600) x 100 = 12.5% = 12 1/2%

So on selling for Rs. 4050 the profit will be 12 1/2%.

Exercise 3.1 — Question 5

Q. The selling price of 12 articles is equal to the cost price of 15 articles. Find profit percentage.

Step 1: Let the cost price of each article = Re. 1, so CP of 15 articles = Rs. 15

Step 2: SP of 12 articles = CP of 15 articles = Rs. 15, and CP of 12 articles = Rs. 12

Step 3: Profit = 15 - 12 = Rs. 3

Step 4: Profit% = (3/12) x 100 = 25%

So the profit is 25%.

Exercise 3.1 — Question 6

Q. Find the cost price, if a fan is sold for Rs. 1470, to get a profit 1/6th of its cost price.

Step 1: Let CP = x ; Profit = x/6

Step 2: SP = CP + Profit = x + x/6 = 7x/6

Step 3: 7x/6 = 1470, so x = 1470 x 6/7 = Rs. 1260

So the cost price is Rs. 1260.

Exercise 3.1 — Question 7

Q. A man sold an almirah at a profit of 7 1/2%, had he sold it for Rs. 209, he would have lost 2%. For how much the man purchased it?

Step 1: Let CP = x

Step 2: In the first case SP = x x (107.5/100) ; in the second case SP = 209 = x x (98/100)

Step 3: From the second case: x = 209 x 100/98 = Rs. 213.27

So the man purchased the almirah for about Rs. 213 (the book's answer key gives Rs. 213).

Exercise 3.1 — Question 8

Q. Three chairs are purchased at Rs. 450 each. One of these is sold at a loss of 10%. At what price should the other two be sold so as to gain 20% on the whole transaction?

Step 1: Total CP = 3 x 450 = Rs. 1350

Step 2: Required SP for the whole transaction = 1350 x (120/100) = Rs. 1620

Step 3: SP of the first chair = 450 x (90/100) = Rs. 405

Step 4: Required total price of the other two chairs = 1620 - 405 = Rs. 1215

So the other two chairs should be sold for Rs. 1215 in total.

mcqs.q: Find the selling price when CP = Rs. 950 and Profit = 10%.
mcqs.why: Formula: SP = CP x (100 + Profit%)/100. Working: SP = 950 x 110/100 = 950 x 1.10 = Rs. 1045.

mcqs.q: Haris bought a car for Rs. 248000 and spent Rs. 12000 on denting and painting. He sold it at a profit of 5%. How much did the customer pay?
mcqs.why: Formula: SP = CP x (100 + Profit%)/100, with extra expenses added to CP. Working: Actual CP = 2,48,000 + 12,000 = Rs. 2,60,000; SP = 2,60,000 x 105/100 = Rs. 2,73,000.

mcqs.q: Find the cost price when SP = Rs. 672 and Profit = 5%.
mcqs.why: Formula: CP = SP x 100/(100 + Profit%). Working: CP = 672 x 100/105 = 67,200/105 = Rs. 640.

mcqs.q: Find the cost price when SP = Rs. 100 and Profit = 33 1/3%.
mcqs.why: Formula: CP = SP x 100/(100 + Profit%). Working: CP = 100 x 100/(100 + 33 1/3) = 100 x 100/(400/3) = Rs. 75. Note: the book prints the rate like 33 1/2%, but its own answer Rs. 75 is correct only for 33 1/3%, so 33 1/3% is used.

mcqs.q: A shopkeeper gains 7% by selling a dinner set for Rs. 3852. If he sells it for Rs. 4050, what is his profit percentage?
mcqs.why: Formula: CP = SP x 100/(100 + Profit%) and Profit% = (Profit/CP) x 100. Working: CP = 3852 x 100/107 = Rs. 3600; new profit = 4050 - 3600 = Rs. 450; Profit% = (450/3600) x 100 = 12.5% = 12 1/2%.

mcqs.q: The selling price of 12 articles is equal to the cost price of 15 articles. Find the profit percentage.
mcqs.why: Formula: Profit% = (Profit/CP) x 100. Working: let CP of each article = Re. 1, so CP of 12 articles = Rs. 12 and SP of 12 articles = CP of 15 articles = Rs. 15; Profit = 15 - 12 = Rs. 3; Profit% = (3/12) x 100 = 25%.

mcqs.q: A fan is sold for Rs. 1470 to get a profit of 1/6th of its cost price. Find the cost price.
mcqs.why: Formula: SP = CP + Profit. Working: let CP = x, then Profit = x/6 and SP = x + x/6 = 7x/6; 7x/6 = 1470, so x = 1470 x 6/7 = Rs. 1260.

mcqs.q: A man sold an almirah so that, had he sold it for Rs. 209, he would have lost 2%. For how much did he purchase it?
mcqs.why: Formula: CP = SP x 100/(100 - Loss%). Working: CP = 209 x 100/98 = 20,900/98 = Rs. 213.27 (the book key rounds this to Rs. 213).

mcqs.q: Three chairs are purchased at Rs. 450 each. One is sold at a loss of 10%. At what total price should the other two be sold to gain 20% on the whole transaction?
mcqs.why: Formula: SP = CP x (100 + Profit%)/100 for the whole deal. Working: total CP = 3 x 450 = Rs. 1350; required total SP = 1350 x 120/100 = Rs. 1620; first chair SP = 450 x 90/100 = Rs. 405; other two = 1620 - 405 = Rs. 1215.

mcqs.q: Find the selling price when CP = Rs. 480 and Profit = 3%.
mcqs.why: Formula: SP = CP x (100 + Profit%)/100. Working: SP = 480 x 103/100 = 480 x 1.03 = Rs. 494.40.

lessons.title: Exercise 3.2 — Marked Price and Discount
lessons.notes_html:
Exercise 3.2 of Unit 3 — Business Mathematics — complete solved exercises with every step shown.

Exercise 3.2 — Question 1: Find the selling price, when

Q. (i) MP = Rs. 728, Discount = 6% (ii) MP = Rs. 2760, Discount = 5% (iii) MP = Rs. 395.75, Discount = 8%

Formula: SP = MP - Discount, where Discount = MP x Discount%/100 ; here MP = marked price

(i) Discount = 728 x 6/100 = Rs. 43.68 ; SP = 728 - 43.68 = Rs. 684.32

(ii) Discount = 2760 x 5/100 = Rs. 138 ; SP = 2760 - 138 = Rs. 2622

(iii) Discount = 395.75 x 8/100 = Rs. 31.66 ; SP = 395.75 - 31.66 = Rs. 364.09

Note: In part (iii) the book's answer key prints Rs. 364.08; the correct calculation is Rs. 364.09.

Exercise 3.2 — Question 2: Find the marked price when

Q. (i) SP = Rs. 515.20, Discount = 8% (ii) SP = Rs. 858, Discount = 12% (iii) SP = Rs. 2400, Discount = 4%

Formula: MP = SP x 100/(100 - Discount%)

(i) MP = 515.20 x 100/92 = Rs. 560

(ii) MP = 858 x 100/88 = Rs. 975

(iii) MP = 2400 x 100/96 = Rs. 2500

Exercise 3.2 — Question 3

Q. The marked price of a ceiling fan is Rs. 720. It is sold for Rs. 684. What percentage discount is being allowed?

Step 1: Discount = MP - SP = 720 - 684 = Rs. 36

Step 2: Formula: Discount% = (Discount/MP) x 100 = (36/720) x 100

Step 3: = 5%

So a discount of 5% is being allowed.

Exercise 3.2 — Question 4

Q. The marked price of washing machine is Rs. 3640. During sale season it is sold for Rs. 3367. Find the discount percentage.

Step 1: Discount = 3640 - 3367 = Rs. 273

Step 2: Discount% = (273/3640) x 100 = 7.5%

So the discount is 7.5%.

Exercise 3.2 — Question 5

Q. The marked price of a book is Rs. 480. The shopkeeper offers a discount of 10% and still gains 8%. Find the price at which the shopkeeper purchased it.

Step 1: SP = MP x (100 - 10)/100 = 480 x 90/100 = Rs. 432

Step 2: Formula: CP = SP x 100/(100 + Profit%) = 432 x 100/108 = Rs. 400

So the shopkeeper purchased the book for Rs. 400.

Exercise 3.2 — Question 6

Q. A trader marks his goods in such a way that after allowing a discount of 10%, he gains 15%. If an article costs him Rs. 720, what is its marked price?

Step 1: SP = CP x (100 + 15)/100 = 720 x 115/100 = Rs. 828

Step 2: Formula: MP = SP x 100/(100 - Discount%) = 828 x 100/90 = Rs. 920

So the marked price is Rs. 920.

Exercise 3.2 — Question 7

Q. The list price of a TV is Rs. 12600. A discount of 5% is allowed on it. Further for cash payment a second discount of 2% is given. How much cash payment is to be made for buying it?

Step 1: Price after the first discount = 12,600 x 95/100 = Rs. 11,970

Step 2: Second (cash) discount = 11,970 x 2/100 = Rs. 239.40

Step 3: Cash payment = 11,970 - 239.40 = Rs. 11,730.60

So Rs. 11,730.60 are to be paid in cash.

Exercise 3.2 — Question 8

Q. If 15% discount on MP of a heater is allowed and still makes a profit of 2%. If it is sold on MP, what is profit percentage?

Step 1: Let MP = Rs. 100 ; SP (after discount) = 100 x 85/100 = Rs. 85

Step 2: CP = SP x 100/(100 + 2) = 85 x 100/102 = Rs. 83.33

Step 3: Profit on selling at the marked price = 100 - 83.33 = Rs. 16.67

Step 4: Profit% = (16.67/83.33) x 100 = 20%

So on selling at the marked price the profit will be 20%.

mcqs.q: Find the selling price when MP = Rs. 728 and Discount = 6%.
mcqs.why: Formula: SP = MP - Discount, where Discount = MP x Discount%/100. Working: Discount = 728 x 6/100 = Rs. 43.68; SP = 728 - 43.68 = Rs. 684.32.

mcqs.q: Find the selling price when MP = Rs. 395.75 and Discount = 8%.
mcqs.why: Formula: SP = MP - MP x Discount%/100. Working: Discount = 395.75 x 8/100 = Rs. 31.66; SP = 395.75 - 31.66 = Rs. 364.09. Note: the book key prints Rs. 364.08, but the correct subtraction gives Rs. 364.09.

mcqs.q: Find the marked price when SP = Rs. 515.20 and Discount = 8%.
mcqs.why: Formula: MP = SP x 100/(100 - Discount%). Working: MP = 515.20 x 100/92 = 51,520/92 = Rs. 560.

mcqs.q: The marked price of a ceiling fan is Rs. 720 and it is sold for Rs. 684. What percentage discount is allowed?
mcqs.why: Formula: Discount% = (Discount/MP) x 100, where Discount = MP - SP. Working: Discount = 720 - 684 = Rs. 36; Discount% = (36/720) x 100 = 5%.

mcqs.q: The marked price of a washing machine is Rs. 3640. During the sale season it is sold for Rs. 3367. Find the discount percentage.
mcqs.why: Formula: Discount% = ((MP - SP)/MP) x 100. Working: Discount = 3640 - 3367 = Rs. 273; Discount% = (273/3640) x 100 = 7.5%.

mcqs.q: The marked price of a book is Rs. 480. A discount of 10% is offered and the shopkeeper still gains 8%. At what price did he purchase the book?
mcqs.why: Formulas: SP = MP x (100 - Discount%)/100 and CP = SP x 100/(100 + Profit%). Working: SP = 480 x 90/100 = Rs. 432; CP = 432 x 100/108 = Rs. 400.

mcqs.q: A trader marks his goods so that after allowing a discount of 10%, he gains 15%. If an article costs him Rs. 720, what is its marked price?
mcqs.why: Formulas: SP = CP x (100 + Profit%)/100 and MP = SP x 100/(100 - Discount%). Working: SP = 720 x 115/100 = Rs. 828; MP = 828 x 100/90 = Rs. 920.

mcqs.q: The list price of a TV is Rs. 12600. A discount of 5% is allowed, and for cash payment a second discount of 2% is given. How much cash is paid?
mcqs.why: Formula: each discount is taken on the price left after the previous discount. Working: after 5% discount, price = 12,600 x 95/100 = Rs. 11,970; second discount = 11,970 x 2/100 = Rs. 239.40; cash payment = 11,970 - 239.40 = Rs. 11,730.60.

mcqs.q: A 15% discount on the marked price of a heater still makes a profit of 2%. If it is sold at the marked price, what is the profit percentage?
mcqs.why: Formulas: CP = SP x 100/(100 + Profit%) and Profit% = (Profit/CP) x 100. Working: let MP = Rs. 100, so SP after discount = Rs. 85; CP = 85 x 100/102 = Rs. 83.33; profit at MP = 100 - 83.33 = Rs. 16.67; Profit% = (16.67/83.33) x 100 = 20%.

mcqs.q: Find the selling price when MP = Rs. 2760 and Discount = 5%.
mcqs.why: Formula: SP = MP - MP x Discount%/100. Working: Discount = 2760 x 5/100 = Rs. 138; SP = 2760 - 138 = Rs. 2622.

lessons.title: Exercise 3.3 — Partnership and Sharing of Profit
lessons.notes_html:
Exercise 3.3 of Unit 3 — Business Mathematics — complete solved exercises with every step shown.

Exercise 3.3 — Question 1

Q. Distribute Rs. 200,000 as a profit in a business regarding three persons, if their shares are in the ratio 3:2:5.

Step 1: Sum of the ratio = 3 + 2 + 5 = 10

Step 2: First share = (3/10) x 2,00,000 = Rs. 60,000

Step 3: Second share = (2/10) x 2,00,000 = Rs. 40,000

Step 4: Third share = (5/10) x 2,00,000 = Rs. 1,00,000

So the shares are Rs. 60,000, Rs. 40,000 and Rs. 1,00,000 respectively.

Exercise 3.3 — Question 2

Q. If Ali, Daniyal and Abdullah earned 15% profit against an investment of Rs. 750,000. Find the profit of each if their shares are in the ratio 2:3:5.

Step 1: Total profit = 7,50,000 x 15/100 = Rs. 1,12,500

Step 2: Sum of the ratio = 2 + 3 + 5 = 10

Step 3: Ali = (2/10) x 1,12,500 = Rs. 22,500 ; Daniyal = (3/10) x 1,12,500 = Rs. 33,750 ; Abdullah = (5/10) x 1,12,500 = Rs. 56,250

So Ali gets Rs. 22,500, Daniyal Rs. 33,750 and Abdullah Rs. 56,250.

Exercise 3.3 — Question 3

Q. Distribute Rs. 720 as profit amongst three people, so that their shares are in the ratio 3:4:5.

Step 1: Sum of the ratio = 3 + 4 + 5 = 12

Step 2: Shares = (3/12) x 720 = Rs. 180 ; (4/12) x 720 = Rs. 240 ; (5/12) x 720 = Rs. 300

So the shares are Rs. 180, Rs. 240 and Rs. 300 respectively.

Exercise 3.3 — Question 4

Q. Three persons invested an amount of Rs. 3,000,000 in a business with shares ratio 2:3:7. They earned a profit of Rs. 600,000. If they are interested to wind up their business, what amount every share holder would get?

Step 1: Sum of the ratio = 2 + 3 + 7 = 12

Step 2: Investment shares: first = (2/12) x 30,00,000 = Rs. 5,00,000 ; second = (3/12) x 30,00,000 = Rs. 7,50,000 ; third = (7/12) x 30,00,000 = Rs. 17,50,000

Step 3: Profit shares: first = (2/12) x 6,00,000 = Rs. 1,00,000 ; second = Rs. 1,50,000 ; third = Rs. 3,50,000

Step 4: Total received = investment + profit: first = 5,00,000 + 1,00,000 = Rs. 6,00,000 ; second = 7,50,000 + 1,50,000 = Rs. 9,00,000 ; third = 17,50,000 + 3,50,000 = Rs. 21,00,000

So every share holder will get Rs. 6,00,000, Rs. 9,00,000 and Rs. 21,00,000 respectively.

Exercise 3.3 — Question 5

Q. Three members of a firm distribute the profit Rs. 67,200 among themselves in the ratio 2:3:7. What is the biggest share of the profit?

Step 1: Sum of the ratio = 2 + 3 + 7 = 12

Step 2: Biggest share = (7/12) x 67,200 = Rs. 39,200

So the biggest share is Rs. 39,200.

Exercise 3.3 — Question 6

Q. A sum of money is divided among three persons, A, B and C in the ratio 10:7:5 respectively. If "B" gets Rs. 14 more than "C". How much will "A" get and what is the total sum of money?

Step 1: Difference of the shares of B and C = 7 - 5 = 2 shares

Step 2: 2 shares = Rs. 14, so 1 share = Rs. 7

Step 3: A's share = 10 x 7 = Rs. 70

Step 4: Total sum = (10 + 7 + 5) x 7 = 22 x 7 = Rs. 154

So A will get Rs. 70 and the total sum is Rs. 154.

mcqs.q: Distribute Rs. 200,000 as profit among three persons whose shares are in the ratio 3:2:5. What is the first person's share?
mcqs.why: Formula: Share = (own ratio part / sum of ratio) x total amount. Working: sum of ratio = 3 + 2 + 5 = 10; first share = (3/10) x 2,00,000 = Rs. 60,000.

mcqs.q: Ali, Daniyal and Abdullah earned 15% profit on an investment of Rs. 750,000. Their shares are in the ratio 2:3:5. What is Daniyal's profit?
mcqs.why: Formulas: Total profit = Investment x Profit%/100; Share = (part/sum of ratio) x total profit. Working: total profit = 7,50,000 x 15/100 = Rs. 1,12,500; sum of ratio = 10; Daniyal = (3/10) x 1,12,500 = Rs. 33,750.

mcqs.q: Distribute Rs. 720 as profit among three people in the ratio 3:4:5. What is the middle share?
mcqs.why: Formula: Share = (own ratio part / sum of ratio) x total amount. Working: sum of ratio = 3 + 4 + 5 = 12; middle share = (4/12) x 720 = Rs. 240.

mcqs.q: Three persons invested Rs. 3,000,000 in the ratio 2:3:7 and earned a profit of Rs. 600,000. On winding up, how much does the third person get in total?
mcqs.why: Formula: Total received = investment share + profit share, each = (part/sum of ratio) x amount. Working: sum of ratio = 12; investment share = (7/12) x 30,00,000 = Rs. 17,50,000; profit share = (7/12) x 6,00,000 = Rs. 3,50,000; total = 17,50,000 + 3,50,000 = Rs. 21,00,000.

mcqs.q: Three members of a firm distribute a profit of Rs. 67,200 in the ratio 2:3:7. What is the biggest share?
mcqs.why: Formula: Biggest share = (largest ratio part / sum of ratio) x total profit. Working: sum of ratio = 2 + 3 + 7 = 12; biggest share = (7/12) x 67,200 = Rs. 39,200.

mcqs.q: A sum is divided among A, B and C in the ratio 10:7:5. B gets Rs. 14 more than C. How much does A get?
mcqs.why: Formula: value of one share = given difference / difference of ratio parts. Working: B - C = 7 - 5 = 2 shares = Rs. 14, so 1 share = Rs. 7; A = 10 x 7 = Rs. 70.

mcqs.q: A sum is divided among A, B and C in the ratio 10:7:5, and B gets Rs. 14 more than C. What is the total sum?
mcqs.why: Formula: Total sum = (sum of ratio) x value of one share. Working: B - C = 2 shares = Rs. 14, so 1 share = Rs. 7; sum of ratio = 10 + 7 + 5 = 22; total = 22 x 7 = Rs. 154.

mcqs.q: Distribute Rs. 1200 as profit among three persons in the ratio 3:4:5. What is the biggest share?
mcqs.why: Formula: Biggest share = (largest ratio part / sum of ratio) x total amount. Working: sum of ratio = 3 + 4 + 5 = 12; biggest share = (5/12) x 1200 = Rs. 500. (Same method as the book's ratio questions, with new numbers.)

mcqs.q: A profit of Rs. 90,000 is divided among three partners in the ratio 2:3:5. What is the smallest share?
mcqs.why: Formula: Smallest share = (smallest ratio part / sum of ratio) x total profit. Working: sum of ratio = 2 + 3 + 5 = 10; smallest share = (2/10) x 90,000 = Rs. 18,000. (Same method as the book's ratio questions, with new numbers.)

mcqs.q: Three persons invested in the ratio 2:3:7 and earned a profit of Rs. 600,000. What is the second person's share of the profit?
mcqs.why: Formula: Profit share = (own ratio part / sum of ratio) x total profit. Working: sum of ratio = 2 + 3 + 7 = 12; second share = (3/12) x 6,00,000 = Rs. 1,50,000.

lessons.title: Review Exercise 3 — Unit 3 Review — Business Mathematics
lessons.notes_html:
Review Exercise 3 of Unit 3 — Business Mathematics — complete solved exercises with every step shown.

Review Exercise 3 — Question 1 (i): Encircle the correct answer

Profit is earned when:

(a) SP = CP   (b) SP < CP   (c) SP > CP   (d) none of these

Correct answer: SP > CP

Review Exercise 3 — Question 1 (ii): Encircle the correct answer

Loss is there when:

(a) SP = CP   (b) SP < CP   (c) SP = MP   (d) SP > CP

Correct answer: SP < CP

Review Exercise 3 — Question 1 (iii): Encircle the correct answer

Profit % = ? where SP > CP

(a) Profit/CP   (b) (Profit/CP) x 100   (c) (CP x Profit%)/100   (d) (100 x SP)/(100 + Profit%)

Correct answer: (Profit/CP) x 100

Review Exercise 3 — Question 1 (iv): Encircle the correct answer

SP = ? where SP > CP

(a) Profit - CP   (b) ((100 + Profit%)/100) x CP   (c) CP - Loss   (d) (CP x Loss%)/100

Correct answer: ((100 + Profit%)/100) x CP

Review Exercise 3 — Question 1 (v): Encircle the correct answer

CP = ?

(a) (100 x SP)/(100 + Profit%)   (b) Loss - SP   (c) MP + Discount   (d) (Discount x 100)/MP

Correct answer: (100 x SP)/(100 + Profit%)

Review Exercise 3 — Question 2 (i): Fill in the blanks

Fill in the blank: The price at which a particular item is purchased is called _______ Answer: cost price

Review Exercise 3 — Question 2 (ii): Fill in the blanks

Fill in the blank: The price at which an article is sold out is called _______ Answer: sale price

Review Exercise 3 — Question 2 (iii): Fill in the blanks

Fill in the blank: When SP > CP, CP = SP - _______ Answer: profit

Review Exercise 3 — Question 2 (iv): Fill in the blanks

Fill in the blank: When SP < CP, Loss % = _______ Answer: (Loss/CP) x 100

Review Exercise 3 — Question 2 (v): Fill in the blanks

Fill in the blank: MP = (100 x SP)/_______ Answer: 100 - Discount%

Review Exercise 3 — Question 3

Q. A shopkeeper gains a profit of 8% by selling a washing machine for Rs. 12000. If he sells it for Rs. 10,500, find his loss percentage.

Step 1: CP = SP x 100/(100 + 8) = 12,000 x 100/108 = Rs. 11,111.11

Step 2: Loss at the new price = 11,111.11 - 10,500 = Rs. 611.11

Step 3: Loss% = (611.11/11,111.11) x 100 = 5.5%

So the loss will be 5.5%.

Review Exercise 3 — Question 4

Q. If there is a 10% discount on marked price of a television and still makes a profit of 5%. If it is sold in marked price, what is profit percentage?

Step 1: Let MP = Rs. 100 ; SP after discount = Rs. 90

Step 2: CP = 90 x 100/105 = Rs. 85.71

Step 3: Profit on selling at the marked price = 100 - 85.71 = Rs. 14.29

Step 4: Profit% = (14.29/85.71) x 100 = 16.67% (the book's answer key gives 16.6%)

So on selling at the marked price the profit will be about 16.6%.

Review Exercise 3 — Question 5

Q. Distribute Rs. 33,000 as a profit in a business regarding three persons, if their shares are in the ratio 3:5:3.

Step 1: Sum of the ratio = 3 + 5 + 3 = 11

Step 2: Shares = (3/11) x 33,000 = Rs. 9000 ; (5/11) x 33,000 = Rs. 15,000 ; (3/11) x 33,000 = Rs. 9000

So the shares are Rs. 9000, Rs. 15,000 and Rs. 9000 respectively.

Review Exercise 3 — Question 6

Q. Three members of a firm distribute the profit amounting Rs. 1,44,000 among themselves in the 3:4:5. (i) What is the biggest share of the profit? (ii) What is the smallest share of the profit?

Step 1: Sum of the ratio = 3 + 4 + 5 = 12

Step 2: (i) Biggest share = (5/12) x 1,44,000 = Rs. 60,000

Step 3: (ii) Smallest share = (3/12) x 1,44,000 = Rs. 36,000

So the biggest share is Rs. 60,000 and the smallest share is Rs. 36,000.

mcqs.q: Profit is earned when:
mcqs.why: Profit = SP - CP. A profit exists only when the selling price SP is greater than the cost price CP, so that SP - CP is a positive amount. (Book Review Exercise 3, Question 1.)

mcqs.q: Loss is there when:
mcqs.why: Loss = CP - SP. A loss exists only when the selling price SP is less than the cost price CP, so that CP - SP is a positive amount. (Book Review Exercise 3, Question 1.)

mcqs.q: Profit % = ? when SP is greater than CP
mcqs.why: Formula: Profit% = (Profit/CP) x 100. The profit is always compared with the cost price CP and then multiplied by 100 to express it as a percentage. (Book Review Exercise 3, Question 1.)

mcqs.q: SP = ? when SP is greater than CP
mcqs.why: Formula: SP = CP x (100 + Profit%)/100, written as ((100 + Profit%)/100) x CP. It comes from SP = CP + Profit and Profit = CP x Profit%/100. (Book Review Exercise 3, Question 1.)

mcqs.q: CP = ?
mcqs.why: Formula: CP = (100 x SP)/(100 + Profit%). It is obtained by rearranging SP = CP x (100 + Profit%)/100 to make CP the subject. (Book Review Exercise 3, Question 1.)

mcqs.q: The price at which a particular item is purchased is called its:
mcqs.why: The price paid to purchase an item is its cost price (CP); the price at which it is sold is the sale price, and the price printed on it is the marked price. (Book Review Exercise 3, Question 2, converted from fill-in-the-blank.)

mcqs.q: When SP is greater than CP, CP = SP - _______
mcqs.why: Formula: Profit = SP - CP, so rearranging gives CP = SP - Profit. This holds when SP is greater than CP, that is, when there is a profit. (Book Review Exercise 3, Question 2, converted from fill-in-the-blank.)
Formula: MP = (100 x SP)/(100 - Discount%), obtained by rearranging SP = MP x (100 - Discount%)/100 to make MP the subject. (Book Review Exercise 3, Question 2, converted from fill-in-the-blank.)

mcqs.q: A shopkeeper gains a profit of 8% by selling a washing machine for Rs. 12000. If he sells it for Rs. 10,500, find his loss percentage.
There is a 10% discount on the marked price of a television and it still makes a profit of 5%. If it is sold at the marked price, what is the profit percentage?
mcqs.why: Formulas: CP = SP x 100/(100 + Profit%) and Profit% = (Profit/CP) x 100. Working: let MP = Rs. 100, so SP after discount = Rs. 90; CP = 90 x 100/105 = Rs. 85.71; profit at MP = 100 - 85.71 = Rs. 14.29; Profit% = (14.29/85.71) x 100 = 16.67% (the book key rounds this to 16.6%).

lessons.title: Exercise 4.1 — Foreign Exchange and Currency Conversion
lessons.notes_html:
Exercise 4.1 of Unit 4 — Financial Mathematics — complete solved exercises with every step shown.

Exercise 4.1 — Question 1

Q. Convert 250 US Dollar into Sterling Pound.

Note: The rates of the bank exchange-rate table given in the book (book page 74) are used in this exercise: US Dollar selling 84.100, buying TT Clean 83.800 ; Pound selling 129.7968, buying TT Clean 129.4542 ; Saudi Riyal buying TT Clean 22.3449

Step 1: The bank buys dollars at the buying (TT Clean) rate: 250 x 83.800 = Rs. 20,950

Step 2: The bank sells pounds at the selling rate: Pounds = 20,950/129.7968

Step 3: = 161.406

So 250 US Dollars = 161.406 Sterling Pounds.

Exercise 4.1 — Question 2

Q. Convert 5000 Riyals into Pak rupees.

Note: The rates of the bank exchange-rate table given in the book (book page 74) are used in this exercise: US Dollar selling 84.100, buying TT Clean 83.800 ; Pound selling 129.7968, buying TT Clean 129.4542 ; Saudi Riyal buying TT Clean 22.3449

Step 1: Buying rate (TT Clean) of the Riyal = Rs. 22.3449 per Riyal

Step 2: Amount = 5000 x 22.3449 = Rs. 1,11,724.50

So 5000 Riyals = Rs. 1,11,724.50.

Exercise 4.1 — Question 3

Q. An importer imports a car from Japan for 5000 yen. Delivery was to be made after three months. At the time of contract 1 yen = Rs 0.895236. At the time of delivery 1 yen = Rs 0.892236. Payment was made at the time of contract. Determine the profit or loss of the importer.

Step 1: Amount paid at the time of contract = 5000 x 0.895236 = Rs. 4476.18

Step 2: Value at the rate at the time of delivery = 5000 x 0.892236 = Rs. 4461.18

Step 3: He paid 4476.18 - 4461.18 = Rs. 15 more

So the importer suffered a loss of Rs. 15.

Exercise 4.1 — Question 4

Q. A customer wants to convert 150 American dollars into rupees. He goes to an authorised dealer. He offers him conversion at the rate of 1 dollar = Rs. 84.100. If it is converted with a money changer, the rate is 1 dollar = Rs. 83.4495, determine the amount into rupees if it is converted with: (i) Authorised dealer (ii) Money Changer (iii) The loss due to conversion with the money changer.

Step 1: (i) Authorised dealer: 150 x 84.100 = Rs. 12,615

Step 2: (ii) Money changer: 150 x 83.4495 = Rs. 12,517.42

Step 3: (iii) Loss = 12,615 - 12,517.42 = Rs. 97.58

So (i) Rs. 12,615, (ii) Rs. 12,517.42, (iii) loss Rs. 97.58.

Exercise 4.1 — Question 5

Q. Rate of tea in Pakistan is Rs. 2.1 per pound. Find the rate per Kilogram. (i) 1 pound = 0.4536 kilogram (ii) What will be the rate in Saudi Arabia if Saudi Riyal = Rs. 22.400.

Step 1: (i) The price of 0.4536 kg = Rs. 2.1, so the price of 1 kg = 2.1/0.4536 = Rs. 4.63

Step 2: (ii) Rate in Saudi Arabia = 4.6296/22.400 = 0.207 Riyal per kilogram (about 0.21 Riyal)

Note: The book's answer key prints 1.89375 Riyals for part (ii), which does not follow from the given rates; the correct calculation is 0.207 Riyal.

Exercise 4.1 — Question 6

Q. An exporter of carpets exports to England Carpets amounting to 40000 Sterling Pound. The spot buying rate exchange at that time was Rs. 129.4542 to 1 Sterling. He receives the amount at the time when rate is Rs. 129.0599 to 1 Sterling. How much he loses?

Step 1: Expected receipt = 40,000 x 129.4542 = Rs. 51,78,168

Step 2: Actual receipt = 40,000 x 129.0599 = Rs. 51,62,396

Step 3: Loss = 51,78,168 - 51,62,396 = Rs. 15,772

So he loses Rs. 15,772.

Exercise 4.1 — Question 7

Q. A Pakistani living in Saudi Arabia earns 4370 Riyals a month. His monthly expenses comes to 3450 Riyals. He remits his saving monthly to Pakistan. How much he saved in a year if rate of exchange is Rs. 22.400 = 1 Saudi Riyal. After a year Rate of exchanges is Rs. 22.3004. Determine the loss due to monthly remittance.

Step 1: Monthly saving = 4370 - 3450 = 920 Riyals

Step 2: Yearly saving = 920 x 12 = 11,040 Riyals, i.e. 11,040 x 22.400 = Rs. 2,47,296

Step 3: Fall in the rate = 22.400 - 22.3004 = 0.0996 rupees per Riyal

Step 4: Loss on the year's remittances = 11,040 x 0.0996 = Rs. 1099.58

So he loses Rs. 1099.58 due to the fall in the rate (profit in the book's key: Rs. 1099.58).

Exercise 4.1 — Question 8

Q. Rizwan purchases a car in Saudi Arabia for 15000 Riyals. Delivery was to be made after three months and payment is also to be made at the time of delivery. At the time of contract, the rate was 1 Riyal = Rs. 22.400, while at the time of delivery the rate was 1 Riyal = Rs. 22.0827. Determine the profit or loss in rupees due to change in the rate.

Step 1: Price at the contract rate = 15,000 x 22.400 = Rs. 3,36,000

Step 2: Payment at the delivery rate = 15,000 x 22.0827 = Rs. 3,31,240.50

Step 3: He pays 3,36,000 - 3,31,240.50 = Rs. 4759.50 less

So he gains (saves) Rs. 4759.50.

Exercise 4.1 — Question 9

Q. A friend of Ali living in Saudi Arabia remits Ali 450 Riyals. The bank offers two conversions rate. T.T. Buying Rs. 22.3449 = 1 Riyal ; T/C Buying Rate: Rs. 22.2146 = 1 Riyal. Which one of the rate will be profitable and also calculate the amount in rupees.

Step 1: Amount at the TT rate = 450 x 22.3449 = Rs. 10,055.20

Step 2: Amount at the T/C rate = 450 x 22.2146 = Rs. 9996.57

Step 3: Comparison: 10,055.20 > 9996.57, difference = Rs. 58.63

So the TT buying rate is profitable and Ali will receive Rs. 10,055.20. (Note: The book's answer key prints the second amount as Rs. 1857.37, which does not agree with the rates given in the question; at the printed T/C rate the amount is Rs. 9996.57, and the key's first figure Rs. 10055.20 is for TT buying.)

mcqs.q: Convert 250 US Dollars into Sterling Pounds. (Bank rates: 1 Dollar buying TT Clean = Rs. 83.800; 1 Pound selling = Rs. 129.7968)
mcqs.why: Method: first change dollars into rupees at the bank buying rate, then change rupees into pounds at the bank selling rate. Working: 250 x 83.800 = Rs. 20,950; Pounds = 20,950/129.7968 = 161.406 Pounds.

mcqs.q: Convert 5000 Saudi Riyals into Pak rupees. (1 Riyal buying TT Clean = Rs. 22.3449)
mcqs.why: Formula: Amount in rupees = foreign amount x buying rate per unit. Working: 5000 x 22.3449 = Rs. 1,11,724.50.

mcqs.q: An importer paid for a 5000-yen car at 1 yen = Rs. 0.895236. At delivery time 1 yen = Rs. 0.892236. What was his profit or loss?
mcqs.why: Working: amount paid = 5000 x 0.895236 = Rs. 4476.18; value at the delivery rate = 5000 x 0.892236 = Rs. 4461.18; he paid 4476.18 - 4461.18 = Rs. 15 more, so it is a loss of Rs. 15.

mcqs.q: A customer converts 150 American dollars at an authorised dealer at 1 dollar = Rs. 84.100. How many rupees does he get?
mcqs.why: Formula: Amount in rupees = dollars x rate per dollar. Working: 150 x 84.100 = Rs. 12,615.

mcqs.q: Tea costs Rs. 2.1 per pound and 1 pound = 0.4536 kilogram. What is the rate per kilogram?
mcqs.why: Formula: Rate per kg = price of 1 pound / weight of 1 pound in kg. Working: 0.4536 kg costs Rs. 2.1, so 1 kg costs 2.1/0.4536 = Rs. 4.63 (more exactly Rs. 4.6296).

mcqs.q: Tea costs Rs. 4.6296 per kilogram in Pakistan. What is the rate per kilogram in Saudi Arabia if 1 Saudi Riyal = Rs. 22.400?
mcqs.why: Formula: Rate in Riyals = rate in rupees / rupees per Riyal. Working: 4.6296/22.400 = 0.207 Riyal per kilogram (about 0.21 Riyal). Note: the book key prints 1.89375 Riyals, which does not follow from the given rates; the correct value is 0.207 Riyal.

mcqs.q: An exporter was to receive 40000 Sterling Pounds at Rs. 129.4542 per Pound, but received them at Rs. 129.0599 per Pound. How much does he lose?
mcqs.why: Formula: Loss = amount x (expected rate - actual rate), worked in two steps. Working: expected = 40,000 x 129.4542 = Rs. 51,78,168; actual = 40,000 x 129.0599 = Rs. 51,62,396; Loss = 51,78,168 - 51,62,396 = Rs. 15,772.

mcqs.q: A man in Saudi Arabia saves 920 Riyals every month and remits them to Pakistan. The rate falls from Rs. 22.400 to Rs. 22.3004 per Riyal. What is his loss on one year's remittances?
mcqs.why: Formula: Loss = total Riyals remitted x fall in the rate. Working: yearly saving = 920 x 12 = 11,040 Riyals; fall = 22.400 - 22.3004 = 0.0996; Loss = 11,040 x 0.0996 = Rs. 1099.58.

mcqs.q: Rizwan buys a car for 15000 Riyals, payable at delivery. The rate falls from Rs. 22.400 to Rs. 22.0827 per Riyal before delivery. What is his profit or loss?
mcqs.why: Working: price at the contract rate = 15,000 x 22.400 = Rs. 3,36,000; payment at the delivery rate = 15,000 x 22.0827 = Rs. 3,31,240.50; he pays 3,36,000 - 3,31,240.50 = Rs. 4759.50 less, so he gains Rs. 4759.50.

mcqs.q: Ali receives 450 Riyals. At the T/C buying rate of Rs. 22.2146 per Riyal, how much does he get in rupees?
mcqs.why: Formula: Amount in rupees = Riyals x rate per Riyal. Working: 450 x 22.2146 = Rs. 9996.57. Note: the book key prints Rs. 1857.37 for this rate, which is wrong; at the T/C rate the amount is Rs. 9996.57 (the TT rate Rs. 22.3449 gives Rs. 10,055.20 and is the profitable one).

lessons.title: Exercise 4.2 — Simple Profit
lessons.notes_html:
Exercise 4.2 of Unit 4 — Financial Mathematics — complete solved exercises with every step shown.

Exercise 4.2 — Question 1

Q. A financial institution charges Rs. 55 simple profit on a sum of money which is borrowed for five months. Given that the rate of profit is 12% per annum, find the sum of money.

Formula: Simple profit = (Principal x Rate x Time)/100, where the time is in years

Step 1: Time = 5/12 year ; let the principal = P

Step 2: 55 = (P x 12 x (5/12))/100 = 5P/100

Step 3: P = 55 x 100/5 = Rs. 1100

So the sum of money is Rs. 1100.

Exercise 4.2 — Question 2

Q. Mrs. Javed invests in Savings Scheme Rs. 800 at 6% per annum and Rs. 1,200 at 7% per annum. What is her total amount of profit on these two investments (in one year)?

Formula: Simple profit = (Principal x Rate x Time)/100, where the time is in years

Step 1: Profit on the first investment = (800 x 6 x 1)/100 = Rs. 48

Step 2: Profit on the second investment = (1200 x 7 x 1)/100 = Rs. 84

Step 3: Total profit = 48 + 84 = Rs. 132

So the total profit is Rs. 132.

Exercise 4.2 — Question 3

Q. How long would Rs. 1250 have to be deposited at 6% per year simple profit to gain Rs. 750 simple profit?

Formula: Simple profit = (Principal x Rate x Time)/100, where the time is in years

Step 1: 750 = (1250 x 6 x T)/100 = 75T

Step 2: T = 750/75 = 10

So the money will have to be deposited for 10 years.

Exercise 4.2 — Question 4

Q. Ali lent to Abid Rs. 4,800 for 7 months. At the end of this period Abid had to pay Ali profit of Rs. 119. What was the rate of simple profit per annum?

Formula: Simple profit = (Principal x Rate x Time)/100, where the time is in years

Step 1: 119 = (4800 x R x (7/12))/100 = 28R

Step 2: R = 119/28 = 4.25

So the rate per annum was 4.25%.

Exercise 4.2 — Question 5

Q. In a certain year, Javed puts Rs. 600 in a private bank at the end of March and Rs. 400 in the same bank at the end of June. The bank offers 3% per annum simple profit rate. Find the total amount Javed receives from the bank at the end of December in that year?

Formula: Simple profit = (Principal x Rate x Time)/100, where the time is in years

Step 1: Rs. 600 stays from April to December, 9 months: profit = (600 x 3 x (9/12))/100 = Rs. 13.50

Step 2: Rs. 400 stays from July to December, 6 months: profit = (400 x 3 x (6/12))/100 = Rs. 6.00

Step 3: Total received = 600 + 400 + 13.50 + 6.00 = Rs. 1019.50

So Javed will receive Rs. 1019.50.

Exercise 4.2 — Question 6

Q. At what annual rate of profit would a sum of Rs. 680 will increase to Rs. 850 in 3 years and 4 months?

Formula: Simple profit = (Principal x Rate x Time)/100, where the time is in years

Step 1: Profit = 850 - 680 = Rs. 170 ; Time = 3 1/3 years = 10/3 years

Step 2: 170 = (680 x R x (10/3))/100, so R = (170 x 100 x 3)/(680 x 10) = 7.5

So the rate is 7 1/2% per annum.

Exercise 4.2 — Question 7: Copy and complete the following table with the help of formula given in this unit (Principal, Profit rate, Time, Simple profit, Amount)

Q. (a) Principal Rs. 12,000, rate 8%, time 7 years (b) Principal Rs. 500, rate 11%, simple profit Rs. 220 (c) Rate 9%, time 4 years, simple profit Rs. 108 (d) Principal Rs. 3000, time 10 years, simple profit Rs. 1200 (e) Time 2 years, simple profit Rs. 360, amount Rs. 3960 (f) Principal Rs. 1800, time 18 years (as printed), simple profit Rs. 189 (g) Principal Rs. 4500, time 2 years, amount Rs. 5040 (h) Rate 5%, simple profit Rs. 90, amount Rs. 1290

Formula: Simple profit = (P x R x T)/100 ; Amount = Principal + Simple profit

(a) Profit = (12,000 x 8 x 7)/100 = Rs. 6720 ; Amount = 12,000 + 6720 = Rs. 18,720

(b) Time = (220 x 100)/(500 x 11) = 4 years ; Amount = 500 + 220 = Rs. 720

(c) Principal = (108 x 100)/(9 x 4) = Rs. 300 ; Amount = 300 + 108 = Rs. 408

(d) Rate = (1200 x 100)/(3000 x 10) = 4% ; Amount = 3000 + 1200 = Rs. 4200

(e) Principal = 3960 - 360 = Rs. 3600 ; Rate = (360 x 100)/(3600 x 2) = 5%

(f) Rate = (189 x 100)/(1800 x 1.5) = 7% ; Amount = 1800 + 189 = Rs. 1989 (Note: The book's table prints the time as '18 years', but the book key's rate of 7% is obtained only with 18 months; with 18 years the rate would be 0.58%.)

(g) Profit = 5040 - 4500 = Rs. 540 ; Rate = (540 x 100)/(4500 x 2) = 6%

(h) Principal = 1290 - 90 = Rs. 1200 ; Time = (90 x 100)/(1200 x 5) = 1 1/2 years

Exercise 4.2 — Question 8

Q. A bank increased the rate of profit from 3.5% to 4% per annum. Find how much more profit Saeed would receive if he deposited Rs. 6400 in the bank for 6 months at the new profit rate.

Formula: Simple profit = (Principal x Rate x Time)/100, where the time is in years

Step 1: Increase in the rate = 4% - 3.5% = 0.5%

Step 2: Extra profit = (6400 x 0.5 x (6/12))/100 = Rs. 16

So Saeed will receive Rs. 16 more profit.

Exercise 4.2 — Question 9

Q. Mrs. Jamshed invested Rs. 4000 in XYZ Bank Limited which paid simple profit at a rate 7 1/4% per annum to its investors. After 2 years, the rate was increased to 8% per annum. Find the amount she had at the end of 7 years.

Formula: Simple profit = (Principal x Rate x Time)/100, where the time is in years

Step 1: Profit of the first 2 years = (4000 x 7.25 x 2)/100 = Rs. 580

Step 2: Profit of the next 5 years = (4000 x 8 x 5)/100 = Rs. 1600

Step 3: Total amount = 4000 + 580 + 1600 = Rs. 6180

So at the end of 7 years she had Rs. 6180.

Exercise 4.2 — Question 10

Q. Mr. Dawood deposits a certain sum of money in ABC Limited. If the profit rate of the bank decreases from 3 3/4% per annum to 3 1/2% per annum, Mr. Dawood's profit will decrease by Rs. 50 in a year. Find the sum of money he deposits.

Formula: Simple profit = (Principal x Rate x Time)/100, where the time is in years

Step 1: Decrease in the rate = 3 3/4% - 3 1/2% = 1/4% = 0.25%

Step 2: Let the sum = P ; (P x 0.25)/100 = 50

Step 3: P = 50 x 100/0.25 = Rs. 20,000

So he deposits Rs. 20,000.

Exercise 4.2 — Question 11: Find the compound profit on

Q. (i) Rs. 450 for 2 years at 10% per annum compounded yearly; (ii) Rs. 700 for 3 years at 11% per annum compounded yearly; (iii) Rs. 5000 for 2 years at 11 3/4% per annum compounded yearly; (iv) Rs. 1200 for 3 years at 4% per annum compounded yearly; (v) Rs. 10000 for 3 years at 7 1/2% per annum compounded yearly;

Formula: Amount = P(1 + R/100)^T ; Compound profit = Amount - P

(i) Amount = 450 x (1.10)^2 = 450 x 1.21 = Rs. 544.50 ; Profit = 544.50 - 450 = Rs. 94.50

(ii) Amount = 700 x (1.11)^3 = 700 x 1.367631 = Rs. 957.34 ; Profit = Rs. 257.34

(iii) Amount = 5000 x (1.1175)^2 = 5000 x 1.24881 = Rs. 6244.03 ; Profit = Rs. 1244.03

(iv) Amount = 1200 x (1.04)^3 = 1200 x 1.124864 = Rs. 1349.84 ; Profit = Rs. 149.84 (the book's answer key prints Rs. 149.4)

(v) Amount = 10,000 x (1.075)^3 = 10,000 x 1.242297 = Rs. 12,422.97 ; Profit = Rs. 2422.97 (the book's answer key prints Rs. 2422.94 — a difference of step-by-step rounding)

Exercise 4.2 — Question 12

Q. Waseem invests Rs. 5000 at 5 1/4% per annum profit compounded annually. Find the amount at the end of the third year.

Formula: Amount = P(1 + R/100)^T

Step 1: Amount = 5000 x (1 + 5.25/100)^3 = 5000 x (1.0525)^3

Step 2: (1.0525)^3 = 1.165913, so Amount = 5000 x 1.165913 = Rs. 5829.57

So the amount at the end of the third year will be Rs. 5829.57.

Exercise 4.2 — Question 13

Q. Javed invests Rs. 800 at 12 1/2% per annum compound profit compounded half-yearly. What is the amount at the end of the first year?

Formula: In half-yearly compounding the rate is halved and the time is doubled: rate = 12.5/2 = 6.25% per half year, time = 2 half years

Step 1: Amount = 800 x (1.0625)^2 = 800 x 1.12890625

Step 2: = Rs. 903.13

So the amount at the end of the first year is Rs. 903.13.

Exercise 4.2 — Question 14

Q. Mr. Saleem invests Rs. 9000 at 2% per annum compound profit compounded daily. What is his amount at the end of the third day.

Note: As per the book's answer key (Rs. 9550.87), in this question the rate has been compounded at 2% per day.

Formula: Amount = P(1 + R/100)^T

Step 1: Amount = 9000 x (1.02)^3 = 9000 x 1.061208

Step 2: = Rs. 9550.87

So his amount at the end of the third day is Rs. 9550.87. (If the 2% per annum rate were strictly divided over the days, the amount would be about Rs. 9001.48.)

mcqs.q: A financial institution charges Rs. 55 simple profit on a sum borrowed for five months at 12% per annum. Find the sum of money.
mcqs.why: Formula: Simple profit = (Principal x Rate x Time)/100, Time in years. Working: Time = 5/12 year; 55 = (P x 12 x 5/12)/100 = 5P/100; P = 55 x 100/5 = Rs. 1100.

mcqs.q: Mrs. Javed invests Rs. 800 at 6% per annum and Rs. 1200 at 7% per annum. What is her total profit in one year?
mcqs.why: Formula: Simple profit = (Principal x Rate x Time)/100. Working: first profit = (800 x 6 x 1)/100 = Rs. 48; second profit = (1200 x 7 x 1)/100 = Rs. 84; total = 48 + 84 = Rs. 132.

mcqs.q: How long must Rs. 1250 be deposited at 6% per year simple profit to gain Rs. 750 simple profit?
mcqs.why: Formula: Simple profit = (Principal x Rate x Time)/100. Working: 750 = (1250 x 6 x T)/100 = 75T; T = 750/75 = 10 years.

mcqs.q: Ali lent Abid Rs. 4800 for 7 months. Abid paid Rs. 119 profit. What was the rate of simple profit per annum?
mcqs.why: Formula: Simple profit = (Principal x Rate x Time)/100, Time in years. Working: Time = 7/12 year; 119 = (4800 x R x 7/12)/100 = 28R; R = 119/28 = 4.25% per annum.

mcqs.q: At what annual rate of simple profit will Rs. 680 increase to Rs. 850 in 3 years and 4 months?
mcqs.why: Formula: Simple profit = (Principal x Rate x Time)/100. Working: Profit = 850 - 680 = Rs. 170; Time = 10/3 years; 170 = (680 x R x 10/3)/100, so R = (170 x 100 x 3)/(680 x 10) = 7.5% per annum.

mcqs.q: In the book's table, the principal is Rs. 1800, the simple profit is Rs. 189 and the time is 18 months. Find the rate.
mcqs.why: Formula: Rate = (Simple profit x 100)/(Principal x Time), Time in years. Working: Time = 18 months = 1.5 years; Rate = (189 x 100)/(1800 x 1.5) = 18,900/2700 = 7%. Note: the book table misprints the time as 18 years; with 18 years the rate would be 0.58%, and the key's 7% comes from 18 months.

mcqs.q: Mr. Dawood's yearly profit falls by Rs. 50 when the rate decreases from 3 3/4% to 3 1/2% per annum. Find the sum he deposits.
mcqs.why: Formula: Simple profit = (Principal x Rate x Time)/100. Working: decrease in rate = 3 3/4% - 3 1/2% = 0.25%; (P x 0.25 x 1)/100 = 50, so P = 50 x 100/0.25 = Rs. 20,000.

mcqs.q: Find the compound profit on Rs. 450 for 2 years at 10% per annum compounded yearly.
mcqs.why: Formula: Amount = P(1 + R/100)^T and Compound profit = Amount - P. Working: Amount = 450 x (1.10)^2 = 450 x 1.21 = Rs. 544.50; Profit = 544.50 - 450 = Rs. 94.50.

mcqs.q: Find the compound profit on Rs. 1200 for 3 years at 4% per annum compounded yearly.
mcqs.why: Formula: Amount = P(1 + R/100)^T and Compound profit = Amount - P. Working: Amount = 1200 x (1.04)^3 = 1200 x 1.124864 = Rs. 1349.84; Profit = 1349.84 - 1200 = Rs. 149.84. Note: the book key prints Rs. 149.4; the correct value is Rs. 149.84.

mcqs.q: Find the compound profit on Rs. 10000 for 3 years at 7 1/2% per annum compounded yearly.
mcqs.why: Formula: Amount = P(1 + R/100)^T and Compound profit = Amount - P. Working: Amount = 10,000 x (1.075)^3 = 10,000 x 1.242297 = Rs. 12,422.97; Profit = 12,422.97 - 10,000 = Rs. 2422.97. Note: the book key prints Rs. 2422.94 due to step rounding; the direct calculation gives Rs. 2422.97.

lessons.title: Exercise 4.3 — Compound Profit
lessons.notes_html:
Exercise 4.3 of Unit 4 — Financial Mathematics — complete solved exercises with every step shown.

Exercise 4.3 — Question 1

Q. A man borrowed Rs. 1460 from ABC Bank on the 3rd of March at 12 1/2% annually. What should he pay on the 1st of July to pay off the debt.

Formula: Markup/profit = (Principal x Rate x Time)/100 (simple) ; Compound amount = P(1 + R/100)^T

Step 1: Days from 3rd March to 1st July = 121 days (as counted in the book)

Step 2: Markup = (1460 x 12.5 x 121)/(100 x 365) = Rs. 60.50

Step 3: Total payment = 1460 + 60.50 = Rs. 1520.50

So he should pay Rs. 1520.50.

Exercise 4.3 — Question 2

Q. A shopkeeper borrowed Rs. 3540 from ABC Bank at 10 3/4% and lent the whole amount at 11 1/2% on the same day, what would be gained from this after 3 years and 4 months.

Formula: Markup/profit = (Principal x Rate x Time)/100 (simple) ; Compound amount = P(1 + R/100)^T

Step 1: Difference of the rates = 11 1/2% - 10 3/4% = 3/4% = 0.75%

Step 2: Time = 3 1/3 years ; Gain = (3540 x 0.75 x (10/3))/100 = Rs. 88.50

So he will gain Rs. 88.50.

Exercise 4.3 — Question 3

Q. XYZ Bank gained Rs. 8034 on its loan at 6% compound markup in 2 years. What amount did it lend?

Formula: Compound markup = P[(1 + R/100)^T - 1]

Step 1: (1.06)^2 - 1 = 1.1236 - 1 = 0.1236

Step 2: P = 8034/0.1236 = Rs. 65,000

So the bank lent Rs. 65,000.

Exercise 4.3 — Question 4

Q. A Company borrowed Rs. 6,600 from ABC Bank Ltd at 8% simple markup per annum. How much did the company owe to the bank at the end of 11 months?

Formula: Markup/profit = (Principal x Rate x Time)/100 (simple) ; Compound amount = P(1 + R/100)^T

Step 1: Markup = (6600 x 8 x (11/12))/100 = Rs. 484

Step 2: Total owed = 6600 + 484 = Rs. 7084

So the company owed Rs. 7084.

Exercise 4.3 — Question 5

Q. XYZ Bank charges 2.25% per month simple markup on personal loans. If Ali borrows Rs. 6,400 for a period of 2 years 1 month, find the total markup he has to pay to XYZ Bank.

Formula: Markup/profit = (Principal x Rate x Time)/100 (simple) ; Compound amount = P(1 + R/100)^T

Step 1: Time = 2 x 12 + 1 = 25 months

Step 2: Markup = 6400 x (2.25/100) x 25 = Rs. 3600

So the total markup is Rs. 3600.

Exercise 4.3 — Question 6

Q. Find out the compound markup on Rs. 250,000 for one year @ 14% compounded markup annually.

Step 1: Compound markup for one year = 2,50,000 x (14/100) = Rs. 35,000

So the compound markup is Rs. 35,000.

Exercise 4.3 — Question 7

Q. Find compound profit on Rs. 600 for 4 years at 6 percent per annum.

Formula: Compound profit = P[(1 + R/100)^T - 1]

Step 1: (1.06)^4 = 1.262477 ; Profit = 600 x 0.262477

Step 2: = Rs. 157.49

So the compound profit is Rs. 157.49.

Exercise 4.3 — Question 8

Q. Find the compound profit of Rs. 50000 at 4% for 1 1/2 years.

Method (as in the book): first one year's compound profit, then simple profit for the remaining half year on the new amount.

Step 1: Amount after one year = 50,000 x 1.04 = Rs. 52,000

Step 2: Profit for the next half year = (52,000 x 4 x 0.5)/100 = Rs. 1040

Step 3: Total amount = 52,000 + 1040 = Rs. 53,040 ; Compound profit = 53,040 - 50,000 = Rs. 3040

So the compound profit is Rs. 3040.

Exercise 4.3 — Question 9

Q. Find the compound profit on Rs. 54000 for one year at 12% per annum.

Step 1: Compound profit for one year = 54,000 x (12/100) = Rs. 6480

So the compound profit is Rs. 6480.

mcqs.q: A man borrowed Rs. 1460 on 3rd March at 12 1/2% annually. What should he pay on 1st July (121 days) to clear the debt?
mcqs.why: Formula: Markup = (Principal x Rate x Time)/100 with Time = days/365; Total = Principal + Markup. Working: Markup = (1460 x 12.5 x 121)/(100 x 365) = Rs. 60.50; Total payment = 1460 + 60.50 = Rs. 1520.50.

mcqs.q: A shopkeeper borrowed Rs. 3540 at 10 3/4% and lent it at 11 1/2% the same day. What does he gain after 3 years and 4 months?
mcqs.why: Formula: Gain = (Principal x difference of rates x Time)/100. Working: difference = 11 1/2% - 10 3/4% = 0.75%; Time = 10/3 years; Gain = (3540 x 0.75 x 10/3)/100 = Rs. 88.50.

mcqs.q: XYZ Bank gained Rs. 8034 on a loan at 6% compound markup in 2 years. What amount did it lend?
A company borrowed Rs. 6600 at 8% simple markup per annum. How much did it owe at the end of 11 months?
mcqs.why: Formula: Markup = (Principal x Rate x Time)/100; Total owed = Principal + Markup. Working: Markup = (6600 x 8 x 11/12)/100 = Rs. 484; Total owed = 6600 + 484 = Rs. 7084.

mcqs.q: XYZ Bank charges 2.25% per month simple markup. Ali borrows Rs. 6400 for 2 years 1 month. Find the total markup.
mcqs.why: Formula: Markup = Principal x monthly rate x number of months. Working: Time = 2 x 12 + 1 = 25 months; Markup = 6400 x (2.25/100) x 25 = 6400 x 0.5625 = Rs. 3600.

mcqs.q: Find the compound markup on Rs. 250,000 for one year at 14% per annum.
mcqs.why: Formula: Markup for one year = Principal x Rate/100 (for a single year compound and simple markup are equal). Working: 2,50,000 x 14/100 = Rs. 35,000.

mcqs.q: Find the compound profit on Rs. 600 for 4 years at 6% per annum.
mcqs.why: Formula: Compound profit = P[(1 + R/100)^T - 1]. Working: (1.06)^4 = 1.262477; Profit = 600 x 0.262477 = Rs. 157.49.

mcqs.q: Find the compound profit on Rs. 50000 at 4% for 1 1/2 years.
mcqs.why: Method of the book: one year compound, then simple profit for the half year on the new amount. Working: Amount after 1 year = 50,000 x 1.04 = Rs. 52,000; half-year profit = (52,000 x 4 x 0.5)/100 = Rs. 1040; Compound profit = 1040 + (52,000 - 50,000) = Rs. 3040.

mcqs.q: Find the compound profit on Rs. 54000 for one year at 12% per annum.
mcqs.why: Formula: Profit for one year = Principal x Rate/100. Working: 54,000 x 12/100 = Rs. 6480.

mcqs.q: A company borrowed Rs. 6600 at 8% simple markup per annum for 11 months. How much is the markup alone?
mcqs.why: Formula: Markup = (Principal x Rate x Time)/100, Time in years. Working: Time = 11/12 year; Markup = (6600 x 8 x 11/12)/100 = (6600 x 88)/(1200) = Rs. 484. (Same loan as the total-owed question in this exercise, asking only for the markup part.)

lessons.title: Exercise 4.4 — Insurance Premiums
lessons.notes_html:
Exercise 4.4 of Unit 4 — Financial Mathematics — complete solved exercises with every step shown.

Exercise 4.4 — Question 1: Complete the table for calculation of the premiums

Q. Conditions: Yearly premium @ 4.5% of the policy amount with policy fee @ 0.25% of the policy amount or at the most Rs. 200. Half yearly premium @ 52% of yearly premium. Quarterly premium @ 27% of yearly premium. Monthly premium @ 9% of yearly premium. Policy amounts: (i) Rs. 50,000 (ii) Rs. 1,00,000 (iii) Rs. 1,50,000 (iv) Rs. 2,00,000

Step 1: (i) 50,000: Yearly = 2250 + 125 = Rs. 2375 (fee = 0.25% x 50,000 = 125) ; Half yearly = 52% x 2375 = Rs. 1235 ; Quarterly = 27% x 2375 = Rs. 641.25 ; Monthly = 9% x 2375 = Rs. 213.75

Step 2: (ii) 1,00,000: Yearly = 4500 + 200 = Rs. 4700 (fee 0.25% = 250 but the limit is 200) ; Half yearly = Rs. 2444 ; Quarterly = Rs. 1269 ; Monthly = Rs. 423

Step 3: (iii) 1,50,000: Yearly = 6750 + 200 = Rs. 6950 ; Half yearly = Rs. 3614 ; Quarterly = Rs. 1876.50 ; Monthly = Rs. 625.50

Step 4: (iv) 2,00,000: Yearly = 9000 + 200 = Rs. 9200 ; Half yearly = Rs. 4784 ; Quarterly = Rs. 2484 ; Monthly = Rs. 828

Note: The book's answer key prints the quarterly premium of (i) as Rs. 641.50 and the monthly premium of (iii) as Rs. 625.30; the correct calculations are Rs. 641.25 and Rs. 625.50 respectively.

Exercise 4.4 — Question 2

Q. Calculate the amount to be received by the heirs of an insured if he died 2 years after buying the policy while. The amount of policy = Rs. 50,000 ; Premium is fixed @ 4.2% yearly ; Policy fee @ 0.3% ; Family income contract @ 0.6% ; Maturity period = 22 years ; Bonus @ 4.5% and Rs. 6000 yearly income is promised by the company.

By the book's method the heirs receive: policy amount + family income for the remaining period + bonus for the elapsed years

Step 1: Policy amount = Rs. 50,000

Step 2: Family income = 6000 x (22 - 2) = 6000 x 20 = Rs. 1,20,000

Step 3: Bonus = 4.5% x 50,000 x 2 years = 2250 x 2 = Rs. 4500

Step 4: Total amount = 50,000 + 1,20,000 + 4500 = Rs. 1,74,500

So the heirs will receive Rs. 1,74,500.

Exercise 4.4 — Question 3

Q. Mr. Ahmed Ali insured his house worth Rs. 75,00,000 @ 2% for 4 years calculate the amount paid in 4 years, while the rate of depreciation is 10% yearly.

Rule: Each year's premium is charged on that year's depreciated value.

Step 1: First premium = 2% x 75,00,000 = Rs. 1,50,000 ; depreciated value = 67,50,000

Step 2: Second premium = 2% x 67,50,000 = Rs. 1,35,000 ; depreciated value = 60,75,000

Step 3: Third premium = 2% x 60,75,000 = Rs. 1,21,500

Step 4: As per the book's answer key, total = 1,50,000 + 1,35,000 + 1,21,500 + 0 = Rs. 4,06,500

Note: The book's answer key shows the fourth year's premium as 0; if the fourth premium is also charged by the same rule (2% x 54,67,500 = Rs. 1,09,350), the total will be Rs. 5,15,850 — see Review Exercise 4 Question 3, where four premiums are counted in the same type of question.

Exercise 4.4 — Question 4

Q. Mr. Nadeem insured his shop @ 3% for 3 years, the depreciation rate is 5% yearly. If he paid an amount of Rs. 21000 as the 1st premium, what is the worth of his shop. If he got a claim of Rs. 200,000 after two years, how much benefit did he get?

Step 1: Worth of the shop = 21,000/0.03 = Rs. 7,00,000 (because the first premium = 3% of the worth)

Step 2: Second premium: depreciated value = 7,00,000 x 0.95 = 6,65,000 ; premium = 3% x 6,65,000 = Rs. 19,950

Step 3: Premiums paid in two years = 21,000 + 19,950 = Rs. 40,950

Step 4: Benefit = Claim - Premiums paid = 2,00,000 - 40,950 = Rs. 1,59,050

So the worth of the shop is Rs. 7,00,000 and the benefit is Rs. 1,59,050.

Exercise 4.4 — Question 5

Q. Mr. Adil bought a running business worth Rs. 10,00,000 and got it insured @ 2.5% as yearly premium for 4 years. After 3 years he got a claim of Rs. 500,000 for actual damages. How much loss had he recovered through insurance?

Rule (by the book's method for this exercise): the premium is charged each year on the value after 10% depreciation.

Step 1: Premiums: Year 1 = 2.5% x 10,00,000 = Rs. 25,000 ; Year 2 = 2.5% x 9,00,000 = Rs. 22,500 ; Year 3 = 2.5% x 8,10,000 = Rs. 20,250

Step 2: Total premiums paid = 25,000 + 22,500 + 20,250 = Rs. 67,750

Step 3: Loss recovered = Claim - Premiums = 5,00,000 - 67,750 = Rs. 4,32,250

So he recovered a loss of Rs. 4,32,250. (Note: The question states no depreciation, but the book key's Rs. 4,32,250 is obtained only with 10% yearly depreciation, as solved here.)

Exercise 4.4 — Question 6

Q. Mr. Javeed bought an insurance policy against his car worth Rs. 8,50,000, @ 4.25% for 3 years. What total amount will he pay as premium, if he had not claimed and damages during the period? Where depreciation rate is 10%.

Step 1: First premium = 4.25% x 8,50,000 = Rs. 36,125

Step 2: Depreciated value = 8,50,000 x 0.90 = 7,65,000 ; second premium = 4.25% x 7,65,000 = Rs. 32,512.50

Step 3: As per the book's answer key, total premium = 36,125 + 32,512.50 = Rs. 68,637.50

Note: The book's answer key counts two premiums; if the third year's premium (4.25% x 6,88,500 = Rs. 29,261.25) is also included, the total will be Rs. 97,898.75.

Exercise 4.4 — Question 7

Q. Mr. Rehman bought a vehicle worth Rs. 7,50,000. He got it insured @ 3.5% for 5 years. How much he paid in total for covering the risks, if he had got a claim of damages worth Rs. 100,000 during the period? Where depreciation rate is 10%.

Step 1: Premiums (on the depreciated value): Year 1 = 3.5% x 7,50,000 = Rs. 26,250 ; Year 2 = 3.5% x 6,75,000 = Rs. 23,625 ; Year 3 = 3.5% x 6,07,500 = Rs. 21,262.50 ; Year 4 = 3.5% x 5,46,750 = Rs. 19,136.25

Step 2: Total premiums paid = 26,250 + 23,625 + 21,262.50 + 19,136.25 = Rs. 90,273.75

Step 3: Net benefit = Claim - Premiums = 1,00,000 - 90,273.75 = Rs. 9726.25

So he paid Rs. 90,273.75 in total as premium and the net benefit is Rs. 9726.25.

Exercise 4.4 — Question 8

Q. Ms. Maria bought an insurance policy @ 3.25% for her car for 3 years. Her 1st premium is Rs. 26000. Tell the price of her car. Also calculate the amount of her 2nd and 3rd premium. (Assume depreciation 10% yearly)

Step 1: Price of the car = 26,000/0.0325 = Rs. 8,00,000

Step 2: Second premium: depreciated value = 8,00,000 x 0.90 = 7,20,000 ; premium = 3.25% x 7,20,000 = Rs. 23,400

Step 3: Third premium: depreciated value = 7,20,000 x 0.90 = 6,48,000 ; premium = 3.25% x 6,48,000 = Rs. 21,060

Note: The book's answer key prints the third premium as 'Zero' — a KEY ERROR; the correct third premium is Rs. 21,060.

mcqs.q: For a policy of Rs. 50,000 (yearly premium 4.5% of the policy amount plus policy fee 0.25%, quarterly premium 27% of the yearly premium), find the quarterly premium.
mcqs.why: Working: Yearly premium = 4.5% x 50,000 + 0.25% x 50,000 = 2250 + 125 = Rs. 2375; Quarterly premium = 27% x 2375 = Rs. 641.25. Note: the book key misprints this as Rs. 641.50; the correct value is Rs. 641.25.

mcqs.q: For a policy of Rs. 1,50,000 (yearly premium 4.5% plus policy fee 0.25%, fee at most Rs. 200; monthly premium 9% of the yearly premium), find the monthly premium.
mcqs.why: Working: Yearly premium = 4.5% x 1,50,000 + 200 (fee capped at Rs. 200) = 6750 + 200 = Rs. 6950; Monthly premium = 9% x 6950 = Rs. 625.50. Note: the book key misprints this as Rs. 625.30; the correct value is Rs. 625.50.

mcqs.q: For a policy of Rs. 1,00,000, the yearly premium is 4.5% of the policy amount plus a policy fee of 0.25% of the policy amount, the fee being at most Rs. 200. Find the yearly premium.
mcqs.why: Working: Premium part = 4.5% x 1,00,000 = Rs. 4500; fee = 0.25% x 1,00,000 = Rs. 250, but the fee is capped at Rs. 200; Yearly premium = 4500 + 200 = Rs. 4700.

mcqs.q: An insured person died 2 years after buying a policy of Rs. 50,000 (maturity 22 years, bonus 4.5% per year, family income Rs. 6000 per year for the remaining period). How much do his heirs receive?
mcqs.why: Method of the book: heirs receive policy amount + family income for the remaining years + bonus for the elapsed years. Working: family income = 6000 x (22 - 2) = Rs. 1,20,000; bonus = 4.5% x 50,000 x 2 = Rs. 4500; Total = 50,000 + 1,20,000 + 4500 = Rs. 1,74,500.

mcqs.q: Mr. Ahmed Ali insured his house worth Rs. 75,00,000 at 2% for 4 years, with depreciation 10% yearly. What is the total of the four yearly premiums?
Mr. Nadeem insured his shop at 3% and paid Rs. 21000 as the 1st premium. What is the worth of his shop?
mcqs.why: Formula: Worth = 1st premium / premium rate, because the first premium is charged on the full worth. Working: Worth = 21,000/0.03 = Rs. 7,00,000.

mcqs.q: Mr. Nadeem's shop is worth Rs. 7,00,000 (premium 3%, depreciation 5% yearly). He got a claim of Rs. 200,000 after two years. How much benefit did he get?
mcqs.why: Formula: Benefit = Claim - total premiums paid. Working: 2nd premium = 3% x (7,00,000 x 0.95) = 3% x 6,65,000 = Rs. 19,950; premiums paid = 21,000 + 19,950 = Rs. 40,950; Benefit = 2,00,000 - 40,950 = Rs. 1,59,050.

mcqs.q: Mr. Adil insured a business worth Rs. 10,00,000 at 2.5% yearly premium for 4 years (premium each year on the value after 10% depreciation). After 3 years he got a claim of Rs. 500,000. How much loss did he recover?
mcqs.why: Formula: Loss recovered = Claim - total premiums paid. Working: premiums = 2.5% x 10,00,000 = Rs. 25,000; 2.5% x 9,00,000 = Rs. 22,500; 2.5% x 8,10,000 = Rs. 20,250; total = Rs. 67,750; Loss recovered = 5,00,000 - 67,750 = Rs. 4,32,250.

mcqs.q: Mr. Javeed insured his car worth Rs. 8,50,000 at 4.25% for 3 years, with depreciation 10% yearly. What total premium does he pay in the 3 years?
mcqs.why: Rule: each year's premium is charged on the depreciated value. Working: premiums = 4.25% x 8,50,000 = Rs. 36,125; 4.25% x 7,65,000 = Rs. 32,512.50; 4.25% x 6,88,500 = Rs. 29,261.25; Total = 36,125 + 32,512.50 + 29,261.25 = Rs. 97,898.75.

mcqs.q: Ms. Maria's car policy is at 3.25% and her 1st premium is Rs. 26000 (depreciation 10% yearly). What is her 3rd premium?
mcqs.why: Working: price of car = 26,000/0.0325 = Rs. 8,00,000; 2nd premium = 3.25% x (8,00,000 x 0.90) = 3.25% x 7,20,000 = Rs. 23,400; 3rd premium = 3.25% x (7,20,000 x 0.90) = 3.25% x 6,48,000 = Rs. 21,060. Note: the book key prints the 3rd premium as Zero, which is a key error; the correct 3rd premium is Rs. 21,060.

lessons.title: Exercise 4.5 — Hire Purchase
lessons.notes_html:
Exercise 4.5 of Unit 4 — Financial Mathematics — complete solved exercises with every step shown.

Exercise 4.5 — Question 1: For each of the following, (i) find the additional amount you have to pay by financing and (ii) express the additional amount obtained in as a percentage of the cash price

Q. (a) Cash Rs. 360, Down Rs. 50, Monthly instalment Rs. 40, Instalments 10 (b) Cash Rs. 900, Down Rs. 150, Monthly instalment Rs. 75, Instalments 12 (c) Cash Rs. 25,000, Down Rs. 10,000, Monthly instalment Rs. 500, Instalments 36

Formula: Total payment = Down payment + (monthly instalment x number of instalments) ; Additional amount = Total payment - Cash price

(a) Total = 50 + 40 x 10 = Rs. 450 ; Additional = 450 - 360 = Rs. 90 ; Percentage = (90/360) x 100 = 25%

(b) Total = 150 + 75 x 12 = Rs. 1050 ; Additional = 1050 - 900 = Rs. 150 ; Percentage = (150/900) x 100 = 16 2/3%

(c) Total = 10,000 + 500 x 36 = Rs. 28,000 ; Additional = 28,000 - 25,000 = Rs. 3000 ; Percentage = (3000/25,000) x 100 = 12%

Exercise 4.5 — Question 2

Q. Pervaiz buys a window air-conditioner at Rs. 900. He pays 20% deposit and the outstanding balance plus markup in 48 months. Markup on the balance is charged at 10% (per annum). Find (i) the cost of his monthly instalment; (ii) the amount he saves by paying cash.

Step 1: Deposit = 20% of 900 = Rs. 180 ; Balance = 900 - 180 = Rs. 720

Step 2: Markup (48 months = 4 years) = 720 x 10% x 4 = Rs. 288

Step 3: (i) Total balance with markup = 720 + 288 = Rs. 1008 ; Monthly instalment = 1008/48 = Rs. 21

Step 4: (ii) Saving by paying cash = the markup = Rs. 288 (total payment in instalments 180 + 1008 = Rs. 1188, which is Rs. 288 more than the cash price 900)

So (i) monthly instalment Rs. 21, (ii) cash saving Rs. 288.

Exercise 4.5 — Question 3: On each of the following (i) find the financial price of the goods and (ii) express the amount saved by paying cash as a percentage of the cash price

Q. (a) Computer: Cash Rs. 200, Deposit 10%, Instalments 24, Monthly instalment Rs. 9 (b) Printer: Cash Rs. 450, Deposit 15%, Instalments 18, Monthly instalment Rs. 25 (c) Scanner: Cash Rs. 1600, Deposit 25%, Instalments 30, Monthly instalment Rs. 52

Formula: Finance price = Deposit + (monthly instalment x instalments) ; Amount saved by cash = Finance price - Cash price

(a) Deposit = 10% of 200 = Rs. 20 ; Finance price = 20 + 24 x 9 = Rs. 236 ; Saved = 36 ; Percentage = (36/200) x 100 = 18%

(b) Deposit = 15% of 450 = Rs. 67.50 ; Finance price = 67.50 + 18 x 25 = Rs. 517.50 ; Saved = 67.50 ; Percentage = (67.50/450) x 100 = 15%

(c) Deposit = 25% of 1600 = Rs. 400 ; Finance price = 400 + 30 x 52 = Rs. 1960 ; Saved = 360 ; Percentage = (360/1600) x 100 = 22.5%

Exercise 4.5 — Question 4: For each of the following, find (i) the monthly instalment and (ii) the difference in the hire purchase price and the cash price as a percentage of the cash price

Q. (a) Cash Rs. 800 ; Rs. 100 deposit; balance 8%; 1 year (b) Cash Rs. 8000 ; Rs. 200 deposit; balance 10%; 2 1/2 year (c) Cash Rs. 1200 ; Rs. 200 deposit; balance 15%; 1 1/3 year

Formula: Markup = Balance x Rate x Time (years) ; Monthly instalment = (Balance + Markup)/months ; Difference = Markup

(a) Balance = 700 ; Markup = 700 x 8% x 1 = Rs. 56 ; (i) Instalment = 756/12 = Rs. 63 ; (ii) Difference percentage = (56/800) x 100 = 7%

(b) Balance = 7800 ; Markup = 7800 x 10% x 2.5 = Rs. 1950 ; (i) Instalment = 9750/30 = Rs. 325 ; (ii) Difference percentage = (1950/8000) x 100 = 24.375% (Note: The book's answer key prints Rs. 200 and 15% for part (b), which do not follow from the printed terms.)

(c) Balance = 1000 ; Markup = 1000 x 15% x (4/3) = Rs. 200 ; (i) Instalment = 1200/16 = Rs. 75 ; (ii) Difference percentage = (200/1200) x 100 = 16 2/3%

Exercise 4.5 — Question 5

Q. The cash price of a computer package deal was Rs. 3200. Markup paid @ 15% down payment and the outstanding balance plus markup over 24 months. Markup on the balance was charged at 9.5%. (i) Find the cost of the package deal if it is bought on hire-purchase. (ii) Find the difference between the hire-purchase price and the cash price. (iii) Express the difference obtained in (ii) as a percentage of the cash price.

Step 1: Down payment = 15% of 3200 = Rs. 480 ; Balance = 3200 - 480 = Rs. 2720

Step 2: Markup = 2720 x 9.5% x 2 years = Rs. 516.80

Step 3: (i) Hire-purchase price = 3200 + 516.80 = Rs. 3716.80

Step 4: (ii) Difference = Rs. 516.80

Step 5: (iii) Percentage = (516.80/3200) x 100 = 16.15%

So (i) Rs. 3716.80, (ii) Rs. 516.80, (iii) 16.15%.

mcqs.q: Cash price Rs. 360, down payment Rs. 50, monthly instalment Rs. 40, 10 instalments. The additional amount paid by financing is what percentage of the cash price?
mcqs.why: Formulas: Total payment = Down payment + instalment x number of instalments; Additional = Total - Cash price; Percentage = (Additional/Cash price) x 100. Working: Total = 50 + 40 x 10 = Rs. 450; Additional = 450 - 360 = Rs. 90; Percentage = (90/360) x 100 = 25%.

mcqs.q: Cash price Rs. 900, down payment Rs. 150, monthly instalment Rs. 75, 12 instalments. Find the additional amount paid by financing.
mcqs.why: Formulas: Total payment = Down payment + instalment x number of instalments; Additional = Total - Cash price. Working: Total = 150 + 75 x 12 = Rs. 1050; Additional = 1050 - 900 = Rs. 150.

mcqs.q: Cash price Rs. 25,000, down payment Rs. 10,000, monthly instalment Rs. 500, 36 instalments. Find the additional amount paid by financing.
mcqs.why: Formulas: Total payment = Down payment + instalment x number of instalments; Additional = Total - Cash price. Working: Total = 10,000 + 500 x 36 = Rs. 28,000; Additional = 28,000 - 25,000 = Rs. 3000.

mcqs.q: Pervaiz buys an air-conditioner for Rs. 900. He pays a 20% deposit and the balance plus markup at 10% per annum over 48 months. Find his monthly instalment.
mcqs.why: Working: Deposit = 20% x 900 = Rs. 180; Balance = Rs. 720; Markup = 720 x 10% x 4 years = Rs. 288; total to pay in instalments = 720 + 288 = Rs. 1008; Monthly instalment = 1008/48 = Rs. 21.

mcqs.q: A printer has cash price Rs. 450, deposit 15%, 18 instalments of Rs. 25. Find the finance (hire-purchase) price.
mcqs.why: Formula: Finance price = Deposit + instalment x number of instalments. Working: Deposit = 15% x 450 = Rs. 67.50; Finance price = 67.50 + 18 x 25 = 67.50 + 450 = Rs. 517.50.

mcqs.q: A scanner has cash price Rs. 1600, deposit 25%, 30 instalments of Rs. 52. The amount saved by paying cash is what percentage of the cash price?
mcqs.why: Formulas: Finance price = Deposit + instalments total; Saved = Finance price - Cash price; Percentage = (Saved/Cash price) x 100. Working: Deposit = 25% x 1600 = Rs. 400; Finance price = 400 + 30 x 52 = Rs. 1960; Saved = Rs. 360; Percentage = (360/1600) x 100 = 22.5%.

mcqs.q: Cash price Rs. 800, deposit Rs. 100, balance charged at 8% for 1 year. The difference between the hire-purchase price and the cash price is what percentage of the cash price?
mcqs.why: Formulas: Difference = Markup on the balance; Percentage = (Markup/Cash price) x 100. Working: Balance = 800 - 100 = Rs. 700; Markup = 700 x 8% x 1 = Rs. 56; Percentage = (56/800) x 100 = 7%.

mcqs.q: Cash price Rs. 8000, deposit Rs. 200, balance charged at 10% for 2 1/2 years, paid in 30 monthly instalments. Find the monthly instalment.
mcqs.why: Formulas: Markup = Balance x Rate x Time; Monthly instalment = (Balance + Markup)/months. Working: Balance = 8000 - 200 = Rs. 7800; Markup = 7800 x 10% x 2.5 = Rs. 1950; Instalment = (7800 + 1950)/30 = 9750/30 = Rs. 325. Note: the book key prints Rs. 200, which does not follow from the given terms; the correct instalment is Rs. 325.

mcqs.q: For the same purchase (cash Rs. 8000, deposit Rs. 200, balance at 10% for 2 1/2 years), the difference between the hire-purchase price and the cash price is what percentage of the cash price?
mcqs.why: Formulas: Difference = Markup; Percentage = (Markup/Cash price) x 100. Working: Markup = 7800 x 10% x 2.5 = Rs. 1950; Percentage = (1950/8000) x 100 = 24.375%. Note: the book key prints 15%, which is irreconcilable with the given terms; the correct value is 24.375%.

mcqs.q: A computer package has cash price Rs. 3200, 15% down payment, and the balance plus markup at 9.5% over 24 months. The difference from the cash price is what percentage of the cash price?
mcqs.why: Formulas: Markup = Balance x Rate x Time; Percentage = (Markup/Cash price) x 100. Working: Down payment = 15% x 3200 = Rs. 480; Balance = Rs. 2720; Markup = 2720 x 9.5% x 2 = Rs. 516.80; Percentage = (516.80/3200) x 100 = 16.15%.

Review Exercise 4 of Unit 4 — Financial Mathematics — complete solved exercises with every step shown.

Review Exercise 4 — Question 2 (ix): Fill in the blanks

Review Exercise 4 — Question 2 (x): Fill in the blanks

Review Exercise 4 — Question 3

Q. Raheel insured his house worth Rs. 75,00,000 @ 2% for 5 years. Calculate the amount paid in 5 years, while the rate of depreciation is 10% yearly.

Rule: Each year's premium is charged on the depreciated value.

Step 1: Premiums: Year 1 = 2% x 75,00,000 = Rs. 1,50,000 ; Year 2 = 2% x 67,50,000 = Rs. 1,35,000 ; Year 3 = 2% x 60,75,000 = Rs. 1,21,500 ; Year 4 = 2% x 54,67,500 = Rs. 1,09,350

Step 2: As per the book's answer key, total = 1,50,000 + 1,35,000 + 1,21,500 + 1,09,350 = Rs. 5,15,850

Note: The book's answer key counts four premiums; if the fifth premium (2% x 49,20,750 = Rs. 98,415) is also included, the total will be Rs. 6,14,265.

Review Exercise 4 — Question 4

Q. Naeem insured his factory @ 3% for 3 years. With depreciation rate 5% yearly. If first premium is Rs. 21,000, find the worth of the factory, if he got a claim of Rs. 200,000 after two years. How much benefit did he get?

Step 1: Worth of the factory = 21,000/0.03 = Rs. 7,00,000

Step 2: Second premium = 3% x (7,00,000 x 0.95) = 3% x 6,65,000 = Rs. 19,950

Step 3: Benefit = 2,00,000 - (21,000 + 19,950) = 2,00,000 - 40,950 = Rs. 1,59,050

So the worth of the factory is Rs. 7,00,000 and the benefit is Rs. 1,59,050.

Review Exercise 4 — Question 5

Q. M/s Rahim printer purchases under hire-purchase system a machine from Lahore company on 1st January 2000, paying cash Rs. 10,000 and agreeing to pay three further instalments of Rs. 10,000 each on 31st December every year. The cash price of the machine is Rs. 37,230 and the Lahore company charges markup at 5% p.a. Draw table showing annual installment (Principal + Markup). (Table given in words)

Method: Each year the markup is charged at 5% on the outstanding principal at the start of the year; from the instalment the markup is taken out first and the rest goes to the principal; in the last instalment the small rounding difference is adjusted in the principal so that the balance becomes zero (the method of the book's Example 3).

Step 1: Start: Cash price Rs. 37,230 ; payment on 1st January 2000 Rs. 10,000 (principal) ; outstanding principal = Rs. 27,230

Step 2: 31st December 2000: Markup = 5% x 27,230 = Rs. 1361.50 ; principal part = 10,000 - 1361.50 = Rs. 8638.50 ; balance = Rs. 18,591.50

Step 3: 31st December 2001: Markup = 5% x 18,591.50 = Rs. 929.58 ; principal part = 10,000 - 929.58 = Rs. 9070.42 ; balance = Rs. 9521.08

Step 4: 31st December 2002: Principal part = balance Rs. 9521.08 ; Markup = 10,000 - 9521.08 = Rs. 478.92 ; balance = zero

Step 5: Totals: Total markup = 1361.50 + 929.58 + 478.92 = Rs. 2770 ; total principal repaid in instalments = Rs. 27,230 (plus the Rs. 10,000 paid in cash = cash price Rs. 37,230)

So the table's totals agree with the book's answer key: Markup Rs. 2,770, Principal (financed) Rs. 27,230.

mcqs.q: An instrument for payment order issued by a bank on the request of its customers is called:
mcqs.why: A pay order is the instrument a bank issues, on the request of its customer, ordering payment of a stated sum. A cheque is drawn by the customer himself. (Book Review Exercise 4, Question 1.)

mcqs.q: The person or entity whose insurance is being done is called the:
mcqs.why: The person or entity whose life or property is insured is the insured; the company doing the insurance is the insurer. (Book Review Exercise 4, Question 1.)

mcqs.q: The company undertaking the act of insurance is called:
mcqs.why: The company that undertakes the insurance risk is the insurer; the person covered is the insured, and the written contract is the insurance policy. (Book Review Exercise 4, Question 1.)

mcqs.q: The periodic instalment to be paid by the insured is called:
mcqs.why: The periodic instalment the insured pays to the insurer for the insurance cover is called the premium. (Book Review Exercise 4, Question 1.)

mcqs.q: The return earned by the bank on a loan is named as:
mcqs.why: The return a bank earns on the loans it gives is called mark up, while the amount a bank pays on deposits is called profit. (Book Review Exercise 4, Question 1.)

mcqs.q: The amount which is paid by the bank on the deposits is called:
mcqs.why: The amount a bank pays to its depositors on their deposits is called profit; the return the bank earns on loans is markup. (Book Review Exercise 4, Question 1.)

mcqs.q: The percentage of profit/markup charged is called:
mcqs.why: In the formula Profit = (Principal x Rate x Time)/100, the percentage charged is the rate, the sum lent or deposited is the principal, and the period is the time. (Book Review Exercise 4, Question 1.)

mcqs.q: A machine installed by the bank to dispense cash to customers is called an:
mcqs.why: An ATM is the machine installed by a bank that dispenses cash to customers holding a bank card, without going to a bank counter. (Book Review Exercise 4, Question 1.)

mcqs.q: A bill of exchange drawn on a specified banker and not expressed to be payable otherwise than on demand is called:
mcqs.why: By definition, a bill of exchange drawn on a specified banker and payable on demand is a cheque. (Book Review Exercise 4, Question 1.)
