lessons.title: Exercise 5.1 — Sales Tax and Other Taxes
lessons.notes_html:
Exercise 5.1 of Unit 5 — Consumer Mathematics — complete solved exercises with every step shown.

Exercise 5.1 — Question 1

Q. The price of a bicycle is Rs. 3500. If 16% sales tax is charged, then calculate the amount of sales tax on 50 such bicycles.

Step 1: Price of 50 bicycles = 50 x 3500 = Rs. 1,75,000

Step 2: Formula: Sales tax = Price x 16/100 = 1,75,000 x 0.16 = Rs. 28,000

So the sales tax is Rs. 28,000.

Exercise 5.1 — Question 2

Q. If the price of an air conditioner is Rs. 40,000, then work out the amount of sales tax on it at the rate of 16%. Also calculate the price of an air conditioner with sales tax.

Step 1: Sales tax = 40,000 x 16/100 = Rs. 6400

Step 2: Price with tax = 40,000 + 6400 = Rs. 46,400

So the sales tax is Rs. 6400 and the total price is Rs. 46,400.

Exercise 5.1 — Question 3

Q. The price of two cars of 1300 cc and 1600 cc without excise duty are 6,00,000 and Rs. 8,00,000 respectively. If the excise duty on these two are 200% and 250% respectively. Find the prices of the two cars inclusive duties.

Step 1: First car: Duty = 6,00,000 x 200/100 = Rs. 12,00,000 ; Price with duty = 6,00,000 + 12,00,000 = Rs. 18,00,000

Step 2: Second car: Duty = 8,00,000 x 250/100 = Rs. 20,00,000 ; Price with duty = 8,00,000 + 20,00,000 = Rs. 28,00,000

So the prices are Rs. 18,00,000 and Rs. 28,00,000 respectively.

Exercise 5.1 — Question 4

Q. The annual price of a house and price of land is Rs. 15,00,000 and Rs. 20,00,000 respectively. Find the property tax on each of these two at the rate of 16%.

Step 1: Tax on the house = 15,00,000 x 16/100 = Rs. 2,40,000

Step 2: Tax on the land = 20,00,000 x 16/100 = Rs. 3,20,000

So the property taxes are Rs. 2,40,000 and Rs. 3,20,000 respectively.

Exercise 5.1 — Question 5

Q. The total taxable income of two persons is Rs. 2,50,000 and Rs. 3,10,000 respectively. Work out the income tax for each of them @ 4.5%.

Formula: Tax = Taxable amount x Rate/100 ; Taxable income = Total income - Exempted amount

Step 1: First person's tax = 2,50,000 x 4.5/100 = Rs. 11,250

Step 2: Second person's tax = 3,10,000 x 4.5/100 = Rs. 13,950

So the income taxes are Rs. 11,250 and Rs. 13,950 respectively.

Exercise 5.1 — Question 6

Q. The total taxable income of a person is Rs. 4,30,000. If he is given rebate Rs. 3000 on the tax chargeable, then work out the amount he has to pay as an income tax @ 4.5%.

Formula: Tax = Taxable amount x Rate/100 ; Taxable income = Total income - Exempted amount

Step 1: Total tax = 4,30,000 x 4.5/100 = Rs. 19,350

Step 2: Payable after rebate = 19,350 - 3000 = Rs. 16,350

So he will pay Rs. 16,350.

Exercise 5.1 — Question 7

Q. If the total annual income of a person is Rs. 6,25,000 with exemption of amount of Rs. 1,50,000, then find the tax chargeable @ 4.5%.

Formula: Tax = Taxable amount x Rate/100 ; Taxable income = Total income - Exempted amount

Step 1: Taxable income = 6,25,000 - 1,50,000 = Rs. 4,75,000

Step 2: Tax = 4,75,000 x 4.5/100 = Rs. 21,375

So the tax chargeable is Rs. 21,375.

Exercise 5.1 — Question 8

Q. The total income of a person is Rs. 5,25,000. Whereas the exemption is Rs. 1,50,000. Work out the tax payable @ 4.5% along with the income tax rate, if Rs. 10,000 has already been deducted at source as income tax.

Formula: Tax = Taxable amount x Rate/100 ; Taxable income = Total income - Exempted amount

Step 1: Taxable income = 5,25,000 - 1,50,000 = Rs. 3,75,000

Step 2: Total tax = 3,75,000 x 4.5/100 = Rs. 16,875

Step 3: Payable = 16,875 - 10,000 = Rs. 6875

So the rate is 4.5% and the tax payable is Rs. 6875.

mcqs.q: The price of one bicycle is Rs. 3500. If 16% sales tax is charged, what is the sales tax on 50 such bicycles?
mcqs.why: Formula: Sales tax = Price x Rate/100. Price of 50 bicycles = 50 x 3500 = Rs. 175,000. Sales tax = 175,000 x 16/100 = 175,000 x 0.16 = Rs. 28,000.

mcqs.q: The price of an air conditioner is Rs. 40,000. What is the sales tax on it at the rate of 16%?
mcqs.why: Formula: Sales tax = Price x Rate/100. Sales tax = 40,000 x 16/100 = 40,000 x 0.16 = Rs. 6400. The price Rs. 46,400 is the total after adding this tax.

mcqs.q: The price of an air conditioner is Rs. 40,000 and sales tax is charged at 16%. What is the price of the air conditioner including sales tax?
mcqs.why: Step 1: Sales tax = 40,000 x 16/100 = Rs. 6400. Step 2: Price with tax = Price + Sales tax = 40,000 + 6400 = Rs. 46,400.

mcqs.q: A 1300 cc car costs Rs. 6,00,000 without excise duty. The excise duty is 200%. What is its price inclusive of duty?
A 1600 cc car costs Rs. 8,00,000 without excise duty. The excise duty is 250%. What is its price inclusive of duty?
The annual price of a house is Rs. 15,00,000. What is the property tax on the house at the rate of 16%?
mcqs.why: Formula: Property tax = Annual price x Rate/100. Tax = 15,00,000 x 16/100 = 15,00,000 x 0.16 = Rs. 2,40,000.

mcqs.q: The price of land is Rs. 20,00,000. What is the property tax on the land at the rate of 16%?
mcqs.why: Formula: Property tax = Price x Rate/100. Tax = 20,00,000 x 16/100 = 20,00,000 x 0.16 = Rs. 3,20,000.

mcqs.q: The total taxable income of a person is Rs. 2,50,000. What is his income tax at 4.5%?
mcqs.why: Formula: Tax = Taxable income x Rate/100. Tax = 2,50,000 x 4.5/100 = 2,50,000 x 0.045 = Rs. 11,250.

mcqs.q: The total taxable income of a person is Rs. 4,30,000. He is given a rebate of Rs. 3000 on the tax chargeable at 4.5%. How much income tax does he actually pay?
mcqs.why: Step 1: Total tax = 4,30,000 x 4.5/100 = Rs. 19,350. Step 2: Tax payable = Total tax minus Rebate = 19,350 - 3000 = Rs. 16,350.

mcqs.q: The total income of a person is Rs. 5,25,000 and the exemption is Rs. 1,50,000. Tax is charged at 4.5%, and Rs. 10,000 has already been deducted at source. What tax remains payable?
mcqs.why: Step 1: Taxable income = Total income minus Exemption = 5,25,000 - 1,50,000 = Rs. 3,75,000. Step 2: Total tax = 3,75,000 x 4.5/100 = Rs. 16,875. Step 3: Payable = 16,875 - 10,000 = Rs. 6875.

Exercise 5.2 — Question 1: Complete the gas bills with the help of the slabs given in the unit. Also include the meter rent and GST

Q. (i) 3.0756 Hm^3 (ii) 4.285 Hm^3 (iii) 2.796 Hm^3 (iv) 1.378 Hm^3 (v) 5.235 Hm^3 (vi) 4.665 Hm^3

Method (as per the book's answer key): 1 Hm^3 = 3.30 MMBTU ; Gas charges = Consumption (Hm^3) x 3.30 x slab rate (per MMBTU) ; then meter rent Rs. 120 is added and GST 16% is charged. Slab rates: 0-0.50: 80.65 ; 0.50-1: 84.45 ; 1-2: 153.73 ; 2-3: 325.48 ; 3-4: 423.42 ; 4-5: 550.44 ; above 5: 730.17. (Note: The book's worked example in the unit does not apply this 3.30 conversion, but its answer key does; the key's method is followed here.)

(i) Slab 5 (3-4): Charges = 3.0756 x 3.30 x 423.42 = Rs. 4297.49 ; + rent 120 = 4417.49 ; with GST = 4417.49 x 1.16 = Rs. 5124.29

(ii) Slab 6 (4-5): Charges = 4.285 x 3.30 x 550.44 = Rs. 7783.76 ; + 120 = 7903.76 ; with GST = Rs. 9168.06 (as per the book's answer key)

(iii) Slab 4 (2-3): Charges = 2.796 x 3.30 x 325.48 = Rs. 3003.13 ; + 120 = 3123.13 ; with GST = Rs. 3622.84

(iv) Slab 3 (1-2): Charges = 1.378 x 3.30 x 153.73 = Rs. 699.07 ; + 120 = 819.07 ; with GST = Rs. 950.12

(v) Slab 7 (above 5): Charges = 5.235 x 3.30 x 730.17 = Rs. 12,613.05 ; + 120 = 12,733.05 ; with GST = about Rs. 14,771.50 (as per the book's answer key)

(vi) Slab 6 (4-5): Charges = 4.665 x 3.30 x 550.44 = Rs. 8473.75 ; + 120 = 8593.75 ; with GST = Rs. 9968.75 (Note: The book's answer key prints Rs. 9848.75, which is exactly Rs. 120, the meter rent, less — a key shortfall.)

Exercise 5.2 — Question 2: Complete the Electricity bills, including the items as well as shown in the solved example of electricity bill

Q. (i) 315 units (ii) 210 units (iii) 375 units (iv) 290 units

Rates (as per the book): first 100 units @ Rs. 2.65 ; next 200 units @ Rs. 3.64 ; next 700 units @ Rs. 6.15 ; the rest @ Rs. 7.41. Extra items: excise duty 1.5%, electricity duty (as implied by the book's answer key), PTV fee Rs. 25, income tax 1.6% — all charged on the cost of units.

(i) 315 units: Cost = 100 x 2.65 + 200 x 3.64 + 15 x 6.15 = 265 + 728 + 92.25 = Rs. 1085.25 ; Excise = 16.28 ; Electricity duty = 11.50 ; PTV = 25 ; Income tax = 17.36 ; Total bill = Rs. 1155.39

(ii) 210 units: Cost = 265 + 110 x 3.64 = Rs. 665.40 ; Excise = 9.98 ; Electricity duty = 7.06 ; PTV = 25 ; Income tax = 10.65 ; Total bill = Rs. 718.09

(iii) 375 units: Cost = 265 + 728 + 75 x 6.15 = Rs. 1454.25 ; Excise = 21.81 ; Electricity duty = 15.67 ; PTV = 25 ; Income tax = 23.27 ; Total bill = about Rs. 1540

(iv) 290 units: Cost = 265 + 190 x 3.64 = Rs. 956.60 ; Excise = 14.35 ; Electricity duty = 10.15 ; PTV = 25 ; Income tax = 15.31 ; Total bill = Rs. 1021.41

Exercise 5.2 — Question 3: Complete the telephone bill including the items; Call rate Rs. 5 per call, FED @ 15%, W.H tax @ 4%

Q. (i) 530 (ii) 640 (iii) 750 (iv) 270 (v) 480 (vi) 315

Formula: Basic amount = Number of calls x 5 ; Total bill = Basic amount + FED 15% + Withholding tax 4% = Basic amount x 1.19

(i) 530 x 5 = 2650 ; Total = 2650 x 1.19 = Rs. 3153.50

(ii) 640 x 5 = 3200 ; Total = Rs. 3808.00

(iii) 750 x 5 = 3750 ; Total = Rs. 4462.50

(iv) 270 x 5 = 1350 ; Total = Rs. 1606.50

(v) 480 x 5 = 2400 ; Total = Rs. 2856.00

(vi) 315 x 5 = 1575 ; Total = Rs. 1874.25

mcqs.q: In the gas bill method of this unit, 1 Hm^3 of gas is equal to how many MMBTU?
mcqs.why: The book answer key method uses the conversion 1 Hm^3 = 3.30 MMBTU. Gas charges = Consumption in Hm^3 x 3.30 x slab rate per MMBTU, then meter rent Rs. 120 is added and GST 16% is charged.

mcqs.q: A consumer used 3.0756 Hm^3 of gas. This falls in slab 5 (3 to 4 Hm^3) at Rs. 423.42 per MMBTU. Including meter rent Rs. 120 and GST at 16%, what is the total gas bill?
A consumer used 1.378 Hm^3 of gas. This falls in slab 3 (1 to 2 Hm^3) at Rs. 153.73 per MMBTU. Including meter rent Rs. 120 and GST at 16%, what is the total gas bill?
A consumer used 4.665 Hm^3 of gas. This falls in slab 6 (4 to 5 Hm^3) at Rs. 550.44 per MMBTU. Including meter rent Rs. 120 and GST at 16%, what is the correct total gas bill?
mcqs.why: Step 1: Gas charges = 4.665 x 3.30 x 550.44 = Rs. 8473.75. Step 2: Add meter rent: 8473.75 + 120 = Rs. 8593.75. Step 3: Add GST 16%: 8593.75 x 1.16 = Rs. 9968.75. The book key prints Rs. 9848.75, which is exactly Rs. 120, the meter rent, less, so the corrected total is Rs. 9968.75.

mcqs.q: A consumer used 2.796 Hm^3 of gas. This falls in slab 4 (2 to 3 Hm^3) at Rs. 325.48 per MMBTU. Including meter rent Rs. 120 and GST at 16%, what is the total gas bill?
mcqs.why: Step 1: Gas charges = 2.796 x 3.30 x 325.48 = Rs. 3003.13. Step 2: Add meter rent: 3003.13 + 120 = Rs. 3123.13. Step 3: Add GST 16%: 3123.13 x 1.16 = Rs. 3622.84 (rounded).

mcqs.q: Electricity rates are: first 100 units at Rs. 2.65, next 200 units at Rs. 3.64, next 700 units at Rs. 6.15. What is the cost of 315 units?
mcqs.why: Step 1: First 100 units: 100 x 2.65 = Rs. 265. Step 2: Next 200 units: 200 x 3.64 = Rs. 728. Step 3: Remaining 15 units: 15 x 6.15 = Rs. 92.25. Total cost = 265 + 728 + 92.25 = Rs. 1085.25.

mcqs.q: For 210 units of electricity the cost of units is Rs. 665.40. The extra items are: excise duty Rs. 9.98, electricity duty Rs. 7.06, PTV fee Rs. 25 and income tax Rs. 10.65. What is the total bill?
mcqs.why: Total bill = Cost of units + Excise duty + Electricity duty + PTV fee + Income tax = 665.40 + 9.98 + 7.06 + 25 + 10.65 = Rs. 718.09.

mcqs.q: Electricity rates are: first 100 units at Rs. 2.65, next 200 units at Rs. 3.64, next 700 units at Rs. 6.15. What is the cost of 290 units?
mcqs.why: Step 1: First 100 units: 100 x 2.65 = Rs. 265. Step 2: Remaining 190 units fall in the next slab: 190 x 3.64 = Rs. 691.60. Total cost = 265 + 691.60 = Rs. 956.60.

mcqs.q: A telephone bill charges Rs. 5 per call, FED at 15% and withholding tax at 4%, both on the basic amount. What is the total bill for 530 calls?
mcqs.why: Step 1: Basic amount = Number of calls x 5 = 530 x 5 = Rs. 2650. Step 2: Total bill = Basic amount x (1 + 0.15 + 0.04) = 2650 x 1.19 = Rs. 3153.50.

mcqs.q: A telephone bill charges Rs. 5 per call, FED at 15% and withholding tax at 4%, both on the basic amount. What is the total bill for 750 calls?
mcqs.why: Step 1: Basic amount = Number of calls x 5 = 750 x 5 = Rs. 3750. Step 2: Total bill = Basic amount x (1 + 0.15 + 0.04) = 3750 x 1.19 = Rs. 4462.50.

lessons.title: Exercise 5.3 — Wages, Salaries and Income
lessons.notes_html:
Exercise 5.3 of Unit 5 — Consumer Mathematics — complete solved exercises with every step shown.

Exercise 5.3 — Question 1

Q. A lady worker works a six-day week. She starts work at 7.00 am and finishes at 4pm. She has 15 minutes break in the morning and 45 minutes break in the afternoon. How long does she actually work in a week and how much she is paid, if the rate of payment is Rs. 40 per hour?

Step 1: Total daily span = 7 am to 4 pm = 9 hours

Step 2: Breaks = 15 + 45 = 60 minutes = 1 hour ; Actual work = 9 - 1 = 8 hours daily

Step 3: Weekly work = 8 x 6 = 48 hours

Step 4: Payment = 48 x 40 = Rs. 1920

So she works 48 hours in a week and is paid Rs. 1920.

Exercise 5.3 — Question 2

Q. Khalid works 6 day-week. Find his gross monthly wage, if his rate of pay is Rs. 200 per day. (Month = 4 weeks)

Step 1: Working days in a month = 6 x 4 = 24 days

Step 2: Gross monthly wage = 24 x 200 = Rs. 4800

So his gross monthly wage is Rs. 4800.

Exercise 5.3 — Question 3

Q. Aslam gets paid Rs. 70 per hour for his normal working 8 hours daily (6 day week). The rate of over time is 1.5 of Rs. 70 per hour. If he works 40 hours as overtime, then work out his gross monthly pay. (Month = 4 weeks)

Step 1: Normal monthly hours = 8 x 6 x 4 = 192 hours ; Normal pay = 192 x 70 = Rs. 13,440

Step 2: Overtime rate = 1.5 x 70 = Rs. 105 per hour ; Overtime pay = 40 x 105 = Rs. 4200

Step 3: Gross monthly pay = 13,440 + 4200 = Rs. 17,640

So his gross monthly pay is Rs. 17,640.

Exercise 5.3 — Question 4

Q. Calculate the gross monthly pay of a person, if his basic pay is Rs. 18000, house rent allowances is Rs. 3500, dearness allowances is Rs. 3000, conveyance allowance is Rs. 1500 and medical allowance is Rs. 500.

Formula: Gross pay = Basic pay + all allowances

Step 1: Gross = 18,000 + 3500 + 3000 + 1500 + 500

Step 2: = Rs. 26,500

So the gross monthly pay is Rs. 26,500.

Exercise 5.3 — Question 5

Q. If gross pay of a person is Rs. 45,000, then calculate his net take home salary, after deductions of Rs. 400 as income tax, Rs. 1200 as benevolent fund, Rs. 1500 as G.P. fund and Rs. 400 as group insurance.

Formula: Net salary = Gross pay - Total deductions

Step 1: Total deductions = 400 + 1200 + 1500 + 400 = Rs. 3500

Step 2: Net salary = 45,000 - 3500 = Rs. 41,500

So the net take home salary is Rs. 41,500.

Exercise 5.3 — Question 6

Q. Noman works in a factory where the basic hourly rate is Rs. 50 for a 35 hour week. An over time is paid at time and-a-half. How much will he earn in a week when he works for: (i) 38 hours (ii) 48 hours (iii) 50 hours

Formula: Overtime rate = 1.5 x 50 = Rs. 75 per hour ; Basic weekly = 35 x 50 = Rs. 1750

(i) 38 hours: Overtime = 3 hours ; Earnings = 1750 + 3 x 75 = 1750 + 225 = Rs. 1975

(ii) 48 hours: Overtime = 13 hours ; Earnings = 1750 + 13 x 75 = 1750 + 975 = Rs. 2725

(iii) 50 hours: Overtime = 15 hours ; Earnings = 1750 + 15 x 75 = 1750 + 1125 = Rs. 2875

Exercise 5.3 — Question 7

Q. Abdullah's pay slip showed that he had worked 6 hours over time in addition to his basic 36 hours in a week. If his basic rate of pay is Rs. 60 and over time is paid at time and a-half. Find his gross pay for the month. (Month = 4 weeks)

Step 1: Basic weekly pay = 36 x 60 = Rs. 2160

Step 2: Overtime rate = 1.5 x 60 = Rs. 90 ; Overtime pay = 6 x 90 = Rs. 540

Step 3: Weekly gross = 2160 + 540 = Rs. 2700

Step 4: Monthly gross = 2700 x 4 = Rs. 10,800

So his gross monthly pay is Rs. 10,800.

mcqs.q: A lady worker works a six-day week, from 7.00 am to 4.00 pm daily. She has breaks of 15 minutes and 45 minutes each day. How many hours does she actually work in a week?
mcqs.why: Step 1: Daily span = 7 am to 4 pm = 9 hours. Step 2: Breaks = 15 + 45 = 60 minutes = 1 hour, so actual daily work = 9 - 1 = 8 hours. Step 3: Weekly work = 8 x 6 = 48 hours.

mcqs.q: A lady worker actually works 48 hours in a week and is paid at Rs. 40 per hour. How much is she paid for the week?
mcqs.why: Formula: Weekly payment = Hours worked x Rate per hour = 48 x 40 = Rs. 1920.

mcqs.q: Khalid works a 6-day week and his rate of pay is Rs. 200 per day. Taking a month as 4 weeks, what is his gross monthly wage?
mcqs.why: Step 1: Working days in a month = 6 days x 4 weeks = 24 days. Step 2: Gross monthly wage = 24 x 200 = Rs. 4800.

mcqs.q: Aslam is paid Rs. 70 per hour for 8 hours daily in a 6-day week. His overtime rate is 1.5 times Rs. 70 per hour, and he works 40 hours of overtime in a month of 4 weeks. What is his gross monthly pay?
mcqs.why: Step 1: Normal monthly hours = 8 x 6 x 4 = 192 hours; normal pay = 192 x 70 = Rs. 13,440. Step 2: Overtime rate = 1.5 x 70 = Rs. 105 per hour; overtime pay = 40 x 105 = Rs. 4200. Step 3: Gross monthly pay = 13,440 + 4200 = Rs. 17,640.

mcqs.q: Aslam's normal rate is Rs. 70 per hour and overtime is paid at 1.5 times the normal rate. What is his overtime rate per hour?
mcqs.why: Formula: Overtime rate = 1.5 x Normal rate = 1.5 x 70 = Rs. 105 per hour.

mcqs.q: A person's basic pay is Rs. 18,000, house rent allowance Rs. 3500, dearness allowance Rs. 3000, conveyance allowance Rs. 1500 and medical allowance Rs. 500. What is his gross monthly pay?
mcqs.why: Formula: Gross pay = Basic pay + All allowances = 18,000 + 3500 + 3000 + 1500 + 500 = Rs. 26,500.

mcqs.q: The gross pay of a person is Rs. 45,000. Deductions are: income tax Rs. 400, benevolent fund Rs. 1200, G.P. fund Rs. 1500 and group insurance Rs. 400. What is his net take home salary?
mcqs.why: Formula: Net salary = Gross pay minus Total deductions. Step 1: Total deductions = 400 + 1200 + 1500 + 400 = Rs. 3500. Step 2: Net salary = 45,000 - 3500 = Rs. 41,500.

mcqs.q: Noman's basic hourly rate is Rs. 50 for a 35-hour week, and overtime is paid at time and a half. How much does he earn in a week in which he works 38 hours?
mcqs.why: Step 1: Basic weekly pay = 35 x 50 = Rs. 1750. Step 2: Overtime rate = 1.5 x 50 = Rs. 75 per hour; overtime hours = 38 - 35 = 3; overtime pay = 3 x 75 = Rs. 225. Step 3: Total earnings = 1750 + 225 = Rs. 1975.

mcqs.q: Noman's basic hourly rate is Rs. 50 for a 35-hour week, and overtime is paid at time and a half. How much does he earn in a week in which he works 48 hours?
mcqs.why: Step 1: Basic weekly pay = 35 x 50 = Rs. 1750. Step 2: Overtime rate = 1.5 x 50 = Rs. 75 per hour; overtime hours = 48 - 35 = 13; overtime pay = 13 x 75 = Rs. 975. Step 3: Total earnings = 1750 + 975 = Rs. 2725.

mcqs.q: Abdullah worked 6 hours overtime in addition to his basic 36 hours in a week. His basic rate is Rs. 60 per hour and overtime is paid at time and a half. Taking a month as 4 weeks, what is his gross pay for the month?
mcqs.why: Step 1: Basic weekly pay = 36 x 60 = Rs. 2160. Step 2: Overtime rate = 1.5 x 60 = Rs. 90; overtime pay = 6 x 90 = Rs. 540. Step 3: Weekly gross = 2160 + 540 = Rs. 2700. Step 4: Monthly gross = 2700 x 4 = Rs. 10,800.

Review Exercise 5 — Question 3

Q. The price of a tricycle is Rs. 4000. If 16% sales tax is charged, then calculate the amount of sales tax on 30 such tricycles.

Step 1: Price of 30 tricycles = 30 x 4000 = Rs. 1,20,000

Step 2: Sales tax = 1,20,000 x 16/100 = Rs. 19,200

So the sales tax is Rs. 19,200.

Review Exercise 5 — Question 4

Q. If the total income of a person is Rs. 7,00,000 with exempted amount of Rs. 1,50,000. Find the tax chargeable @ 4.5%.

Formula: Tax = Taxable amount x Rate/100 ; Taxable income = Total income - Exempted amount

Step 1: Taxable income = 7,00,000 - 1,50,000 = Rs. 5,50,000

Step 2: Tax = 5,50,000 x 4.5/100 = Rs. 24,750

So the tax chargeable is Rs. 24,750.

Review Exercise 5 — Question 5

Q. The gas meter shows that 5.670 Hm^3 gas was used during a month period. Workout the payable amount inclusive of GST @ 16%.

Method: Slab 7 (above 5) rate = Rs. 730.17 per MMBTU ; 1 Hm^3 = 3.30 MMBTU ; Meter rent Rs. 120

Step 1: Gas charges = 5.670 x 3.30 x 730.17 = Rs. 13,662.21

Step 2: With rent = 13,662.21 + 120 = Rs. 13,782.21

Step 3: Total with GST = 13,782.21 x 1.16 = Rs. 15,987.37

Note: The book's answer key prints Rs. 15,867.37, which is Rs. 120 (the meter rent) less — the same key shortfall as in Exercise 5.2 Question 1 (vi).

Review Exercise 5 — Question 6: Complete the electricity bills, including the items as well as shown in the solved example of electricity bill

Q. The number of units consumed while using electricity are as under. (i) 275 units (ii) 200 units (iii) 340 units (iv) 285 units

Rates: first 100 @ 2.65 ; next 200 @ 3.64 ; next 700 @ 6.15. Items: excise duty 1.5%, electricity duty Rs. 62.52 (fixed, as in the solved example), PTV fee Rs. 25, income tax 1.6%

(i) 275 units: Cost = 265 + 175 x 3.64 = Rs. 902 ; Excise = 13.53 ; Duty = 62.52 ; PTV = 25 ; Income tax = 14.43 ; Total = Rs. 1017.48

(ii) 200 units: Cost = 265 + 100 x 3.64 = Rs. 629 ; Excise = 9.44 ; Duty = 62.52 ; PTV = 25 ; Income tax = 10.06 ; Total = Rs. 736.02

(iv) 285 units: Cost = 265 + 185 x 3.64 = Rs. 938.40 ; Excise = 14.08 ; Duty = 62.52 ; PTV = 25 ; Income tax = 15.01 ; Total = Rs. 1055

Review Exercise 5 — Question 7

Q. The gross monthly pay of a person is Rs. 75,000. If Rs. 1500, Rs. 1200 and Rs. 1800 are deducted as income tax, benevolent fund and G.P fund respectively, then calculate the net take home salary of the person.

Formula: Net salary = Gross pay - Total deductions

Step 1: Total deductions = 1500 + 1200 + 1800 = Rs. 4500

Step 2: Net salary = 75,000 - 4500 = Rs. 70,500

So the net take home salary is Rs. 70,500.

mcqs.q: Money that must be paid to the state, charged as a proportion of income and profit and added to the cost of some goods and services, is called a:
mcqs.why: By definition, money that must be paid to the state as a proportion of income and profits, and added to the cost of some goods and services, is called a tax.

mcqs.q: Taxes charged on income, property and profits, in the form of income tax, property tax and profit tax, are called:
mcqs.why: Taxes charged directly on income, property and profits are called direct taxes, because the person who pays them bears the burden himself.

mcqs.q: Taxes in the form of duties and motor vehicle taxes are called:
mcqs.why: Taxes in the form of duties and motor vehicle taxes are called indirect taxes, because their burden can be shifted to another person through prices.

mcqs.q: The tax charged in addition to the price of an article is called:
mcqs.why: The tax charged in addition to the price of an article at the time of sale is called sales tax.

mcqs.q: The form of tax which a buyer pays on a manufactured item at the time of purchase is called:
mcqs.why: The tax a buyer pays on a manufactured item at the time of purchase is called excise duty, which is charged on items manufactured in the country.

mcqs.q: The tax charged on the owner of land, a house, flats or a building is called:
mcqs.why: The tax charged on the owner of land, a house, flats or a building is called property tax.

mcqs.q: The tax charged on all the taxable income is called:
mcqs.why: The tax charged on all the taxable income of a person is called income tax. Formula: Tax = Taxable income x Rate/100.

mcqs.q: The price of a tricycle is Rs. 4000. If 16% sales tax is charged, what is the sales tax on 30 such tricycles?
mcqs.why: Step 1: Price of 30 tricycles = 30 x 4000 = Rs. 120,000. Step 2: Formula: Sales tax = Price x Rate/100 = 120,000 x 16/100 = Rs. 19,200.

mcqs.q: A gas meter shows that 5.670 Hm^3 gas was used in a month. This is slab 7 (above 5) at Rs. 730.17 per MMBTU. Including meter rent Rs. 120, what is the correct payable amount inclusive of GST at 16%?
mcqs.why: Step 1: Gas charges = 5.670 x 3.30 x 730.17 = Rs. 13,662.21. Step 2: Add meter rent: 13,662.21 + 120 = Rs. 13,782.21. Step 3: Add GST 16%: 13,782.21 x 1.16 = Rs. 15,987.37. The book key prints Rs. 15,867.37, which is Rs. 120 less, so the corrected total is Rs. 15,987.37.

mcqs.q: For 340 units of electricity: cost of units Rs. 1239, excise duty Rs. 18.59, electricity duty Rs. 62.52 (fixed), PTV fee Rs. 25 and income tax Rs. 19.82. What is the correct total bill?
mcqs.why: Total bill = Cost of units + Excise duty + Electricity duty + PTV fee + Income tax = 1239 + 18.59 + 62.52 + 25 + 19.82 = Rs. 1364.93. The book key prints Rs. 989.23, which is impossible because it is less than the cost of the units alone, Rs. 1239, so it is a key error.

lessons.title: Exercise 6.1 — Radicals and Radicands
lessons.notes_html:
Exercise 6.1 of Unit 6 — Exponents and Logarithms — complete solved exercises with every step shown.

Exercise 6.1 — Question 1: Determine the radicals and the radicands from the following

Q. (i) sqrt(3) (ii) 4 + 3 sqrt(a) (iii) sqrt(11) (iv) 8 - 2 sqrt(6) (v) sqrt(5)/7 (vi) 9/sqrt(13)

Definition: The expression with the root sign is called the radical and the quantity under the root sign is called the radicand.

(i) Radical: sqrt(3) ; Radicand: 3

(ii) Radical: sqrt(a) ; Radicand: a

(iii) Radical: sqrt(11) ; Radicand: 11

(iv) Radical: sqrt(6) ; Radicand: 6

(v) Radical: sqrt(5) ; Radicand: 5

(vi) Radical: sqrt(13) ; Radicand: 13

Exercise 6.1 — Question 2: Express the following in exponential form

Q. (i) sqrt(a^3) (ii) 5th root of (a^3) (iii) 1/(p-th root of (a^k)) (iv) 1/(b-th root of (a^k))

Formula: n-th root of (a^m) = a^(m/n) ; and 1/a^n = a^(-n)

(i) sqrt(a^3) = a^(3/2)

(ii) (a^3)^(1/5) = a^(3/5)

(iii) 1/(a^(k/p)) = a^(-k/p)

(iv) 1/(a^(k/b)) = a^(-k/b)

Exercise 6.1 — Question 3: Write in the radical form and evaluate the result

Q. (i) (25)^(1/2) (ii) (64)^(1/3) (iii) (81)^(1/4) (iv) (27)^(1/3) (v) (27)^(2/3) (vi) 8^(-1/3) (vii) (1000)^(2/3) (viii) (64)^(1/2)

Formula: a^(m/n) = n-th root of (a^m) ; take the power first, then the root.

(i) sqrt(25) = 5

(ii) (64)^(1/3) = 4 (because 4^3 = 64)

(iii) (81)^(1/4) = 3 (because 3^4 = 81)

(iv) (27)^(1/3) = 3

(v) (27)^(2/3) = ((27)^(1/3))^2 = 3^2 = 9

(vi) 8^(-1/3) = 1/(8^(1/3)) = 1/2

(vii) (1000)^(2/3) = (10)^2 = 100

(viii) sqrt(64) = 8

Exercise 6.1 — Question 4: Simplify and give answer in exponential form

Q. (i) sqrt(a^16) (ii) cube root of (a^15) (iii) cube root of (27 a^9) (iv) cube root of (8 a^9) (v) 4th root of (x^32) (vi) 4th root of (81 x^20) (vii) cube root of (125 x^9 y^15) (viii) sqrt((8+y)^7) (ix) 4th root of (16 x^2 y^6) (x) 4th root of (x^5 y^6 / z^2) (xi) cube root of (8x/(x+y)) (xii) p-th root of (y^n / a^m)

Formula: n-th root of (a^m) = a^(m/n) — divide the exponent of each factor by the order of the root.

(i) a^(16/2) = a^8

(ii) a^(15/3) = a^5

(iii) (27)^(1/3) x a^(9/3) = 3 a^3

(iv) (8)^(1/3) x a^3 = 2 a^3

(v) x^(32/4) = x^8

(vi) (81)^(1/4) x^(20/4) = 3 x^5

(vii) (125)^(1/3) x^3 y^5 = 5 x^3 y^5

(viii) (8+y)^(7/2)

(ix) (16)^(1/4) x^(2/4) y^(6/4) = 2 x^(1/2) y^(3/2)

(x) x^(5/4) y^(3/2) / z^(1/2)

(xi) 2 x^(1/3) / (x+y)^(1/3)

(xii) y^(n/p) / a^(m/p)

Exercise 6.1 — Question 5: Simplify

Q. (i) sqrt(3) x sqrt(7) (ii) 5th root of 4 x 5th root of 128 (iii) 5th root of 81 x 5th root of 27 (iv) sqrt(2) / 9th root of 32 (v) 5th root of 118 / 5th root of 2 (vi) sqrt(27)/sqrt(81) (vii) a^(1/4) x a^(2/3) (viii) x^(6/7) x y^(1/4) (ix) (x^(3/4) y^(1/6))^6 (x) (x^3 y^2)^(1/2) x (y^3 x^4)^(-1/3) (xi) (x^3 y^2)^(1/4) x (x^(1/3) y)^(3/4) (xii) (a^(1/4) b^(1/3))^(-1/2) / (a^(1/3) b^(1/4))^(-5) (xiii) (x^2 y^3)^(1/5) x (x^(1/3) y^2)^(1/4)

Laws: a^m x a^n = a^(m+n) ; a^m / a^n = a^(m-n) ; (a^m)^n = a^(mn) ; a^(-n) = 1/a^n ; n-th root of (a^m) = a^(m/n)

(i) sqrt(3x7) = sqrt(21)

(ii) (4x128)^(1/5) = (512)^(1/5), i.e. the 5th root of 512

(iii) (81x27)^(1/5) = (2187)^(1/5)

(iv) 2^(1/2) / 2^(5/9) = 2^(-1/18) = 1/(2^(1/18))

(v) (118/2)^(1/5) = (59)^(1/5)

(vi) sqrt(27/81) = sqrt(1/3)

(vii) a^(1/4 + 2/3) = a^(11/12)

(viii) x^(6/7) y^(1/4) (different bases cannot be combined; this is the book key's 4th root form of (x^(24/7) y))

(ix) x^(9/2) y = y sqrt(x^9)

(x) x^(3/2) y x x^(-4/3) y^(-1) = x^(1/6)

(xi) x^(3/4) y^(1/2) x x^(1/4) y^(3/4) = x y^(5/4)

(xii) a^(-1/8) b^(-1/6) / (a^(-5/3) b^(-5/4)) = a^(-1/8 + 5/3) b^(-1/6 + 5/4) = a^(37/24) b^(13/12) (this agrees with the book's answer key, which prints it as the 24th root of (a^37 b^26))

(xiii) x^(2/5) y^(3/5) x x^(1/12) y^(1/2) = x^(29/60) y^(11/10)

mcqs.q: In sqrt(11), the radicand is:
mcqs.why: The quantity written under the root sign is called the radicand. In sqrt(11), the quantity under the sign is 11, so the radicand is 11, while sqrt(11) itself is the radical.

mcqs.q: In the expression 8 - 2 sqrt(6), the radical part is:
mcqs.why: The expression containing the root sign is the radical. In 8 - 2 sqrt(6), the part with the root sign is sqrt(6), and the quantity 6 under the sign is its radicand.

mcqs.q: Express sqrt(a^3) in exponential form.
mcqs.why: Formula: n-th root of (a^m) = a^(m/n). Here sqrt(a^3) is the 2nd root of a^3, so sqrt(a^3) = a^(3/2).

mcqs.q: Express the 5th root of (a^3) in exponential form.
mcqs.why: Formula: n-th root of (a^m) = a^(m/n). The 5th root of (a^3) = (a^3)^(1/5) = a^(3/5), because the exponent 3 is divided by the order of the root, 5.

mcqs.q: Evaluate (27)^(2/3).
mcqs.why: Formula: a^(m/n) = n-th root of (a^m). Step 1: Cube root of 27 = 3, because 3^3 = 27. Step 2: (27)^(2/3) = 3^2 = 9.

mcqs.q: Evaluate 8^(-1/3).

mcqs.why: Formula: a^(m/n) = n-th root of (a^m). Step 1: Cube root of 1000 = 10, because 10^3 = 1000. Step 2: (1000)^(2/3) = 10^2 = 100.

mcqs.q: Simplify the cube root of (125 x^9 y^15) and give the answer in exponential form.
mcqs.why: Formula: n-th root of (a^m) = a^(m/n), dividing each exponent by 3. Cube root of 125 = 5, x^(9/3) = x^3 and y^(15/3) = y^5, so the result is 5 x^3 y^5.

mcqs.q: Simplify sqrt(3) x sqrt(7).
mcqs.why: Radicals with the same order multiply under one sign: sqrt(3) x sqrt(7) = sqrt(3 x 7) = sqrt(21).

Step 1: Numerator = a^(-1/8) b^(-1/6). Denominator = a^(-5/3) b^(-5/4). Step 2: On division subtract exponents: for a, -1/8 - (-5/3) = -3/24 + 40/24 = 37/24; for b, -1/6 - (-5/4) = -2/12 + 15/12 = 13/12. Result: a^(37/24) b^(13/12), which is the 24th root of (a^37 b^26).

mcqs.q: In the expression (4y)^3, the base is:
mcqs.why: The whole quantity that is raised to the power is the base. In (4y)^3, the quantity 4y is raised to the power 3, so the base is 4y and the exponent is 3.

mcqs.q: Simplify 5x^(3/2) x x^(1/2) and state the result.
mcqs.why: Law: a^m x a^n = a^(m+n). Add the exponents of x: 3/2 + 1/2 = 4/2 = 2. So 5x^(3/2) x x^(1/2) = 5x^2.

mcqs.q: Simplify sqrt((a^2 b^3)^6).
mcqs.why: Step 1: sqrt means power 1/2, so sqrt((a^2 b^3)^6) = (a^2 b^3)^(6 x 1/2) = (a^2 b^3)^3. Step 2: Law (a^m)^n = a^(mn): a^(2x3) b^(3x3) = a^6 b^9.

mcqs.q: Evaluate (3^2)^5 divided by (9^3 x 27^(-1)).
Simplify x^(3/4) x x^(2/5).
mcqs.why: Law: a^m x a^n = a^(m+n). Add the exponents with common denominator 20: 3/4 + 2/5 = 15/20 + 8/20 = 23/20. So the result is x^(23/20).

mcqs.q: Simplify 3^(1/2) divided by 3^(1/3).
mcqs.why: Law: a^m / a^n = a^(m-n). Subtract the exponents with common denominator 6: 1/2 - 1/3 = 3/6 - 2/6 = 1/6. So the result is 3^(1/6).

mcqs.q: Simplify (a^5 b^4 c^2) divided by (abc).
mcqs.why: Law: a^m / a^n = a^(m-n), applied to each base. a: 5 - 1 = 4; b: 4 - 1 = 3; c: 2 - 1 = 1. Result: a^4 b^3 c.

mcqs.q: Simplify (a^(-5))^3 x (ab)^15 divided by (a^(-1) b^2).
mcqs.why: Step 1: (a^(-5))^3 = a^(-15) and (ab)^15 = a^15 b^15. Step 2: For a: -15 + 15 - (-1) = 1, giving a^1. Step 3: For b: 15 - 2 = 13. Result: a b^13, with positive indices.

lessons.title: Exercise 6.3 — Scientific Notation
lessons.notes_html:
Exercise 6.3 of Unit 6 — Exponents and Logarithms — complete solved exercises with every step shown.

Exercise 6.3 — Questions 1 to 5: Write the following in scientific notation

Q. 1- 0.051 2- 89.99 3- 0.424 4- 2566324 5- 0.00000075

Rule: Write the number in the form b x 10^n where 1 <= b < 10 ; if the decimal point moves to the left n is negative, if to the right n is positive.

1- 0.051 = 5.1 x 10^(-2)

2- 89.99 = 8.999 x 10^1

3- 0.424 = 4.24 x 10^(-1)

4- 2566324 = 2.566324 x 10^6

5- 0.00000075 = 7.5 x 10^(-7)

Exercise 6.3 — Questions 6 to 10: Write the following in decimal form

Q. 6- 0.86 x 10^4 7- 1.345 x 10^(-5) 8- 5.1 x 10^(-9) 9- 0.525 x 10^(-7) 10- 636.5 x 10^(-6)

Rule: For a positive power of 10 move the decimal point to the right, for a negative power to the left.

6- 0.86 x 10^4 = 8600

7- 1.345 x 10^(-5) = 0.00001345

8- 5.1 x 10^(-9) = 0.0000000051

9- 0.525 x 10^(-7) = 0.0000000525

10- 636.5 x 10^(-6) = 0.0006365

Exercise 6.3 — Questions 11 to 13: Simplify and write the answer in scientific notation

Q. 11- (0.96 x 10^7)/(2 x 10^4) 12- (2.61 x 4 x 10^8)/10^3 13- (521 x 10^3 x 12)/(2 x 10^2)

11- (0.96/2) x 10^(7-4) = 0.48 x 10^3 = 4.8 x 10^2

12- (2.61 x 4) x 10^(8-3) = 10.44 x 10^5 = 1.044 x 10^6

13- (521 x 12/2) x 10^(3-2) = 3126 x 10^1 = 3.126 x 10^4

Exercise 6.3 — Question 14

Q. Convert 4.5 x 10^5 cm into metres and write the solution in decimal form.

Step 1: 1 m = 100 cm, so divide the centimetres by 100: 4.5 x 10^5 / 10^2 = 4.5 x 10^3 m

Step 2: In decimal form: 4.5 x 10^3 m = 4500 m

Exercise 6.3 — Question 15

Q. The radius of the earth is 6400 km. Convert it into metres and write the solution in scientific notation.

Step 1: 1 km = 1000 m ; 6400 km = 6400 x 10^3 m = 6.4 x 10^3 x 10^3 m

Step 2: = 6.4 x 10^6 m

mcqs.q: Write 0.051 in scientific notation.
mcqs.why: Rule: Write the number as b x 10^n with b at least 1 and less than 10. Moving the decimal point 2 places to the right gives 5.1, and the point moved right so n is negative: 0.051 = 5.1 x 10^(-2).

mcqs.q: Write 89.99 in scientific notation.
mcqs.why: Rule: Write the number as b x 10^n with b at least 1 and less than 10. Moving the decimal point 1 place to the left gives 8.999, and the point moved left so n is positive: 89.99 = 8.999 x 10^1.

mcqs.q: Write 2566324 in scientific notation.
mcqs.why: Rule: Write the number as b x 10^n with b at least 1 and less than 10. Moving the decimal point 6 places to the left gives 2.566324, so 2566324 = 2.566324 x 10^6.

mcqs.q: Write 0.00000075 in scientific notation.
mcqs.why: Rule: Write the number as b x 10^n with b at least 1 and less than 10. Moving the decimal point 7 places to the right gives 7.5, and the point moved right so n is negative: 0.00000075 = 7.5 x 10^(-7).

mcqs.q: Write 0.86 x 10^4 in decimal form.
mcqs.why: For a positive power of 10, move the decimal point to the right by that many places: 0.86 x 10^4 = 0.86 x 10000 = 8600.

mcqs.q: Write 1.345 x 10^(-5) in decimal form.
mcqs.why: For a negative power of 10, move the decimal point to the left by that many places: 1.345 x 10^(-5) = 0.00001345.

mcqs.q: Write 5.1 x 10^(-9) in decimal form.
mcqs.why: For a negative power of 10, move the decimal point to the left by 9 places: 5.1 x 10^(-9) = 0.0000000051, with eight zeros between the decimal point and the 5.

mcqs.q: Simplify (0.96 x 10^7) divided by (2 x 10^4) and write the answer in scientific notation.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Divide the numbers and subtract the powers: (0.96/2) x 10^(7-4) = 0.48 x 10^3. Step 2: Adjust so the first factor is at least 1 and less than 10: 0.48 x 10^3 = 4.8 x 10^2.

mcqs.q: Convert 4.5 x 10^5 cm into metres and write the answer in decimal form.
mcqs.why: Step 1: 1 m = 100 cm = 10^2 cm, so divide by 10^2: 4.5 x 10^5 / 10^2 = 4.5 x 10^3 m. Step 2: In decimal form, 4.5 x 10^3 m = 4500 m.

mcqs.q: The radius of the earth is 6400 km. Convert it into metres and write the answer in scientific notation.

lessons.title: Exercise 6.4 — Logarithms — Characteristic and Mantissa
lessons.notes_html:
Exercise 6.4 of Unit 6 — Exponents and Logarithms — complete solved exercises with every step shown.

Exercise 6.4 — Question 1: Write the characteristic of the logarithm of the following numbers

Q. (i) 6350 (ii) 2035.6 (iii) 2.057 (iv) 0.8657 (v) 0.0732 (vi) 0.000721

Rule: If the number is >= 1, characteristic = (number of digits before the decimal point) - 1 ; if the number is < 1, the characteristic is negative = -(number of zeros immediately after the decimal point + 1), written with a bar.

(i) 6350: digits 4, characteristic = 3

(ii) 2035.6: digits 4, characteristic = 3

(iii) 2.057: digit 1, characteristic = 0

(iv) 0.8657: characteristic = -1 (bar 1)

(v) 0.0732: characteristic = -2 (bar 2)

(vi) 0.000721: characteristic = -4 (bar 4)

Exercise 6.4 — Question 2: Write the values of the following (from the logarithm table)

Q. (i) log 52.13 (ii) log 6.304 (iii) log 0.6127 (iv) log 0.0057 (v) log 0.00003

Method: log = characteristic + mantissa ; the mantissa is taken from the table for the first four significant digits and is always positive.

(i) log 52.13 = 1.7170

(ii) log 6.304 = 0.7996

(iii) log 0.6127 = (bar 1).7873 (characteristic bar 1, mantissa .7873)

(iv) log 0.0057 = (bar 3).7559

(v) log 0.00003 = (bar 5).4771

Exercise 6.4 — Question 3

Q. If log 6374 = 3.8044, then write the values of the following: (i) log 6.374 (ii) log 0.6374 (iii) log 0.00637

Principle: Changing the position of the decimal point changes only the characteristic; the mantissa (.8044) stays the same.

(i) log 6.374 = 0.8044

(ii) log 0.6374 = (bar 1).8044

(iii) log 0.00637 = (bar 3).8044 (for 0.006374)

Exercise 6.4 — Question 4: Find x

Q. (i) log x = (bar 2).0374 (ii) log x = 0.1597 (iii) log x = 4.4236

Method: x = antilog (given value) ; take the digits for the mantissa from the antilog table and place the decimal point according to the characteristic.

(i) Digits for mantissa .0374 are 1090, characteristic bar 2, so x = 0.01090

(ii) Digits for mantissa .1597 are 1444, characteristic 0, so x = 1.444

(iii) Digits for mantissa .4236 are 2653, characteristic 4, so x = 26530

mcqs.q: What is the characteristic of log 6350?
mcqs.why: Rule: For a number of at least 1, characteristic = (number of digits before the decimal point) minus 1. The number 6350 has 4 digits before the decimal point, so the characteristic = 4 - 1 = 3.

mcqs.q: What is the characteristic of log 2.057?
mcqs.why: Rule: For a number of at least 1, characteristic = (number of digits before the decimal point) minus 1. The number 2.057 has 1 digit before the decimal point, so the characteristic = 1 - 1 = 0.

mcqs.q: What is the characteristic of log 0.0732?
mcqs.why: Rule: For a number less than 1, the characteristic is negative and equals minus (number of zeros immediately after the decimal point plus 1). In 0.0732 there is 1 zero immediately after the decimal point, so the characteristic is bar 2, that is, -2.

mcqs.q: What is the characteristic of log 0.000721?
mcqs.why: Rule: For a number less than 1, the characteristic is negative and equals minus (number of zeros immediately after the decimal point plus 1). In 0.000721 there are 3 zeros immediately after the decimal point, so the characteristic is bar 4, that is, -4.

mcqs.q: Using the logarithm table, log 52.13 is equal to:
mcqs.why: Method: log = characteristic + mantissa. The number 52.13 has 2 digits before the decimal point, so the characteristic is 1. The mantissa for 5213 from the table is .7170, so log 52.13 = 1.7170.

mcqs.q: Using the logarithm table, log 6.304 is equal to:
mcqs.why: Method: log = characteristic + mantissa. The number 6.304 has 1 digit before the decimal point, so the characteristic is 0. The mantissa for 6304 from the table is .7996, so log 6.304 = 0.7996.

mcqs.q: Using the logarithm table, log 0.6127 is equal to:
mcqs.why: Method: log = characteristic + mantissa, and the mantissa is always positive. The number 0.6127 is less than 1 with no zero immediately after the decimal point, so the characteristic is bar 1. The mantissa for 6127 is .7873, so log 0.6127 = (bar 1).7873.

mcqs.q: If log 6374 = 3.8044, then log 6.374 is equal to:
mcqs.why: Principle: Changing the position of the decimal point changes only the characteristic; the mantissa .8044 stays the same. The number 6.374 has 1 digit before the decimal point, so its characteristic is 0, giving log 6.374 = 0.8044.

mcqs.q: If log 6374 = 3.8044, then log 0.00637 is equal to:
mcqs.why: Principle: Changing the position of the decimal point changes only the characteristic; the mantissa .8044 stays the same. The number 0.00637 has 2 zeros immediately after the decimal point, so its characteristic is bar 3, giving log 0.00637 = (bar 3).8044.

mcqs.q: If log x = 0.1597, find x using the antilog table.
mcqs.why: Method: x = antilog of the given value. The digits for the mantissa .1597 from the antilog table are 1444, and the characteristic 0 means 1 digit before the decimal point, so x = 1.444.

lessons.title: Exercise 6.5 — Laws of Logarithms and Their Applications
lessons.notes_html:
Exercise 6.5 of Unit 6 — Exponents and Logarithms — complete solved exercises with every step shown.

Exercise 6.5 — Question 1: Solve

Q. (i) log 81 / log 9 (ii) log 36 / log 6 (iii) log 243 / log 9

Formula: log (a^n) = n log a

(i) log 81 = log 3^4 = 4 log 3 ; log 9 = 2 log 3 ; ratio = 4/2 = 2

(ii) log 36 = 2 log 6 ; ratio = 2

(iii) log 243 = 5 log 3 ; log 9 = 2 log 3 ; ratio = 5/2

Exercise 6.5 — Question 2: Find the value (Hint: in each part write log 5 = log (10/2) = 1 - log 2; Laws: log (mn) = log m + log n, log (m/n) = log m - log n)

Q. (i) log 5 + log 4 + log 3 - log 6 (ii) log 5 + log 20 + log 24 + log 25 - log 60 (iii) 2 log 3 + 3 log 4 + 4 log 5 - 2 log 6 (iv) 2 log 5 + log 8 - (1/2) log 4 (v) log 200 + log 5

(i) = log ((5x4x3)/6) = log 10 = 1

(ii) = log ((5x20x24x25)/60) = log 1000 = 3

(iii) = log ((3^2 x 4^3 x 5^4)/6^2) = log ((9x64x625)/36) = log 10000 = 4

(iv) = log ((25 x 8)/4^(1/2)) = log (200/2) = log 100 = 2

(v) = log (200x5) = log 1000 = 3

Exercise 6.5 — Question 3: Simplify without using the logarithm table

Q. (i) log 1.3472 + log 22.79 - log 5 (ii) log 22.13 + log 0.354 + log 7 - log 3 (iii) log 57.86 + log 4.385 - log 2.391 - log 3.072

Laws: Sums of logs become the log of the product, differences become the log of the quotient.

(i) = log ((1.3472 x 22.79)/5)

(ii) = log ((22.13 x 0.354 x 7)/3)

(iii) = log ((57.86 x 4.385)/(2.391 x 3.072))

Exercise 6.5 — Question 4: Solve with the help of the logarithm table

Q. (i) (2.38 x 3.901)/4.83 (ii) (8.67 x 3.94)/1.78 (iii) (25.36 x 3.4569)/(9.87 x 8.93)

Method: Take the log of each number from the table ; add the logs of the products, subtract the logs of the divisors ; take the antilog at the end.

(i) log = log 2.38 + log 3.901 - log 4.83 ; by antilog the value = 1.923

(ii) By the same method = 19.19

(iii) By the same method = 0.9945

Exercise 6.5 — Question 5: Prove that

Q. (i) log (a^2/(bc)) + log (b^2/(ca)) + log (c^2/(ab)) = 0 (ii) 3 log 2 + 2 log 3 + log 5 = log 360 (iii) 5 log 3 - log 9 = log 27 (iv) log (75/16) + log (32/243) - 2 log (5/9) = log 2 (v) 2 log (11/13) + log (130/77) - log (55/91) = log 2

(i) LHS = log ((a^2 b^2 c^2)/(bc x ca x ab)) = log ((a^2 b^2 c^2)/(a^2 b^2 c^2)) = log 1 = 0

(ii) LHS = log (2^3 x 3^2 x 5) = log (8x9x5) = log 360

(iii) LHS = log (3^5/9) = log (243/9) = log 27

(iv) LHS = log ((75x32)/(16x243)) - log (25/81) = log (50/81) - log (25/81) = log ((50/81)/(25/81)) = log 2

(v) LHS = log ((121/169) x (130/77)) - log (55/91) = log (110/91) - log (55/91) = log 2

Exercise 6.5 — Question 6: Show that

Q. 3 log 4 + 2 log 5 - (1/3) log 64 - (1/2) log 16 = 2

Step 1: = log (4^3) + log (5^2) - log (64^(1/3)) - log (16^(1/2)) = log 64 + log 25 - log 4 - log 4

Step 2: = log ((64 x 25)/(4 x 4)) = log (1600/16) = log 100 = 2, proved.

Exercise 6.5 — Question 7: Show that

Q. log (1 x 2 x 3) = log 1 + log 2 + log 3

Step 1: RHS = log 1 + (log 2 + log 3) = 0 + log (2x3) (Law: log m + log n = log (mn))

Step 2: = log 6 ; and LHS = log (6) = log 6, so both sides are equal, proved.

Exercise 6.5 — Question 8: Using the logarithm table, find the value of the following

Q. (i) 69.13 x 0.34 x 0.014 (ii) (8.67 x 3.94)/1.78 (iii) (4/3) x 3.142 x (1.5)^3 (iv) ((25.36)^2 x 0.4569)/847.5 (v) (0.9876 x (16.42)^2)/(4.567)^(1/3) (vi) sqrt((cube root of 0.0125 x sqrt(31.15))/0.00081) (vii) ((6.45)^3 x (0.00034)^(1/3) x 981.9)/((9.37)^2 x (8.93)^(1/4) x 0.0617) (viii) ((0.0437)^(2/3) x (1.407)^2)/((0.0015)^(1/3) x (1.235)^(1/7))

Method (for each part): Take the logs of all the factors ; add for multiplication, subtract for division, multiply for powers, divide for roots ; take the antilog at the end.

(i) = 0.3291

(ii) = 19.19

(iii) = 14.139

(iv) = 0.3466

(v) = 160.4

(vi) = 48.01

(vii) = 1964

(viii) = 2.082

Exercise 6.5 — Question 9

Q. If v = sqrt((g l)/(2 pi)), then find v, when l = 150, g = 32.16, pi = 3.142.

Step 1: Put the values: v = sqrt((32.16 x 150)/(2 x 3.142)) = sqrt(4824/6.284)

Step 2: = sqrt(767.66)

Step 3: By the log method sqrt(767.66) = 27.71

So v = 27.71

Exercise 6.5 — Question 10

Q. If H = (I^2 R t)/4.2, then find H, when I = 1.3, R = 6.7 and t = 25.

Step 1: I^2 = 1.3^2 = 1.69

Step 2: Numerator = 1.69 x 6.7 x 25 = 283.075

Step 3: H = 283.075/4.2 = 67.39

So H = 67.39

Exercise 6.5 — Question 11

Q. Find h, if h = v/(pi (R^2 - r^2)), when v = 1190, R = 83.6, r = 62.4 and pi = 3.14.

Step 1: R^2 - r^2 = 83.6^2 - 62.4^2 = 6988.96 - 3893.76 = 3095.20

Step 2: Denominator = 3.14 x 3095.20 = 9718.93

Step 3: h = 1190/9718.93 = 0.1224

So h = 0.1224

mcqs.q: Evaluate log 81 divided by log 9.
mcqs.why: Formula: log (a^n) = n log a. Step 1: log 81 = log 3^4 = 4 log 3, and log 9 = log 3^2 = 2 log 3. Step 2: Ratio = (4 log 3)/(2 log 3) = 4/2 = 2.

mcqs.q: Evaluate log 243 divided by log 9.
mcqs.why: Formula: log (a^n) = n log a. Step 1: log 243 = log 3^5 = 5 log 3, and log 9 = log 3^2 = 2 log 3. Step 2: Ratio = (5 log 3)/(2 log 3) = 5/2.

mcqs.q: Evaluate log 5 + log 4 + log 3 - log 6.
mcqs.why: Laws: log m + log n = log (mn) and log m - log n = log (m/n). Step 1: Combine into one log: log ((5 x 4 x 3)/6) = log (60/6) = log 10. Step 2: log 10 = 1, because the base is 10.

mcqs.q: Evaluate log 200 + log 5.
mcqs.why: Law: log m + log n = log (mn). Step 1: log 200 + log 5 = log (200 x 5) = log 1000. Step 2: 1000 = 10^3, so log 1000 = 3.

mcqs.q: Given log 2 = 0.3010, find the value of log 5 without using the table.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Write 5 = 10/2, so log 5 = log (10/2). Step 2: Law: log (m/n) = log m - log n, so log 5 = log 10 - log 2 = 1 - 0.3010 = 0.6990.

mcqs.q: Evaluate 2 log 5 + log 8 - (1/2) log 4.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Use log (a^n) = n log a in reverse: 2 log 5 = log 25 and (1/2) log 4 = log 2. Step 2: Combine: log ((25 x 8)/2) = log (200/2) = log 100. Step 3: log 100 = 2.

mcqs.q: Simplify 5 log 3 - log 9 as a single logarithm.
mcqs.why: Step 1: 5 log 3 = log (3^5) = log 243, by the law log (a^n) = n log a. Step 2: Law: log m - log n = log (m/n), so log 243 - log 9 = log (243/9) = log 27.

mcqs.q: Using the logarithm table, the value of (2.38 x 3.901) divided by 4.83 is:
mcqs.why: Method: Take logs, add the logs of the numbers being multiplied and subtract the log of the divisor: log of the answer = log 2.38 + log 3.901 - log 4.83. Taking the antilog of the result gives 1.923.

mcqs.q: If h = v divided by (pi (R^2 - r^2)), find h when v = 1190, R = 83.6, r = 62.4 and pi = 3.14.
Evaluate 3 log 4 + 2 log 5 - (1/3) log 64 - (1/2) log 16.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Use log (a^n) = n log a: 3 log 4 = log 64, 2 log 5 = log 25, (1/3) log 64 = log 4 and (1/2) log 16 = log 4. Step 2: Combine: log ((64 x 25)/(4 x 4)) = log (1600/16) = log 100. Step 3: log 100 = 2.

Review Exercise 6 — Question 3: Simplify

Q. (i) (x^5 y^3)^(1/2) x (y^7 x^3)^(-1/3) (ii) (a^(1/4) b^(1/3))^(-1/2) / (a^(1/3) b^(1/4))^(-3)

(i) = x^(5/2) y^(3/2) x x^(-1) y^(-7/3) = x^(5/2 - 1) y^(3/2 - 7/3) = x^(3/2) y^(-5/6)

(ii) = a^(-1/8) b^(-1/6) / (a^(-1) b^(-3/4)) = a^(-1/8 + 1) b^(-1/6 + 3/4) = a^(7/8) b^(7/12)

Q. log ((3 x 4 x 5)/7) = log 3 + log 4 + log 5 - log 7

Step 2: By the product law: log (3x4x5) = log 3 + log 4 + log 5

Step 3: So LHS = log 3 + log 4 + log 5 - log 7 = RHS, proved.

mcqs.q: sqrt(3) is:
mcqs.why: sqrt(3) cannot be written as a fraction of two integers and its decimal form neither ends nor repeats, so sqrt(3) is an irrational number.

mcqs.q: The cube root of 7 is called a:
mcqs.why: An expression containing a root sign, such as the cube root of 7, is called a radical. The number under the root sign, 7, is the radicand.

mcqs.q: In sqrt(3), 3 is called the:
mcqs.why: The quantity written under the root sign is called the radicand. In sqrt(3), the quantity under the sign is 3, so 3 is the radicand, while sqrt(3) itself is the radical.

mcqs.q: In a^n, n is called the:
mcqs.why: In a^n, the number written above, showing how many times the base is multiplied, is called the exponent. So n is the exponent and a is the base.

mcqs.q: The logarithm calculated to base 10 is called the:
mcqs.why: The logarithm calculated to base 10 is called the common logarithm. It is written simply as log, without showing the base.

mcqs.q: The integral part in the logarithm of a number is called the:
mcqs.why: The logarithm of a number has two parts: the integral part is called the characteristic, and the decimal part is called the mantissa.

mcqs.q: The decimal part in the logarithm of a number is called the:
mcqs.why: The logarithm of a number has two parts: the integral part is the characteristic, and the decimal part, which is always positive, is called the mantissa.

mcqs.q: sqrt(sqrt(2)) is equal to:
mcqs.why: Step 1: sqrt(2) = 2^(1/2). Step 2: Taking the square root again halves the exponent: (2^(1/2))^(1/2) = 2^(1/2 x 1/2) = 2^(1/4).

mcqs.q: The root symbol (the n-th root sign) itself is called the:
mcqs.why: The root symbol itself is called the radical sign. Note: the book answer key prints radicand for this blank, which is a key error; the radicand is the quantity written under the sign, not the sign itself.

Step 1: Numerator = a^(-1/8) b^(-1/6). Denominator = a^(-1) b^(-3/4). Step 2: On division subtract exponents: for a, -1/8 - (-1) = 7/8; for b, -1/6 - (-3/4) = -2/12 + 9/12 = 7/12. Result: a^(7/8) b^(7/12).

Exercise 7.1 — Question 1: Write the first three terms of the following

Q. (i) a_n = n + 3 (ii) a_n = (-1)^n n^3 (iii) a_n = 3n + 5 (iv) a_n = (n+1)/(2n+5) (v) a_n = 1/(2n-1)^2 (vi) a_n = n + 3 (as printed in the book) (vii) a_n = 1/3^n (viii) a_n = 3n - 5 (ix) a_n = (n+1) a_(n-1), a_1 = 1

Exercise 7.2 — Question 2: Find the missing element using the formula of A.P a_n = a + (n-1)d

Q. (i) a = 2, a_n = 402, n = 26 (ii) a_n = 81, d = -3, n = 18 (iii) a = 5, a_n = 61, n = 15 (iv) a = 16, a_n = 0, d = -1/4 (v) a = 10, a_n = 400, d = 5 (vi) a_n = 261, d = 4, n = 18

Exercise 7.2 — Question 3

Q. Find the 15th term of an A.P where the 3rd term is 8 and the common difference is 1/3.

Formula (A.P): a_n = a + (n-1)d, where a = first term, d = common difference

Step 1: a_3 = a + 2d = 8, so a = 8 - 2/3 = 22/3

Step 2: a_15 = a + 14d = 22/3 + 14/3 = 36/3 = 12

So the 15th term is 12.

Exercise 7.2 — Question 4

Q. Which term of an A.P 6, 2, -2, ... is -146?

Formula (A.P): a_n = a + (n-1)d, where a = first term, d = common difference

Step 1: a = 6, d = 2 - 6 = -4

Step 2: -146 = 6 + (n-1)(-4), so -152 = -4(n-1), n - 1 = 38, n = 39

So -146 is the 39th term of this A.P.

So -118 is the 42nd term of this A.P.

Step 1: 68 = 11 + (n-1)x3

Step 2: 57 = 3(n-1), so n - 1 = 19, n = 20

So the number of terms is 20.

Step 2: a_11 = (2 - x) + 10(1 - x) = 2 - x + 10 - 10x = 12 - 11x

lessons.title: Exercise 7.3 — Arithmetic Mean (A.M.)
lessons.notes_html:
Exercise 7.3 of Unit 7 — Arithmetic and Geometric Sequences — complete solved exercises with every step shown.

Exercise 7.3 — Question 1: Find A.M between the following

Q. (i) -3, 7 (ii) x - 1, x + 7 (iii) sqrt(7), 3 sqrt(7) (iv) x^2 + x + 1 ; x^2 - x + 1

Formula: A.M between two numbers a and b = (a + b)/2 ; for n means, d = (b - a)/(n + 1)

(i) (-3 + 7)/2 = 2

(ii) ((x-1) + (x+7))/2 = (2x + 6)/2 = x + 3

(iii) (sqrt(7) + 3 sqrt(7))/2 = 4 sqrt(7)/2 = 2 sqrt(7)

(iv) ((x^2+x+1) + (x^2-x+1))/2 = (2x^2 + 2)/2 = x^2 + 1

Exercise 7.3 — Question 2

Q. If 3 and 6 are two A.Ms between a and b, then find a and b.

Step 1: a, 3, 6, b is an A.P ; d = 6 - 3 = 3

Step 2: a = 3 - d = 0 ; b = 6 + d = 9

So a = 0 and b = 9.

Exercise 7.3 — Question 3

Q. Find three A.Ms between 11 and 19.

Formula: A.M between two numbers a and b = (a + b)/2 ; for n means, d = (b - a)/(n + 1)

Step 1: d = (19 - 11)/(3 + 1) = 8/4 = 2

Step 2: The means = 11 + 2, 13 + 2, 15 + 2 = 13, 15, 17

Exercise 7.3 — Question 4

Q. Find three A.Ms between sqrt(2) and 6 sqrt(2).

Formula: A.M between two numbers a and b = (a + b)/2 ; for n means, d = (b - a)/(n + 1)

Step 1: d = (6 sqrt(2) - sqrt(2))/4 = 5 sqrt(2)/4

Step 2: The means = sqrt(2) + 5 sqrt(2)/4 = 9 sqrt(2)/4 ; then 7 sqrt(2)/2 ; then 19 sqrt(2)/4

Exercise 7.3 — Question 5

Q. Find six A.Ms between 5 and 8.

Formula: A.M between two numbers a and b = (a + b)/2 ; for n means, d = (b - a)/(n + 1)

Exercise 7.3 — Question 6

Step 1: a, 5, 9, 13, b is an A.P ; d = 9 - 5 = 4

Step 2: a = 5 - 4 = 1 ; b = 13 + 4 = 17

So a = 1 and b = 17.

Exercise 7.4 of Unit 7 — Arithmetic and Geometric Sequences — complete solved exercises with every step shown.

Exercise 7.4 — Question 1

Q. Find the 7th term of G.P 2, 8, 32, ...

Formula (G.P): a_n = a r^(n-1), where a = first term, r = common ratio

Step 1: a = 2, r = 8/2 = 4

Step 2: a_7 = 2 x 4^6 = 2 x 4096 = 8192

Exercise 7.4 — Question 2

Q. Find the 11th term of G.P 2, 6, 18, ...

Formula (G.P): a_n = a r^(n-1), where a = first term, r = common ratio

Step 1: a = 2, r = 3

Step 2: a_11 = 2 x 3^10 = 2 x 59049 = 118098

Exercise 7.4 — Question 3

Q. Find the 6th term of G.P -3/2, 3, -6, ...

Formula (G.P): a_n = a r^(n-1), where a = first term, r = common ratio

Step 1: a = -3/2, r = 3/(-3/2) = -2

Step 2: a_6 = (-3/2) x (-2)^5 = (-3/2) x (-32) = 48

Exercise 7.4 — Question 4

Q. Find the 5th term of G.P 4, -12, 36, ...

Formula (G.P): a_n = a r^(n-1), where a = first term, r = common ratio

Step 1: a = 4, r = -3

Step 2: a_5 = 4 x (-3)^4 = 4 x 81 = 324

Exercise 7.4 — Question 5: Find the missing elements of the G.P

Q. (i) r = 10, a_n = 100, a = 1 (ii) a_n = 400, r = 2, a = 25 (iii) a = 128, r = 1/2, a_n = 1/4

Formula (G.P): a_n = a r^(n-1), where a = first term, r = common ratio

(i) 100 = 1 x 10^(n-1), so n - 1 = 2, n = 3

(ii) 400 = 25 x 2^(n-1), so 2^(n-1) = 16, n - 1 = 4, n = 5

(iii) 1/4 = 128 x (1/2)^(n-1), so (1/2)^(n-1) = 1/512 = (1/2)^9, n = 10

Exercise 7.4 — Question 6

Q. Find the 11th term of a G.P whose 5th term is 9 and common ratio is 2.

Step 1: a_11 = a_5 x r^(11-5) = 9 x 2^6

Step 2: = 9 x 64 = 576

Exercise 7.4 — Question 7

Q. Find the 13th term of a G.P whose 7th term is 25 and common ratio is 3.

Step 1: a_13 = a_7 x r^(13-7) = 25 x 3^6

Step 2: = 25 x 729 = 18225

Exercise 7.4 — Question 8

Q. If a, b, c, d are in G.P, then show that a - b, b - c, c - d are also in G.P.

Step 1: Let the common ratio be r ; then b = ar, c = ar^2, d = ar^3

Step 2: a - b = a(1 - r) ; b - c = ar(1 - r) ; c - d = ar^2 (1 - r)

Step 3: (b - c)/(a - b) = r and (c - d)/(b - c) = r — the common ratio is the same, so a - b, b - c, c - d are also in G.P, proved.

Exercise 7.4 — Question 9

Q. Find the nth term of a G.P, if a_5/a_3 = 4/9 and a_2 = 4/9.

Step 1: a_5/a_3 = r^2 = 4/9, so r = +/- 2/3

Step 2: a_2 = ar = 4/9 ; if r = 2/3 then a = 2/3 and a_n = (2/3)^n ; if r = -2/3 then a = -2/3 and a_n = (-2/3)^n

So a_n = (+/- 2/3)^n

Exercise 7.4 — Question 10

Q. Find three consecutive numbers in G.P whose sum is 26 and product is 216.

Step 1: Let the numbers be a/r, a, ar ; product = a^3 = 216, so a = 6

Step 2: Sum: 6/r + 6 + 6r = 26, so 6(r + 1/r) = 20, 3r^2 - 10r + 3 = 0, (3r - 1)(r - 3) = 0, r = 3 or 1/3

Step 3: The numbers are: 2, 6, 18 or 18, 6, 2

Exercise 7.4 — Question 11

Q. Find the 30th term of G.P x, 1, 1/x, ...

Formula (G.P): a_n = a r^(n-1), where a = first term, r = common ratio

Step 1: a = x, r = 1/x

Step 2: a_30 = x x (1/x)^29 = x^(1-29) = x^(-28) = 1/x^28

Exercise 7.4 — Question 12

Q. Find the pth term of G.P x, x^3, x^5, ...

Formula (G.P): a_n = a r^(n-1), where a = first term, r = common ratio

Step 1: a = x, r = x^3/x = x^2

Step 2: a_p = x x (x^2)^(p-1) = x^(1 + 2p - 2) = x^(2p-1)

mcqs.why: Use a_n = a r^(n-1) with a = x and r = x^3/x = x^2. Then a_p = x x (x^2)^(p-1) = x^(1 + 2p - 2) = x^(2p-1).

lessons.title: Exercise 7.5 — Geometric Mean (G.M.)
lessons.notes_html:
Exercise 7.5 of Unit 7 — Arithmetic and Geometric Sequences — complete solved exercises with every step shown.

Exercise 7.5 — Question 1: Find G.M between the following

Q. (i) 9 and 5 (ii) 4 and 9 (iii) -2 and -8

Formula: for n geometric means (G.Ms), r = (b/a)^(1/(n+1)) ; one G.M = +/- sqrt(ab)

(i) +/- sqrt(9x5) = +/- sqrt(45) = +/- 3 sqrt(5)

(ii) +/- sqrt(4x9) = +/- 6

(iii) +/- sqrt((-2)x(-8)) = +/- sqrt(16) = +/- 4 (Note: The book's answer key prints +/- 2 sqrt(2), which is the answer for -2 and -4; for the printed question -2 and -8 the correct answer is +/- 4.)

Exercise 7.5 — Question 2: Insert two G.Ms between the following

Q. (i) 1 and 8 (ii) 3 and 81

Formula: for n geometric means (G.Ms), r = (b/a)^(1/(n+1)) ; one G.M = +/- sqrt(ab)

(i) r = (8/1)^(1/3) = 2 ; the means = 2, 4

(ii) r = (81/3)^(1/3) = 3 ; the means = 9, 27

Exercise 7.5 — Question 3: Insert three G.Ms between the following

Q. (i) 1 and 16 (ii) 2 and 32

Formula: for n geometric means (G.Ms), r = (b/a)^(1/(n+1)) ; one G.M = +/- sqrt(ab)

(i) r = (16)^(1/4) = 2 ; the means = 2, 4, 8

(ii) r = (32/2)^(1/4) = 2 ; the means = 4, 8, 16

Exercise 7.5 — Question 4

Q. Insert four real geometric means between 3 and 96.

Formula: for n geometric means (G.Ms), r = (b/a)^(1/(n+1)) ; one G.M = +/- sqrt(ab)

Step 1: r = (96/3)^(1/5) = (32)^(1/5) = 2

Step 2: The means = 6, 12, 24, 48

Exercise 7.5 — Question 5

Q. The A.M between two numbers is 5 and their positive G.M is 4. Find the numbers.

Step 1: a + b = 2x5 = 10 and ab = 4^2 = 16

Step 2: The numbers are the roots of t^2 - 10t + 16 = 0: (t - 2)(t - 8) = 0

So the numbers are 2 and 8.

Exercise 7.5 — Question 6

Q. The positive G.M between two numbers is 6 and their A.M is 10. Find the numbers.

Step 1: a + b = 20 and ab = 36

Step 2: t^2 - 20t + 36 = 0, (t - 2)(t - 18) = 0

So the numbers are 2 and 18.

Exercise 7.5 — Question 7

Q. Show that the A.M between the numbers 4 and 8 is greater than their geometric mean.

Step 1: A.M = (4 + 8)/2 = 6

Step 2: Positive G.M = sqrt(4x8) = sqrt(32) = about 5.66

Step 3: 6 > 5.66, so the A.M is greater than the G.M, proved.

Exercise 7.5 — Question 8

Q. Insert four geometric means between 160 and 5.

Formula: for n geometric means (G.Ms), r = (b/a)^(1/(n+1)) ; one G.M = +/- sqrt(ab)

Step 1: r = (5/160)^(1/5) = (1/32)^(1/5) = 1/2

Step 2: The means = 80, 40, 20, 10

Exercise 7.5 — Question 9

Q. Insert three geometric means between 486 and 6.

Formula: for n geometric means (G.Ms), r = (b/a)^(1/(n+1)) ; one G.M = +/- sqrt(ab)

Step 1: r = (6/486)^(1/4) = (1/81)^(1/4) = 1/3

Step 2: The means = 162, 54, 18

Exercise 7.5 — Question 10

Q. Insert four geometric means between 1/8 and 128.

Formula: for n geometric means (G.Ms), r = (b/a)^(1/(n+1)) ; one G.M = +/- sqrt(ab)

Step 1: r = (128/(1/8))^(1/5) = (1024)^(1/5) = 4

Step 2: The means = 1/2, 2, 8, 32

Exercise 7.5 — Question 11

Q. Insert six geometric means between 56 and -7/16.

Formula: for n geometric means (G.Ms), r = (b/a)^(1/(n+1)) ; one G.M = +/- sqrt(ab)

Step 1: r = ((-7/16)/56)^(1/7) = (-1/128)^(1/7) = -1/2

Step 2: The means = -28, 14, -7, 7/2, -7/4, 7/8

Exercise 7.5 — Question 12

Q. Insert five geometric means between 32/81 and 9/2.

Formula: for n geometric means (G.Ms), r = (b/a)^(1/(n+1)) ; one G.M = +/- sqrt(ab)

Step 1: r = ((9/2)/(32/81))^(1/6) = (729/64)^(1/6) = 3/2

Step 2: The means = 16/27, 8/9, 4/3, 2, 3

mcqs.q: The G.M. between 9 and 5 is:
mcqs.why: Use G.M. = sqrt(ab) for one mean, here G.M. = +/- sqrt(9 x 5) = +/- sqrt(45) = +/- 3 sqrt(5), since sqrt(45) = sqrt(9 x 5) = 3 sqrt(5).

mcqs.q: The G.M. between 4 and 9 is:
mcqs.why: Use G.M. = sqrt(ab) for one mean, here G.M. = +/- sqrt(4 x 9) = +/- sqrt(36) = +/- 6.

mcqs.q: The G.M. between -2 and -8 is:
mcqs.why: Use G.M. = sqrt(ab) for one mean, here G.M. = +/- sqrt((-2) x (-8)) = +/- sqrt(16) = +/- 4. The book key prints +/- 2 sqrt(2), which is wrong for -2 and -8; that value would fit -2 and -4.

mcqs.q: Two G.Ms between 1 and 8 are:
mcqs.why: For n geometric means use r = (b/a)^(1/(n+1)) = (8/1)^(1/3) = 2. The means are 1 x 2 = 2 and 2 x 2 = 4.

mcqs.q: Three G.Ms between 1 and 16 are:
mcqs.why: For n geometric means use r = (b/a)^(1/(n+1)) = (16/1)^(1/4) = 2. The means are 1 x 2 = 2, 2 x 2 = 4 and 4 x 2 = 8.

mcqs.q: Four G.Ms between 3 and 96 are:
mcqs.why: For n geometric means use r = (b/a)^(1/(n+1)) = (96/3)^(1/5) = (32)^(1/5) = 2. The means are 3 x 2 = 6, 12, 24 and 48.

mcqs.q: The A.M. of two numbers is 5 and their positive G.M. is 4. The numbers are:
mcqs.why: Use A.M. = (a+b)/2 = 5, so a + b = 10, and G.M. = sqrt(ab) = 4, so ab = 16. The numbers are roots of t^2 - 10t + 16 = 0, that is (t - 2)(t - 8) = 0, giving 2 and 8.

mcqs.q: The positive G.M. of two numbers is 6 and their A.M. is 10. The numbers are:
mcqs.why: Use A.M. = (a+b)/2 = 10, so a + b = 20, and G.M. = sqrt(ab) = 6, so ab = 36. The numbers are roots of t^2 - 20t + 36 = 0, that is (t - 2)(t - 18) = 0, giving 2 and 18.

mcqs.q: Four G.Ms between 160 and 5 are:
mcqs.why: For n geometric means use r = (b/a)^(1/(n+1)) = (5/160)^(1/5) = (1/32)^(1/5) = 1/2. The means are 160 x 1/2 = 80, then 40, 20 and 10.

mcqs.q: Three G.Ms between 486 and 6 are:
mcqs.why: For n geometric means use r = (b/a)^(1/(n+1)) = (6/486)^(1/4) = (1/81)^(1/4) = 1/3. The means are 486 x 1/3 = 162, then 54 and 18.

mcqs.q: For 2, 6, 11, 17, ..., the term a_5 is:

mcqs.q: The A.M. between sqrt(3) and 3 sqrt(3) is:
mcqs.why: Use A.M. = (a+b)/2 = (sqrt(3) + 3 sqrt(3))/2 = 4 sqrt(3)/2 = 2 sqrt(3). The book key marks 5 sqrt(3), which is a key error; the correct value is 2 sqrt(3).

mcqs.q: The term a_5 of 2, 6, 18, ... is:
mcqs.why: This is a G.P with a = 2 and r = 3. Use a_n = a r^(n-1), so a_5 = 2 x 3^4 = 2 x 81 = 162.

mcqs.q: The G.M. between -3 and -12 is:

mcqs.q: The G.M. between 1 and 8 is:

lessons.title: Exercise 8.1 — Sets and Set Operations
lessons.notes_html:
Exercise 8.1 of Unit 8 — Sets and Functions — complete solved exercises with every step shown.

Exercise 8.1 — Question 1: If A = {1,4,7,8}, B = {4,6,8,9} and C = {3,4,5,7}, then find

Q. (i) A ∪ B (ii) B ∪ C (iii) A ∩ C (iv) A ∩ (B ∩ C) (v) (A ∪ B) ∪ C (vi) (A ∩ B) ∩ C

(i) A ∪ B = {1,4,6,7,8,9}

(ii) B ∪ C = {3,4,5,6,7,8,9}

(iii) A ∩ C = {4,7}

(iv) B ∩ C = {4}, so A ∩ (B ∩ C) = {4}

(v) (A ∪ B) ∪ C = {1,3,4,5,6,7,8,9}

(vi) A ∩ B = {4,8}, so (A ∩ B) ∩ C = {4}

Exercise 8.1 — Question 2

Q. If A = {1,7,11,15,17,21}, B = {11,17,19,23} and C = {2,3,5}, then verify that: (A ∩ B) ∩ C = A ∩ (B ∩ C)

Step 1: A ∩ B = {11,17} ; (A ∩ B) ∩ C = {11,17} ∩ {2,3,5} = Φ

Step 2: B ∩ C = Φ ; A ∩ (B ∩ C) = A ∩ Φ = Φ

Step 3: Both sides are Φ, verified.

Exercise 8.1 — Question 3

Q. If A = {2,4,6}, B = {3,6,9,12} and C = {4,6,8,10}, then verify that: A ∪ (B ∪ C) = (A ∪ B) ∪ C

Step 1: B ∪ C = {3,4,6,8,9,10,12} ; A ∪ (B ∪ C) = {2,3,4,6,8,9,10,12}

Step 2: A ∪ B = {2,3,4,6,9,12} ; (A ∪ B) ∪ C = {2,3,4,6,8,9,10,12}

Step 3: Both are equal, verified.

Exercise 8.1 — Question 4

Q. If A = {2,3,5,7,9}, B = {1,3,5,7} and C = {2,3,4,5,6}, then verify that: (A ∩ B) ∩ C = A ∩ (B ∩ C)

Step 1: A ∩ B = {3,5,7} ; (A ∩ B) ∩ C = {3,5}

Step 2: B ∩ C = {3,5} ; A ∩ (B ∩ C) = {3,5}

Step 3: Both are equal, verified.

Exercise 8.1 — Question 5

Q. If U = {7,8,9,10,11,12,13,14}, A = {7,10,13,14} and B = {7,8,11,12}, then verify that: (A ∩ B)^c = A^c ∪ B^c (De Morgan's law)

Step 1: A ∩ B = {7} ; (A ∩ B)^c = U - {7} = {8,9,10,11,12,13,14}

Step 2: A^c = {8,9,11,12} ; B^c = {9,10,13,14} ; A^c ∪ B^c = {8,9,10,11,12,13,14}

Step 3: Both are equal, De Morgan's law verified.

Exercise 8.1 — Question 6

Q. If U = {4,6,8,9,10}, A = {4,6} and B = {6,8,9}, then verify De Morgan's laws.

First law: (A ∪ B)' = A' ∩ B'
Step 1: A ∪ B = {4,6,8,9} ; (A ∪ B)' = {10}
Step 2: A' = {8,9,10} ; B' = {4,10} ; A' ∩ B' = {10} — equal, verified.

Second law: (A ∩ B)' = A' ∪ B'
Step 1: A ∩ B = {6} ; (A ∩ B)' = {4,8,9,10}
Step 2: A' ∪ B' = {8,9,10} ∪ {4,10} = {4,8,9,10} — equal, verified.

Exercise 8.1 — Question 7

Q. If U = {1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9}, A = {2,3,6,9} and B = {1,3,6,7,8}, then verify that: (A ∪ B)^c = A^c ∩ B^c

Step 1: A ∪ B = {1,2,3,6,7,8,9} ; (A ∪ B)^c = {4,5}

Step 2: A^c = {1,4,5,7,8} ; B^c = {2,4,5,9} ; A^c ∩ B^c = {4,5}

mcqs.why: The union A ∪ B collects every element that is in A or in B, without repetition. From {1,4,7,8} and {4,6,8,9} this gives {1,4,6,7,8,9}.
The intersection A ∩ C contains only the elements common to both sets. A has {1,4,7,8} and C has {3,4,5,7}, so the common elements are {4,7}.
First B ∩ C = {4}, since 4 is the only common element of B and C. Then A ∩ (B ∩ C) = {1,4,7,8} ∩ {4} = {4}.
First A ∪ B = {1,4,6,7,8,9}. Then (A ∪ B) ∪ C adds the elements of C = {3,4,5,7}, giving {1,3,4,5,6,7,8,9}.
First A ∩ B = {11,17}. Then (A ∩ B) ∩ C = {11,17} ∩ {2,3,5} has no common element, so the result is the empty set ∅.
First A ∩ B = {7}. Its complement is U minus {7}, which is {8,9,10,11,12,13,14}. By De Morgan law this also equals A complement union B complement.

mcqs.q: If U = {4,6,8,9,10}, A = {4,6} and B = {6,8,9}, then (A ∪ B) complement is:
mcqs.why: First A ∪ B = {4,6,8,9}. Its complement in U = {4,6,8,9,10} is U minus {4,6,8,9}, which is {10}.

mcqs.q: For any set A, A ∪ ∅ equals:
mcqs.why: The empty set ∅ has no elements to add, so A ∪ ∅ = A. This is one of the fill-in-blank identities in Exercise 8.1.

mcqs.q: By De Morgan law, (A ∩ B) complement equals:
mcqs.why: De Morgan law states (A ∩ B) complement = A complement ∪ B complement. The complement of an intersection is the union of the complements.

mcqs.q: For any set A, A ∩ A complement equals:
mcqs.why: A set and its complement have no element in common, so A ∩ A complement = ∅. This is one of the fill-in-blank identities in Exercise 8.1.

lessons.title: Exercise 8.2 — Cartesian Product, Binary Relations and Functions
lessons.notes_html:
Exercise 8.2 of Unit 8 — Sets and Functions — complete solved exercises with every step shown.

Exercise 8.2 — Question 1

Q. If A = {3,5,6}, B = {1,3}, then find A x B and B x A, and also write the domain and range of two binary relations of your own making for each case.

Step 1: A x B = {(3,1), (3,3), (5,1), (5,3), (6,1), (6,3)} ; Dom (A x B) = {3,5,6}, Range (A x B) = {1,3}

Step 2: B x A = {(1,3), (1,5), (1,6), (3,3), (3,5), (3,6)} ; Dom (B x A) = {1,3}, Range (B x A) = {3,5,6}

Step 3 (Examples): From A x B: R_1 = {(3,1), (5,3)}: Dom = {3,5}, Range = {1,3} ; R_2 = {(6,1)}: Dom = {6}, Range = {1}

From B x A: R_3 = {(1,5), (3,6)}: Dom = {1,3}, Range = {5,6} ; R_4 = {(3,3)}: Dom = {3}, Range = {3}

Exercise 8.2 — Question 2

Q. If A = {-2, 1, 4}, then write two binary relations in A and also write their domain and range.

Step 1: R_1 = {(-2,-2), (-2,1)} ; Dom (R_1) = {-2}, Range (R_1) = {-2, 1}

Step 2: R_2 = {(-2,4), (1,-2)} ; Dom (R_2) = {-2, 1}, Range (R_2) = {4, -2}

Exercise 8.2 — Question 3: Write the number of possible binary relations in the following cases

Q. (i) In C x C, when the number of elements of C is 3 (ii) In A x B, when A has 3 elements and B has 4 elements

Rule: If the Cartesian product has n pairs, the possible relations = 2^n

(i) Pairs = 3 x 3 = 9 ; Relations = 2^9

(ii) Pairs = 3 x 4 = 12 ; Relations = 2^12

Exercise 8.2 — Question 4

Q. If L = {1,2,3} and M = {2,3,4}, then write the binary relation R = {(x,y) / x ∈ L, y ∈ M and y <= x}. Also write Dom (R) and Range (R).

Step 1: Pairs satisfying y <= x: for x = 2: (2,2) ; for x = 3: (3,2), (3,3)

Step 2: R = {(2,2), (3,2), (3,3)}

Step 3: Dom (R) = {2,3}, Range (R) = {2,3}

Exercise 8.2 — Question 5

Q. If X = {0,3,5} and Y = {2,4,8}, then establish any four binary relations in X x Y.

Any subsets of X x Y are relations, for example:

R_1 = {(0,2)}

R_2 = {(3,4), (5,8)}

R_3 = {(0,8), (3,2), (5,4)}

R_4 = {(5,2), (0,4), (3,8)}

Exercise 8.2 — Question 6

Q. If A = {a,b,c} and B = {2,4,6} and f = {(a,4), (b,4), (c,4)} is a binary relation from A x B, then show that f is an (into) function from A to B.

Step 1: Dom f = {a,b,c} = A — every element of A appears once, no first element is repeated, so f is a function.

Step 2: Range f = {4}, which is not equal to B = {2,4,6}, so f is an (into) function from A to B, proved.

Exercise 8.2 — Question 7

Q. If A = {l,m,n} and B = {1,2,3} and g = {(l,3), (m,1), (n,1)} is a binary relation from A x B, then show that g is an (into) function from A to B.

Step 1: Dom g = {l,m,n} = A — no first element is repeated, so g is a function.

Step 2: Range g = {1,3}, which is not equal to B = {1,2,3}, so g is an (into) function from A to B, proved.

Exercise 8.2 — Question 8

Q. If A = {1,3,5} and B = {x,y,z} and g = {(1,x), (3,y), (5,z)} is a binary relation from A x B, then show that g is an (onto) function from A to B.

Step 1: Dom g = {1,3,5} = A — no first element is repeated, so g is a function.

Step 2: Range g = {x,y,z} = B — the range equals the whole B, so g is an (onto) function from A to B, proved.

mcqs.q: If A = {3,5,6} and B = {1,3}, then the domain of A x B is:
mcqs.why: A x B = {(3,1), (3,3), (5,1), (5,3), (6,1), (6,3)}. The domain is the set of first elements, which is {3,5,6}.

mcqs.q: If A = {3,5,6} and B = {1,3}, then the range of B x A is:
mcqs.why: B x A = {(1,3), (1,5), (1,6), (3,3), (3,5), (3,6)}. The range is the set of second elements, which is {3,5,6}.

mcqs.q: If C has 3 elements, then the number of possible binary relations in C x C is:
mcqs.why: The number of pairs in C x C is 3 x 3 = 9. Every subset is a relation, so the number of possible relations is 2^9.

mcqs.q: If A has 3 elements and B has 4 elements, then the number of possible binary relations in A x B is:
mcqs.why: The number of pairs in A x B is 3 x 4 = 12. Every subset is a relation, so the number of possible relations is 2^12.

mcqs.q: If L = {1,2,3} and M = {2,3,4}, then R with x in L, y in M and y less than or equal to x is:
mcqs.why: Check each pair with y less than or equal to x: for x = 2 only (2,2) works; for x = 3 the pairs (3,2) and (3,3) work; x = 1 gives none. So R = {(2,2), (3,2), (3,3)}.

mcqs.q: For R = {(2,2), (3,2), (3,3)}, the domain of R is:
mcqs.why: The domain is the set of first elements of the ordered pairs. The first elements are 2, 3 and 3, so Dom (R) = {2,3}.

mcqs.q: If f = {(a,4), (b,4), (c,4)} from A = {a,b,c} to B = {2,4,6}, then the range of f is:
mcqs.why: The range is the set of second elements of the pairs. Every second element is 4, so Range f = {4}.

mcqs.q: The relation f = {(a,4), (b,4), (c,4)} from A = {a,b,c} to B = {2,4,6} is an into function because:
options: its range is equal to B
its range {4} is not equal to B
mcqs.why: Dom f = {a,b,c} = A with no first element repeated, so f is a function. Its range is {4}, which is not equal to B = {2,4,6}, so f is an into function.

mcqs.q: The relation g = {(1,x), (3,y), (5,z)} from A = {1,3,5} to B = {x,y,z} is an onto function because:
options: its range {x,y,z} is equal to B
mcqs.why: Dom g = {1,3,5} = A with no first element repeated, so g is a function. Its range is {x,y,z}, which equals the whole of B, so g is an onto function.

mcqs.q: If R_2 = {(-2,4), (1,-2)}, then the range of R_2 is:
mcqs.why: The range is the set of second elements of the ordered pairs. The second elements are 4 and -2, so Range (R_2) = {4, -2}.

mcqs.q: If A and B are two non-empty sets, then A ∪ B equals:
mcqs.why: Union is commutative, so A ∪ B = B ∪ A. The union collects elements from both sets, and the order of writing the sets does not change the result.

mcqs.q: For any two sets A and B, A ∪ B = B ∪ A is called:
mcqs.why: When the order of the sets can be exchanged without changing the result, the law is the commutative law. Here A ∪ B = B ∪ A is the commutative law under union.

mcqs.q: A ∪ (B ∪ C) = (A ∪ B) ∪ C is called:
mcqs.why: Grouping the sets differently without changing the result is the associative law, so A ∪ (B ∪ C) = (A ∪ B) ∪ C is the associative law. Note the book Review Q4 misprints the right side as (A ∩ B) ∪ C; the correct form uses union on both sides.

mcqs.q: If U = {1,2,3,4} and A = {4}, then A complement is:
mcqs.why: The complement A complement is U minus A. Here U minus {4} from {1,2,3,4} leaves {1,2,3}.

mcqs.q: By De Morgan law, (A ∪ B) complement equals:
mcqs.why: De Morgan law states (A ∪ B) complement = A complement ∩ B complement. The complement of a union is the intersection of the complements.

mcqs.q: By De Morgan law, (A ∩ B) complement equals:
mcqs.why: De Morgan law states (A ∩ B) complement = A complement ∪ B complement. The complement of an intersection is the union of the complements.

mcqs.q: If R = {(4,5), (5,4), (5,6), (6,4)}, then the domain of R is:
mcqs.why: The domain is the set of first elements of the pairs: 4, 5, 5 and 6. Without repetition this is {4,5,6}.

mcqs.q: If R = {(4,5), (5,4), (5,6), (6,4)}, then the range of R is:
mcqs.why: The range is the set of second elements of the pairs: 5, 4, 6 and 4. Without repetition this is {4,5,6}.

mcqs.q: Any subset of a Cartesian product is called a:
mcqs.why: By definition, any subset of a Cartesian product A x B is called a binary relation. This converts the book Review fill-in-blank on relations.

mcqs.q: If R = {(a,b) with a, b whole numbers and 3a + 2b = 16}, counting 0 as a whole number, then the domain and range of R are:
mcqs.why: Solve 3a + 2b = 16 in whole numbers: a = 0 gives b = 8, a = 2 gives b = 5, a = 4 gives b = 2. So R = {(0,8), (2,5), (4,2)}, giving Domain {0,2,4} and Range {2,5,8}. The book key lists only {2,4} and {2,5} because it leaves out the pair (0,8).

Exercise 9.1 — Question 1: Show the following points on the graph whose co-ordinates are given

Q. (i) A(2,-4) (ii) B(3,2) (iii) C(-5,-1) (iv) D(6,-3) (v) E(4,4) (vi) F(-3,7) (vii) G(0,7) (viii) H(5,0)

Method: For a point (x, y), from the origin move x units along the x-axis (right if positive, left if negative) and then y units in the y direction (up if positive, down if negative).

(i) A(2,-4): right 2, down 4 — 4th quadrant (IV)

(ii) B(3,2): right 3, up 2 — 1st quadrant (I)

(iii) C(-5,-1): left 5, down 1 — 3rd quadrant (III)

(iv) D(6,-3): right 6, down 3 — 4th quadrant (IV)

(v) E(4,4): right 4, up 4 — 1st quadrant (I)

(vi) F(-3,7): left 3, up 7 — 2nd quadrant (II)

(vii) G(0,7): 7 units up the y-axis from the origin — lies on the y-axis

(viii) H(5,0): 5 units right on the x-axis — lies on the x-axis

Q. (i) Origin (ii) The point which is at a distance of 5 units from the origin to the left of the x-axis (iii) The point which is on the x-axis at a distance of 3 units to the right of the origin (iv) The point which is above the x-axis and at a distance of 4 units on the y-axis (v) The point which is below the x-axis and at a distance of 6 units on the y-axis

(i) (0, 0)

(ii) (-5, 0)

(iii) (3, 0)

(iv) (0, 4)

(v) (0, -6)

Exercise 9.1 — Question 3: Make figures on graph paper with the help of the following points

Q. (i) A(7,2), B(-6,-3), C(5,3) (ii) A(0,-7), B(3,-2), C(4,0), D(5,6), E(7,8) (iii) A(4,0), B(0,4), C(-4,0), D(0,-4) (iv) A(10,6), B(-10,6), C(-10,-6), D(10,-6)

(i) Plot the three points and join them in order: a triangle is formed.

(ii) Plot the five points: A, B, C come almost on one straight line; D and E are separate points above that line — this is the figure shown in the book's answers.

(iii) Joining the four points forms a square (diamond-shaped) whose vertices lie on the axes.

(iv) Joining the four points forms a rectangle: length 20 units (x = -10 to 10) and width 12 units (y = -6 to 6).

mcqs.q: In which quadrant does the point A(2, -4) lie?
mcqs.why: For A(2, -4), x = 2 is positive so we move right 2, and y = -4 is negative so we move down 4. Positive x with negative y is the 4th quadrant (IV).

mcqs.q: In which quadrant does the point B(3, 2) lie?
mcqs.why: For B(3, 2), x = 3 is positive (right 3) and y = 2 is positive (up 2). Both coordinates positive means the 1st quadrant (I).

mcqs.q: In which quadrant does the point C(-5, -1) lie?
mcqs.why: For C(-5, -1), x = -5 means left 5 and y = -1 means down 1. Both coordinates negative means the 3rd quadrant (III).

mcqs.q: In which quadrant does the point F(-3, 7) lie?
mcqs.why: For F(-3, 7), x = -3 means left 3 and y = 7 means up 7. Negative x with positive y is the 2nd quadrant (II).

mcqs.q: Where does the point G(0, 7) lie?
mcqs.why: For G(0, 7), x = 0 means no move left or right from the origin, then 7 units up. A point with x = 0 lies on the y-axis.

mcqs.q: Where does the point H(5, 0) lie?
mcqs.why: For H(5, 0), we move 5 units right and y = 0 means no move up or down. A point with y = 0 lies on the x-axis.

mcqs.q: What are the coordinates of the origin?
mcqs.why: The origin O is where the x-axis and y-axis cross. Both its coordinates are zero, so the origin is (0, 0).

mcqs.q: What are the coordinates of the point which is at a distance of 5 units from the origin to the left on the x-axis?
mcqs.why: The point is on the x-axis so y = 0. Left of the origin means x is negative, and the distance is 5, so x = -5. The point is (-5, 0).

mcqs.q: What are the coordinates of the point below the x-axis at a distance of 6 units on the y-axis?
mcqs.why: The point is on the y-axis so x = 0. Below the x-axis means y is negative, and the distance is 6, so y = -6. The point is (0, -6).

mcqs.q: Joining the points A(4, 0), B(0, 4), C(-4, 0), D(0, -4) in order forms which figure?
options: A square with vertices on the axes
mcqs.why: Each point is 4 units from the origin on an axis. Joining (4, 0) to (0, 4) to (-4, 0) to (0, -4) and back gives four equal sides, a square whose vertices lie on the axes.
