mcqs.q: Which point lies on the graph of y = 3x?
mcqs.why: Put x = 2 in y = 3x. Then y = 3 times 2 = 6. So the point (2, 6) from the table of y = 3x lies on the graph.

mcqs.q: What is the y-intercept of the graph of y = x + 7?
mcqs.why: The y-intercept is found by putting x = 0. Then y = 0 + 7 = 7, so the line meets the y-axis at the point (0, 7).

mcqs.q: What is the x-intercept of the graph of y = x + 7?
mcqs.why: The x-intercept is found by putting y = 0. Then 0 = x + 7, so x = -7. The line meets the x-axis at the point (-7, 0).

mcqs.q: Which point lies on the graph of y = 2x - 3?
mcqs.why: Put x = 2 in y = 2x - 3. Then y = 2 times 2 minus 3 = 4 - 3 = 1. This matches the table value, so (2, 1) lies on the graph.

mcqs.q: What is the y-intercept of the graph of y = 4x + 1?
mcqs.why: Put x = 0 in y = 4x + 1. Then y = 4 times 0 plus 1 = 1, so the y-intercept is 1 and the point is (0, 1).

mcqs.q: What is the x-intercept of the graph of y = -x/2 - 3/2?
mcqs.why: Put y = 0 in y = -x/2 - 3/2. Then x/2 = -3/2, so x = -3. The table also gives the point (-3, 0) on this line.

mcqs.q: For the graph of y = x - 1, what is the value of y when x = 3?
mcqs.why: Put x = 3 in y = x - 1. Then y = 3 - 1 = 2. This is the last value in the table for y = x - 1, giving the point (3, 2).

mcqs.q: What is the y-intercept of the graph of y = 3x + 5?
mcqs.why: Put x = 0 in y = 3x + 5. Then y = 3 times 0 plus 5 = 5, so the y-intercept is 5 and the point is (0, 5).

mcqs.q: The graph of y = x/2 passes through the origin. What is its slope?
mcqs.why: In y = x/2, y is x multiplied by 1/2, so the slope is 1/2. The table x: -6, -4, -2, 0, 2, 4, 6 gives y: -3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3, confirming the line passes through (0, 0).

mcqs.q: Points A(1, 0), B(7, 0) and C(1, 8) are joined. What is the length of AB?
mcqs.why: A(1, 0) and B(7, 0) are both on the x-axis. Length AB = 7 - 1 = 6 units. With AC = 8 units vertical, the figure is a right-angled triangle with the right angle at A.

lessons.title: Exercise 9.3 — Conversion Graphs
lessons.notes_html:
Exercise 9.3 of Unit 9 — Linear Graphs — complete solved exercises with every step shown.

Exercise 9.3 — Question 1

Q. The table gives temperatures in Fahrenheit (°F) and their equivalent Centigrade (°C) values: °F: 57, 126, 158, 194 ; °C: 14, 52, 70, 90. Plot these points on graph paper (°C 0 to 100, °F 0 to 220; 5 small squares = 20 units on each axis) and convert from the graph: (a) 97°F into °C (b) 127°F into °C (c) 25°C into °F (d) 80°C into °F

Formula (for checking): °C = (5/9)(°F - 32) ; °F = (9/5)°C + 32

(a) (5/9)(97 - 32) = (5/9)(65) = about 36°C

(b) (5/9)(127 - 32) = (5/9)(95) = about 53°C

(c) (9/5)(25) + 32 = 45 + 32 = 77°F

(d) (9/5)(80) + 32 = 144 + 32 = 176°F

Exercise 9.3 — Question 2

Q. The table gives the conversion from US dollars ($) to pounds (£): $: 50, 100, 200 ; £: 35, 70, 140. Plot these points, draw a straight line (5 small squares = 50 units on each axis) and convert from the graph: (a) 160 dollars into £ (b) 96 dollars into £ (c) 120£ into dollars (d) 76£ into dollars

Rate: £0.7 per $1 (100$ = 70£) ; Formula: £ = 0.7 x $ ; $ = £/0.7

(a) 0.7 x 160 = £112

(b) 0.7 x 96 = £67.2

(c) 120/0.7 = about $171.4 (from the graph about $171)

(d) 76/0.7 = about $108.6 (from the graph about $109)

Exercise 9.3 — Question 3

Q. The table gives kilometres and their equivalent miles values: km: 0, 100, 200, 300 ; miles: 0, 62.5, 125, 187.5. Plot these values on graph paper (10 small squares = 100 km on the x-axis; 10 small squares = 100 miles on the y-axis) and convert from the graph: (a) 140 kilometres into miles (b) 175 kilometres into miles (c) 50 miles into kilometres (d) 100 miles into kilometres

Rate: 100 km = 62.5 miles ; Formula: miles = 0.625 x km ; km = miles/0.625

(a) 0.625 x 140 = 87.5 miles

(b) 0.625 x 175 = about 109.4 miles

(c) 50/0.625 = 80 km

(d) 100/0.625 = 160 km

Exercise 9.3 — Question 4

Q. Using the graph of article 9.2.3, convert: (a) 6 acres into hectares (b) 18 acres into hectares (c) 24 acres into hectares (d) 6.0702 hectares into acres (e) 11.3311 hectares into acres

Rate: 1 acre = 0.4047 hectare (approximately) ; 1 hectare = 2.471 acres

(a) 6 x 0.4047 = about 2.43 hectares

(b) 18 x 0.4047 = about 7.28 hectares

(c) 24 x 0.4047 = about 9.71 hectares

(d) 6.0702/0.4047 = 15 acres

(e) 11.3311/0.4047 = 28 acres

Exercise 9.3 — Book activity (temperature graph, article 9.2): Use the graph to convert

Q. (i) 95°F into °C (ii) 113°F into °C (iii) 150°F into °C (iv) 86°C into °F (v) 20°C into °F (vi) 220°F into °C

Formula: °C = (5/9)(°F - 32) ; °F = (9/5)°C + 32

(i) (5/9)(63) = 35°C

(ii) (5/9)(81) = 45°C

(iii) (5/9)(118) = about 65.6°C (from the graph about 65°C)

(iv) (9/5)(86) + 32 = 154.8 + 32 = 186.8 = about 187°F

(v) (9/5)(20) + 32 = 68°F

(vi) (5/9)(188) = about 104.4°C (from the graph about 104°C)

mcqs.q: Convert 97 degrees Fahrenheit into degrees Centigrade.
mcqs.why: Use C = (5/9)(F - 32). Then C = (5/9)(97 - 32) = (5/9)(65) = 325/9, which is about 36 degrees C.

mcqs.q: Convert 127 degrees Fahrenheit into degrees Centigrade.
Convert 25 degrees Centigrade into degrees Fahrenheit.
Convert 80 degrees Centigrade into degrees Fahrenheit.
Using the rate 1 dollar = 0.7 pounds, convert 160 dollars into pounds.
mcqs.why: Use pounds = 0.7 times dollars. Then pounds = 0.7 times 160 = 112. So 160 dollars is 112 pounds.

mcqs.q: Using the rate 1 dollar = 0.7 pounds, convert 96 dollars into pounds.
mcqs.why: Use pounds = 0.7 times dollars. Then pounds = 0.7 times 96 = 67.2. So 96 dollars is 67.2 pounds.

mcqs.q: Using the rate 1 dollar = 0.7 pounds, 120 pounds is about how many dollars?
mcqs.why: Use dollars = pounds divided by 0.7. Then dollars = 120 / 0.7 = about 171.4, so from the graph about 171 dollars.

mcqs.q: Using the rate 100 km = 62.5 miles, convert 140 kilometres into miles.
mcqs.why: Use miles = 0.625 times km, since 62.5 / 100 = 0.625. Then miles = 0.625 times 140 = 87.5 miles.

mcqs.q: Using the rate 100 km = 62.5 miles, convert 50 miles into kilometres.
mcqs.why: Use km = miles divided by 0.625. Then km = 50 / 0.625 = 80. So 50 miles is 80 kilometres.

mcqs.q: Using 1 acre = 0.4047 hectare, convert 6 acres into hectares.
mcqs.why: Use hectares = 0.4047 times acres. Then hectares = 6 times 0.4047 = 2.4282, which is about 2.43 hectares.

mcqs.q: The coordinates of the origin are:
mcqs.why: The origin is the point where the two axes meet. Both coordinates are zero there, so the origin is (0, 0), as in the Review fill-in item as well.

mcqs.q: The perpendicular distance of a point from the y-axis is called:
mcqs.why: The distance of a point from the y-axis is measured along the x direction and is the x-coordinate of the point. This distance is called the abscissa.

mcqs.q: The perpendicular distance of a point from the x-axis is called:
mcqs.why: The distance of a point from the x-axis is measured along the y direction and is the y-coordinate of the point. This distance is called the ordinate.

mcqs.q: For x = 1 in 2x + y = 6, we have y = ?
mcqs.why: Put x = 1 in 2x + y = 6. Then 2 times 1 plus y = 6, so 2 + y = 6 and y = 6 - 2 = 4.

mcqs.q: For y = 2 in 2x - y = 6, we have x = ?
mcqs.why: Put y = 2 in 2x - y = 6. Then 2x - 2 = 6, so 2x = 8 and x = 8 / 2 = 4.

mcqs.q: The graph of an equation in the form y = c has y-coordinate:
mcqs.why: In y = c, the value of y is the constant c for every point of the graph, whatever x is. So the y-coordinate of each point is c.

mcqs.q: The graph of an equation in the form x = a has x-coordinate:
mcqs.why: In x = a, the value of x is the constant a for every point of the graph, whatever y is. So the x-coordinate of each point is a.

mcqs.q: f(x) = x/2, for x from 4 to 12, where x is a multiple of 2. The domain of f(x) is:
mcqs.why: The domain is the set of allowed x values. The multiples of 2 from 4 to 12 are 4, 6, 8, 10 and 12, so the domain is {4, 6, 8, 10, 12}.

mcqs.q: f(x) = x/2, for x from 4 to 12, where x is a multiple of 2. The range of f(x) is:
mcqs.why: Apply f(x) = x/2 to each domain value: 4/2 = 2, 6/2 = 3, 8/2 = 4, 10/2 = 5, 12/2 = 6. So the range is {2, 3, 4, 5, 6}.

mcqs.q: If y = 3x, then for x = 2, we have y = ?
mcqs.why: Put x = 2 in y = 3x. Then y = 3 times 2 = 6. This item was missing from the book key and the computed answer is 6.

lessons.title: Exercise 10.1 — Data and Frequency Tables
lessons.notes_html:
Exercise 10.1 of Unit 10 — Basic Statistics — complete solved exercises with every step shown.

Exercise 10.1 — Question 1

Q. 50 children in a junior school joined the school computer club. Their ages were recorded (as given in the table in the book). Make a frequency table showing how many children there are of each age and represent this information on a bar chart.

Step 1: Count all the 50 ages — how many times each age occurs:

Age 7: 7 children ; Age 8: 9 children ; Age 9: 11 children ; Age 10: 14 children ; Age 11: 9 children

Step 2: Frequency table: Age (years) | Frequency (f) — 7 | 7 ; 8 | 9 ; 9 | 11 ; 10 | 14 ; 11 | 9 ; Total = 50

Step 3: Bar chart (in words): Take age (7 to 11) on the x-axis and frequency (0 to 14) on the y-axis; draw a bar of height equal to the frequency above each age — the tallest bar is for age 10 (14) and the shortest for age 7 (7); keep equal gaps between the bars.

Exercise 10.1 — Question 2

Q. At a local fish and chip shop on a Friday evening 56 customers came. They spent the rupees given in the table in the book. Using the groups Rs. 0-99, Rs. 100-199, Rs. 200-299, Rs. 300-399, Rs. 400-499, Rs. 500-599 make a frequency table and represent the data on a bar chart.

Step 1: Count the 56 amounts into the given groups:

0-99: 9 ; 100-199: 10 ; 200-299: 16 ; 300-399: 12 ; 400-499: 5 ; 500-599: 4

Step 2: Frequency table: Spending (Rs.) | Frequency — 0-99 | 9 ; 100-199 | 10 ; 200-299 | 16 ; 300-399 | 12 ; 400-499 | 5 ; 500-599 | 4 ; Total = 56

Step 3: Bar chart (in words): Take the six groups on the x-axis and frequency (0 to 16) on the y-axis; draw a bar of the height of its frequency over each group — the tallest bar is of the group 200-299 (16).

Exercise 10.1 — Question 3

Q. The weights (to the nearest gram) of 30 packets of popcorn sold at a fair are given in the table in the book. Make a frequency table and represent the data on a bar chart.

Step 1: The weights range from 60 to 88 grams; make the classes 60-64, 65-69, 70-74, 75-79, 80-84, 85-89 and count:

60-64: 3 ; 65-69: 12 ; 70-74: 6 ; 75-79: 3 ; 80-84: 3 ; 85-89: 3

Step 2: Frequency table: Weight (g) | Frequency — 60-64 | 3 ; 65-69 | 12 ; 70-74 | 6 ; 75-79 | 3 ; 80-84 | 3 ; 85-89 | 3 ; Total = 30

Step 3: Bar chart (in words): Take the six classes on the x-axis and frequency (0 to 12) on the y-axis; draw a bar of the height of its frequency over each class — the tallest bar is of 65-69 (12).

mcqs.q: In the computer club survey of 50 children, how many children are aged 10 years?
mcqs.why: Counting the recorded ages gives age 10 occurring 14 times. The frequencies 7, 9, 11, 14, 9 for ages 7 to 11 add to 7 + 9 + 11 + 14 + 9 = 50.

mcqs.q: In the computer club survey, which age has the tallest bar on the bar chart?
mcqs.why: The frequencies are age 7: 7, age 8: 9, age 9: 11, age 10: 14, age 11: 9. The largest frequency is 14, so the tallest bar is for age 10.

mcqs.q: In the computer club survey, how many children are aged 9 years?
mcqs.why: Counting the recorded ages gives age 9 occurring 11 times. Check: the total is 7 + 9 + 11 + 14 + 9 = 50 children, as stated.

mcqs.q: How many children in total joined the computer club in Exercise 10.1 Question 1?
mcqs.why: Add the frequencies: 7 + 9 + 11 + 14 + 9 = 50. So the frequency table total is 50 children.

mcqs.q: At the fish and chip shop, which spending group has the highest frequency?
mcqs.why: The group frequencies are 9, 10, 16, 12, 5, 4. The largest is 16, which belongs to the group Rs. 200-299, so its bar is the tallest.

mcqs.q: At the fish and chip shop, what is the frequency of the group Rs. 200-299?
mcqs.why: Counting the 56 amounts into the groups gives Rs. 200-299 occurring 16 times. Check: 9 + 10 + 16 + 12 + 5 + 4 = 56 customers.

mcqs.q: How many customers in total came to the fish and chip shop?
mcqs.why: Add the group frequencies: 9 + 10 + 16 + 12 + 5 + 4 = 56. So 56 customers came on that Friday evening.

mcqs.q: For the 30 popcorn packets, which weight class has the highest frequency?
mcqs.why: The class frequencies are 3, 12, 6, 3, 3, 3. The largest is 12, which belongs to the class 65-69 g, so its bar is the tallest.

mcqs.q: For the popcorn packets, what is the frequency of the class 65-69 g?
mcqs.why: Counting the 30 weights into the classes 60-64, 65-69, 70-74, 75-79, 80-84, 85-89 gives 12 packets in 65-69 g. Check: 3 + 12 + 6 + 3 + 3 + 3 = 30.

mcqs.q: At the fish and chip shop, what is the frequency of the group Rs. 500-599?
mcqs.why: Counting the amounts gives only 4 customers in Rs. 500-599, the smallest group. The full table 9, 10, 16, 12, 5, 4 adds to 56.

lessons.title: Exercise 10.2 — Histograms
lessons.notes_html:
Exercise 10.2 of Unit 10 — Basic Statistics — complete solved exercises with every step shown.

Exercise 10.2 — Question 1: Draw a histogram for each of the following tables

Q. (i) Ages of 100 people attending a school function: Age (years) 0-19, 20-39, 40-59, 60-79, 80-89 ; Frequency 43, 24, 17, 10, 6 (ii) Survey of the weekly earnings of 100 sixteen-year old boys: Earnings 0-9, 10-19, 20-29, 30-39, 40-49, 50-59 ; Frequency 45, 10, 11, 21, 10, 3 (iii) Average marks in the annual examination of 40 children: Average marks 1-20, 21-40, 41-60, 61-80, 81-100 ; Frequency 2, 4, 19, 12, 3

Method: In a histogram the classes are taken continuously (without gaps) on the x-axis and a rectangle of height equal to its frequency is drawn over each class; the rectangles touch each other.

(i) Five rectangles with heights 43, 24, 17, 10, 6 respectively — the first rectangle is the tallest, then the height keeps decreasing.

(ii) Six rectangles with heights 45, 10, 11, 21, 10, 3 — the first is the tallest (45), the fourth is the second largest (21).

(iii) Five rectangles with heights 2, 4, 19, 12, 3 — the third rectangle (41-60) is the tallest (19).

Exercise 10.2 — Question 2

Q. The histogram in the book shows the distribution of the time taken by 50 children to go to school. Make a frequency table from the histogram.

Step 1: Read the height of each bar from the y-axis (frequency):

Time (minutes) | Frequency — 1-10 | 5 ; 11-20 | 15 ; 21-30 | 12 ; 31-40 | 5 ; 41-50 | 2 ; 51-60 | 2

Step 2: This table is the required frequency table.

Note: In the printed figure the heights of the bars add up to 41, while the question states 50 children — there appears to be a difference in the book's figure/printing; the values above are read from the figure.

mcqs.q: In the histogram of ages of 100 people at a school function, what is the frequency of the class 0-19 years?
mcqs.why: The first rectangle has height 43 for the class 0-19. Check: 43 + 24 + 17 + 10 + 6 = 100 people in total.

mcqs.q: In that ages histogram, what is the frequency of the class 60-79 years?
mcqs.why: Reading the rectangle heights in order gives 43, 24, 17, 10, 6. The fourth class, 60-79 years, has frequency 10.

mcqs.q: In the histogram of weekly earnings of 100 boys, which class is the tallest?
mcqs.why: The rectangle heights are 45, 10, 11, 21, 10, 3. The largest height is 45, which is the first class, earnings 0-9.

mcqs.q: In that earnings histogram, what is the frequency of the class 30-39?
mcqs.why: Reading the heights in order gives 45, 10, 11, 21, 10, 3. The fourth class, 30-39, has frequency 21, the second largest bar.

mcqs.q: In the histogram of average marks of 40 children, which class is the tallest?
mcqs.why: The rectangle heights are 2, 4, 19, 12, 3. The largest height is 19, which belongs to the class 41-60 marks.

mcqs.q: In that average marks histogram, what is the frequency of the class 1-20?
mcqs.why: Reading the heights in order gives 2, 4, 19, 12, 3. The first class, 1-20 marks, has frequency 2. Check: 2 + 4 + 19 + 12 + 3 = 40 children.

mcqs.q: From the histogram of time taken to go to school, what is the frequency for 11-20 minutes?
mcqs.why: Reading each bar height from the histogram gives 1-10: 5, 11-20: 15, 21-30: 12, 31-40: 5, 41-50: 2, 51-60: 2. So 11-20 minutes has frequency 15.

mcqs.q: From that school travel histogram, what is the frequency for 21-30 minutes?
mcqs.why: The bar heights read from the figure are 5, 15, 12, 5, 2, 2 in class order. The third class, 21-30 minutes, has frequency 12.

mcqs.q: From that school travel histogram, what is the frequency for 41-50 minutes?
mcqs.why: The bar heights are 5, 15, 12, 5, 2, 2. The fifth class, 41-50 minutes, has height 2, so its frequency is 2.

mcqs.q: The bar heights in the school travel histogram add up to which total?
mcqs.why: Add the bar readings: 5 + 15 + 12 + 5 + 2 + 2 = 41. The printed bars total 41 children, even though the question states 50.

lessons.title: Exercise 10.3 — Frequency Polygon
lessons.notes_html:
Exercise 10.3 of Unit 10 — Basic Statistics — complete solved exercises with every step shown.

Exercise 10.3 — Question 1: Represent the given data by a frequency polygon

Q. (i) Distribution of the marks of 30 children in a test: Marks 0-39, 40-49, 50-79, 80-99 ; Frequency 8, 8, 10, 4 (ii) Time (seconds) taken by 40 children to complete an obstacle race: 1-40, 41-50, 51-60, 61-70 ; Frequency 8, 15, 7, 10 (iii) Distribution of the weights of 30 packets of chips from a fish and chip shop: Weight (g) 1-50, 51-60, 61-70, 71-80 ; Frequency 4, 8, 14, 4 (iv) Distribution of the marks of 100 students in the last term's mathematics examination: Marks 0-29, 30-39, 40-49, 50-59, 60-99 ; Frequency 10, 15, 25, 34, 16

Method: Find the mid-point (class mark) of each class, plot the point of the frequency against it, join the points with straight lines and extend both ends to the x-axis (imaginary classes of zero frequency at the start and the end).

(i) Class marks: 19.5, 44.5, 64.5, 89.5 ; Points: (19.5, 8), (44.5, 8), (64.5, 10), (89.5, 4)

(ii) Class marks: 20.5, 45.5, 55.5, 65.5 ; Points: (20.5, 8), (45.5, 15), (55.5, 7), (65.5, 10)

(iii) Class marks: 25.5, 55.5, 65.5, 75.5 ; Points: (25.5, 4), (55.5, 8), (65.5, 14), (75.5, 4)

(iv) Class marks: 14.5, 34.5, 44.5, 54.5, 79.5 ; Points: (14.5, 10), (34.5, 15), (44.5, 25), (54.5, 34), (79.5, 16)

mcqs.q: For a frequency polygon, what is the class mark of the marks class 0-39?
mcqs.why: Class mark = (lower limit + upper limit) / 2 = (0 + 39) / 2 = 39 / 2 = 19.5. The polygon point for this class is (19.5, 8).

mcqs.q: In the marks distribution 0-39, 40-49, 50-79, 80-99 with frequencies 8, 8, 10, 4, which point is plotted for the class 50-79?
mcqs.why: Class mark = (50 + 79) / 2 = 129 / 2 = 64.5. Plot the frequency 10 against this mark, giving the point (64.5, 10).

mcqs.q: What is the class mark of the race time class 41-50 seconds?
mcqs.why: Class mark = (lower limit + upper limit) / 2 = (41 + 50) / 2 = 91 / 2 = 45.5. The polygon point for this class is (45.5, 15).

mcqs.q: In the obstacle race distribution with frequencies 8, 15, 7, 10, which is the highest polygon point?
mcqs.why: The class marks are 20.5, 45.5, 55.5, 65.5 with frequencies 8, 15, 7, 10. The largest frequency is 15, so the highest point is (45.5, 15).

mcqs.q: What is the class mark of the chips weight class 1-50 g?
mcqs.why: Class mark = (lower limit + upper limit) / 2 = (1 + 50) / 2 = 51 / 2 = 25.5. The polygon point for this class is (25.5, 4).

mcqs.q: In the chips weights distribution, the class 61-70 g has frequency 14. Which point is plotted?
mcqs.why: Class mark = (61 + 70) / 2 = 131 / 2 = 65.5. Plot the frequency 14 against 65.5, giving the point (65.5, 14), the peak of this polygon.

mcqs.q: What is the class mark of the mathematics marks class 30-39?
mcqs.why: Class mark = (lower limit + upper limit) / 2 = (30 + 39) / 2 = 69 / 2 = 34.5. The polygon point for this class is (34.5, 15).

mcqs.q: In the mathematics examination distribution with frequencies 10, 15, 25, 34, 16, which point is the peak of the polygon?
mcqs.why: The class marks are 14.5, 34.5, 44.5, 54.5, 79.5. The largest frequency is 34 for the class 50-59, whose mark is (50 + 59) / 2 = 54.5, giving the peak point (54.5, 34).

mcqs.q: How is a frequency polygon completed at both ends?
options: By joining the first and last points together
By extending both ends to the x-axis with imaginary classes of zero frequency
By drawing bars at both ends
mcqs.why: After joining the plotted points with straight lines, both ends are extended to the x-axis. This uses imaginary classes of zero frequency before the first class and after the last class.

mcqs.q: What is the class mark of the marks class 80-99 in the first distribution of Exercise 10.3?
mcqs.why: Class mark = (lower limit + upper limit) / 2 = (80 + 99) / 2 = 179 / 2 = 89.5. The polygon point for this class is (89.5, 4).

lessons.title: Exercise 10.4 — Cumulative Frequency Polygon (Ogive)
lessons.notes_html:
Exercise 10.4 of Unit 10 — Basic Statistics — complete solved exercises with every step shown.

Exercise 10.4 — Question 1: Draw a cumulative frequency polygon (ogive) for the given data

Q. (i) Weights (kg) of 60 ten-year old boys: 31-36, 37-39, 40-42, 43-45, 46-54 ; Frequency 8, 10, 18, 12, 12 (ii) Time (minutes) taken by 50 five-year old children to eat the school lunch: 4-5, 6-7, 8-9, 10-11, 12-15, 16-19, 20-29 ; Frequency 5, 4, 10, 9, 6, 6, 10 (iii) Ages of people boarding buses at a bus station from 08.30 to 09.00 in the morning: 0-9, 10-19, 20-29, 30-39, 40-69 ; Frequency 10, 20, 30, 20, 15 (iv) Classes 5-10, 10-15, 15-20, 20-25, 25-30 ; Frequency 10, 15, 20, 30, 15 (v) Weights (kg) of 100 people: 50-59, 60-69, 70-79, 80-89, 90-99, 100-109 ; Frequency 15, 30, 35, 15, 3, 2

Method: First make the cumulative frequencies (cf); then plot each class's cf against its upper limit and join the points; the curve starts from cf = 0 at the lower limit of the first class.

(i) cf: 8, 18, 36, 48, 60 ; Ogive points (upper limit, cf): (36, 8), (39, 18), (42, 36), (45, 48), (54, 60)

(ii) cf: 5, 9, 19, 28, 34, 40, 50 ; Points: (5, 5), (7, 9), (9, 19), (11, 28), (15, 34), (19, 40), (29, 50)

(iii) cf: 10, 30, 60, 80, 95 ; Points: (9, 10), (19, 30), (29, 60), (39, 80), (69, 95)

(iv) cf: 10, 25, 45, 75, 90 ; Points: (10, 10), (15, 25), (20, 45), (25, 75), (30, 90)

(v) cf: 15, 45, 80, 95, 98, 100 ; Points: (59, 15), (69, 45), (79, 80), (89, 95), (99, 98), (109, 100)

mcqs.q: For the weights of 60 boys with frequencies 8, 10, 18, 12, 12, what is the cumulative frequency up to the class 40-42 kg?
mcqs.why: Cumulative frequency adds the frequencies in order: 8, then 8 + 10 = 18, then 18 + 18 = 36. So up to 40-42 kg the cumulative frequency is 36.

mcqs.q: For those weights, which ogive point corresponds to the class 40-42 kg?
mcqs.why: An ogive plots cumulative frequency against the upper limit of the class. For 40-42 kg the upper limit is 42 and the cumulative frequency is 36, giving the point (42, 36).

mcqs.q: For the lunch times of 50 children with frequencies 5, 4, 10, 9, 6, 6, 10, what is the cumulative frequency up to 8-9 minutes?
mcqs.why: Add in order: 5, then 5 + 4 = 9, then 9 + 10 = 19. So up to the class 8-9 minutes the cumulative frequency is 19, giving the ogive point (9, 19).

mcqs.q: For the ages of bus passengers with frequencies 10, 20, 30, 20, 15, what is the cumulative frequency up to the class 20-29?
mcqs.why: Add in order: 10, then 10 + 20 = 30, then 30 + 30 = 60. So up to 20-29 the cumulative frequency is 60, giving the ogive point (29, 60).

mcqs.q: For the classes 5-10, 10-15, 15-20, 20-25, 25-30 with frequencies 10, 15, 20, 30, 15, which ogive point corresponds to 20-25?
mcqs.why: Cumulative frequencies are 10, 25, 45, 75, 90. For the class 20-25 the upper limit is 25 and the cumulative frequency is 75, giving the point (25, 75).

mcqs.q: For the weights of 100 people with frequencies 15, 30, 35, 15, 3, 2, what is the cumulative frequency up to 70-79 kg?
mcqs.why: Add in order: 15, then 15 + 30 = 45, then 45 + 35 = 80. So up to 70-79 kg the cumulative frequency is 80, giving the ogive point (79, 80).

mcqs.q: What is the final cumulative frequency for the weights of 100 people?
mcqs.why: The cumulative frequencies are 15, 45, 80, 95, 98, 100. The last one equals the total frequency, 15 + 30 + 35 + 15 + 3 + 2 = 100 people.

mcqs.q: In drawing an ogive, the cumulative frequency of each class is plotted against what?
options: The class mark of the class
The lower limit of the class
The upper limit of the class
mcqs.why: Method: first make the cumulative frequencies, then plot each cumulative frequency against the upper limit of its class and join the points. The curve starts from cumulative frequency 0 at the lower limit of the first class.

mcqs.q: For the weights of 60 boys, what is the first ogive point for the class 31-36 kg?
mcqs.why: The first frequency is 8, so the first cumulative frequency is 8. The upper limit of 31-36 is 36, so the first ogive point is (36, 8).

mcqs.q: For the classes 5-10 to 25-30 with frequencies 10, 15, 20, 30, 15, what is the total number of observations?
mcqs.why: The final cumulative frequency equals the total: 10 + 15 + 20 + 30 + 15 = 90. The cumulative frequencies are 10, 25, 45, 75, 90.

lessons.notes_html:

Review Exercise 10 — Question 1 (i): Encircle the correct answer

When a bar graph is constructed, so that the area of each bar is proportional to the number of items in each group is called:

Review Exercise 10 — Question 1 (ii): Encircle the correct answer

Review Exercise 10 — Question 1 (iii): Encircle the correct answer

Review Exercise 10 — Question 1 (v): Encircle the correct answer

Review Exercise 10 — Question 1 (vi): Encircle the correct answer

X-bar = (x_1 + x_2 + x_3 + ... + x_n)/n is called:

Review Exercise 10 — Question 1 (ix): Encircle the correct answer

Review Exercise 10 — Question 2 (i): Fill in the blanks

Fill in the blank: When a bar graph is constructed, so that the area of each bar is proportional to the number of items in each group is called _______ Answer: histogram

Review Exercise 10 — Question 2 (ii): Fill in the blanks

Review Exercise 10 — Question 2 (iii): Fill in the blanks

Fill in the blank: If all numbers in a set are added together and then the total is divided by the number of scores in the set is called _______ Answer: mean

Review Exercise 10 — Question 2 (iv): Fill in the blanks

Fill in the blank: The middle value of data arranged in numerical order is called _______ Answer: median

Review Exercise 10 — Question 2 (v): Fill in the blanks

Fill in the blank: The score which occurs most often in a set of data is called _______ Answer: mode

Review Exercise 10 — Question 2 (vi): Fill in the blanks

Fill in the blank: X-bar = (x_1 + x_2 + x_3 + ... + x_n)/n is called _______ Answer: mean value of x_1, x_2, ..., x_n

Review Exercise 10 — Question 2 (vii): Fill in the blanks

Review Exercise 10 — Question 2 (viii): Fill in the blanks

Fill in the blank: H = n / Sum(1/x) is called _______ Answer: harmonic mean

Review Exercise 10 — Question 2 (ix): Fill in the blanks

Review Exercise 10 — Question 2 (x): Fill in the blanks

Review Exercise 10 — Question 3

Q. Find the standard deviation of the values 2, 3, 6, 8, 11.

Formula: S = sqrt( Sum(x - X-bar)^2 / n )

Step 1: Mean X-bar = (2 + 3 + 6 + 8 + 11)/5 = 30/5 = 6

Step 2: Deviations: -4, -3, 0, 2, 5 ; their squares: 16, 9, 0, 4, 25 ; Sum = 54

Step 3: Variance = 54/5 = 10.8 ; S = sqrt(10.8) = 3.286

So the standard deviation is 3.286.

Review Exercise 10 — Question 4

Q. For a set of ungrouped values, find the standard deviation and variance, when n = 15 and Sum(x - X-bar)^2 = 1444.

Formula: Variance = Sum(x - X-bar)^2 / n ; S = sqrt(Variance)

Step 1: Variance = 1444/15 = about 96.27 (the book's answer key gives 96.255 — a small calculation difference)

Step 2: S = sqrt(96.27) = about 9.811

So the standard deviation is about 9.811 and the variance is about 96.27.

Review Exercise 10 — Question 5

Q. For the data 3, 5, 6, 8, 8, 9, 10, find: (i) mean (ii) median (iii) mode

(i) Mean = (3 + 5 + 6 + 8 + 8 + 9 + 10)/7 = 49/7 = 7

(ii) The data is already in order; n = 7, the middle (4th) value = 8, so the median = 8

(iii) 8 occurs twice, the rest once each; mode = 8

Review Exercise 10 — Question 6

Q. For the set of values 4, 6, 7, 4, 8, 9, 7, 10, find the mean, median and mode.

Step 1: Mean = (4 + 6 + 7 + 4 + 8 + 9 + 7 + 10)/8 = 55/8 = 6.875

Step 2: In order: 4, 4, 6, 7, 7, 8, 9, 10 ; n = 8, median = (4th + 5th)/2 = (7 + 7)/2 = 7

Step 3: Both 4 and 7 occur twice each; modes = 4 and 7 (two modes) (Note: In the book's answer key '4, 7' is printed against Question 7, which are this question's modes; the text of Question 7 is not present on the printed Review page.)

mcqs.q: When a bar graph is constructed so that the area of each bar is proportional to the number of items in each group, it is called:
mcqs.why: In a histogram the rectangles touch each other and the area of each rectangle is proportional to the frequency of its group. That is why this construction is called a histogram.

mcqs.q: The summary statistics which measure the middle or center of the data are:
mcqs.why: The mean, the median and the mode each locate the middle or center of a data set. Together they are the measures of central tendency described in the Review items.

mcqs.q: If all numbers in a set are added together and then the total is divided by the number of scores in the set, it is called:
mcqs.why: Mean = Sum(x) / n. Adding all the scores and dividing by how many scores there are is exactly the definition of the mean.

mcqs.q: The middle value of data arranged in numerical order is called:
mcqs.why: First arrange the data in numerical order, then pick the middle value. That middle value is the median of the data.

mcqs.q: The score which occurs most often in a set of data is called:
mcqs.why: Count how often each score occurs. The score with the greatest frequency, the one occurring most often, is the mode.

mcqs.q: X-bar = (x_1 + x_2 + x_3 + ... + x_n) / n is called:
options: mean value of x_1, x_2, ..., x_n
mcqs.why: The formula mean = Sum(x) / n adds all n values and divides by n. The book names X-bar from this formula the mean value of x_1, x_2, ..., x_n.

mcqs.q: H = n / Sum(1/x) is called:
mcqs.why: The formula H = n / Sum(1/x) divides n by the sum of the reciprocals of the values. This mean is called the harmonic mean.

mcqs.q: X-bar_w = Sum(wx) / Sum(w) is called:
mcqs.why: In X-bar_w = Sum(wx) / Sum(w), each value x is multiplied by its weight w before adding. A mean found with weights in this way is the weighted mean.

mcqs.q: Sum(x_i - X-bar) = 0 is one of the properties of:
mcqs.why: For the arithmetic mean, the positive and negative deviations from X-bar cancel out. That is why Sum(x_i - X-bar) = 0 is a property of the arithmetic mean.

mcqs.q: For ungrouped data with n = 15 and Sum(x - X-bar)^2 = 1444, what is the variance?
mcqs.why: Variance = Sum((x - X-bar)^2) / n = 1444 / 15 = 96.266..., which is 96.27. Then S.D. = sqrt(variance) = sqrt(96.27) = about 9.811.
